title: Deploying to PocketHost just got simpler
text: This post is about PocketPages 0.x, the npm package. PocketPages v1 is built into PocketOne: see Moving from PocketPages 0.x. Going live with PocketPages is now four commands, and the tricky part about npm packages is handled for you.

title: Deploying to PocketHost just got simpler
heading: phio is now pockethost
text: The deploy CLI has a new name. If you used phio , swap it out: npm rm -g phio && npm i -g pockethost Your .phioconfig (or the pockethost key in package.json ) migrates to .pockethostconfig automatically.

title: Deploying to PocketHost just got simpler
heading: Four commands to production
text: pockethost login # paste a token from pockethost.io/account/tokens pockethost link # writes .pockethostconfig; commit it npm install pockethost deploy While you work, pockethost dev watches for changes and deploys them.

title: Deploying to PocketHost just got simpler
heading: Your packages ship with the deploy (4.2+)
text: PocketHost doesn't run npm install . Until now that made npm packages awkward, and the old advice to bundle them into pb_hooks never worked for PocketPages, since plugins load by name. Starting with CLI 4.2, pockethost deploy uploads your production node_modules : pocketpages , every pocketpages-plugin- , and anything else in dependencies , plus what they need. devDependencies stay home. It works with npm, pnpm and Bun, and only changed files upload. Two habits make it smooth: Put everything your pages, loaders and +config.js use in dependencies . Install before you deploy. A Cannot find module error in pockethost logs usually means you skipped one of these. Not sure what will ship? Run pockethost deploy --dry-run .

title: Deploying to PocketHost just got simpler
heading: Deploying from GitHub Actions
text: Save a token as the POCKETHOST_TOKEN secret and add two steps: run: npm ci run: npx pockethost@latest deploy env: POCKETHOST_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.POCKETHOST_TOKEN }} The old FTP-based deploy starters are gone. The CLI replaces both of them.

title: Deploying to PocketHost just got simpler
heading: See every starter running
text: Each starter kit now runs live on PocketHost, deployed straight from the repo, so you can click around before you pick one: minimal pocketpages-minimal.pockethost.io mvp pocketpages-mvp.pockethost.io auth pocketpages-auth.pockethost.io htmx pocketpages-htmx.pockethost.io datastar pocketpages-datastar.pockethost.io The full list is on Starter Kits, and the complete guide is in Deploying to Production.

title: MFA, sturdier OAuth2, and an auth starter that does it all
text: This post is about PocketPages 0.x, the npm package. PocketPages v1 is built into PocketOne: see Moving from PocketPages 0.x. Authentication got a lot of attention in this release. The auth plugin learned multi-factor sign-in, OAuth2 got a round of fixes, and the auth starter went from "mostly works" to a complete reference you can deploy.

title: MFA, sturdier OAuth2, and an auth starter that does it all
heading: MFA in the auth plugin (0.3.0)
text: When MFA is on for a user, PocketBase answers the first sign-in step with a 401 whose response.mfaId is set. signInWithPassword() and signInWithOTP() now accept that id to finish the second step: The two steps can come in either order: password then code, or code then password.

title: MFA, sturdier OAuth2, and an auth starter that does it all
heading: OAuth2 fixes
text: redirect_uri is now URL-encoded. The PKCE state cookie stays httpOnly and is cleared once sign-in completes. The plugin no longer quietly depends on micro-dash being loaded.

title: MFA, sturdier OAuth2, and an auth starter that does it all
heading: Cookies and redirects in core (0.22.4)
text: Two small fixes in pocketpages itself make auth flows behave: response.cookie() appends a Set-Cookie header instead of replacing it. Setting several cookies in one request, like signing in while clearing a temporary MFA cookie, now keeps all of them. redirect() only adds ?__flash= when you pass a message . Plain redirects keep clean URLs.

title: MFA, sturdier OAuth2, and an auth starter that does it all
heading: The auth starter, finished
text: The auth starter now demonstrates every PocketBase sign-in method end to end: password, anonymous, OTP and OAuth2 (Google) sign-in opt-in MFA, with a per-user toggle on the account page email verification, password reset and email change OAuth2 pages that show real errors instead of blank pages It's also safe to deploy now. Credentials no longer live in migrations: APP_URL , SMTP_ , MAIL_SENDER_ and GOOGLE_CLIENT_ come from environment variables, and POCKETBASE_URL sets where the plugin reaches PocketBase. npm create pocketpages # pick "auth" Read the auth plugin docs, or try the live demo. It's a public sandbox, so don't use a real password.

title: PocketOne alpha.10: PocketPages fixes
text: Alpha.10 fixes two PocketPages bugs that broke ordinary apps. ctx.pb() writes work. Every create , update or other call with a body threw TypeError: operand 'prototype' property is not an object . The PocketBase JS SDK checks value instanceof FormData on every request with a body, and in PocketOne's JS engine Go constructors like FormData , Record and Collection had no prototype , so instanceof threw. They now behave as they did under goja: each has a prototype , and new X() is an instance of X . Validation and rule failures from ctx.pb() come back as ClientResponseError , as the SDK documents. require() works on every request. A require() inside a handler, or any function that runs at request time, used the request that first loaded the module. From the second request on it failed with require("x"): not found . It now resolves and loads files on its own. Upgrade with brew upgrade pocketone or pocketone upgrade . Release notes

title: PocketOne alpha.8: a language model, WASM modules and desktop apps
text: This is the biggest PocketOne release so far. Three new things ship in the pocketone binary: a language model your hooks can call, WASM modules you can drop into pb_hooks , and a command that turns your app into a desktop app.

title: PocketOne alpha.8: a language model, WASM modules and desktop apps
heading: A language model in every app
text: Most apps have small jobs that want a model. Label a support ticket. Pull a JSON object out of an email. Write a title or an alt text. Until now that meant wiring up an API client in your hooks. Now it's $agent.complete() : const { data } = $agent.complete({ prompt: Classify this ticket: ${record.getString('body')} , schema: { type: 'object', properties: { label: { enum: ['bug', 'billing', 'question'] } } }, }) The answer can come from your own OpenAI-compatible API (OpenAI, OpenRouter, Groq, Ollama) or from a small model PocketOne runs itself, on your server's CPU, in the same binary. No Python, no GPU, nothing else to install. You pick which one in the dashboard under Settings → LLM , and your code doesn't change between them. Give it a JSON schema and the answer comes back parsed, and a built-in model can only write JSON that matches. $agent.stream() gives you the answer a piece at a time. Threads and prompt caching keep follow-up turns fast, and Agent Chat stores conversations with their history. It's off until you choose a model, so nothing downloads or runs unless you ask for it. Start with the Agent docs.

title: PocketOne alpha.8: a language model, WASM modules and desktop apps
heading: WASM modules
text: Some work is better in another language. A Markdown renderer, an image thumbnailer, a QR code generator: there's a good library for each in Go, Rust or Zig. Build it as a WASI module, put it in pb_hooks as .pb.wasm , and call it: const html = await $wasm.run.async('markdown', { text: record.getString('body') }) Each call runs in its own box, with its own memory and time limits, off the app's JS VM. A module can't reach your files, your database or the network. Input goes in, output comes out. The WASM docs have a page for each language (C, Go, TinyGo, Rust, Zig and others) with what each one costs per call, plus recipes built on real libraries. Thanks to @octavonu, who built it.

title: PocketOne alpha.8: a language model, WASM modules and desktop apps
heading: Desktop apps
text: The app folder you run with pocketone serve can now be a desktop app: pocketone desktop build --all That compiles your pb_hooks , pb_migrations and pb_public into one native executable each for macOS, Windows and Linux, from whichever machine you're on. The app runs its server on a private port and shows it in a native window. Builds run in Docker, in a build image pinned to your pocketone version. See Desktop.

title: PocketOne alpha.8: a language model, WASM modules and desktop apps
heading: Also in this release
text: PocketBase v0.42.3. Realtime and OAuth2 redirect fixes from upstream. Extensions can own their schema. An extension's migrations run at startup, kept apart from your app's pb_migrations . types.d.ts covers every contract , generated from its Go interface, and now sits in your project root. pb_cache/ next to pb_data holds files extensions can rebuild. Add it to your .gitignore .

title: PocketOne alpha.8: a language model, WASM modules and desktop apps
heading: Before you upgrade
text: Two things change under you: The Tokens extension is now API Tokens . Rename tokens: to api-tokens: in pocketone.yaml and use $apiTokens in your hooks (was $tokens ). Its collections are renamed on the first start. Go import paths moved to pocketone.dev . If you build PocketOne into your own Go program, replace github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ with pocketone.dev/ in your imports. The repo itself now lives at github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone. Upgrade with brew upgrade pocketone or pocketone upgrade . Everything else is in the release notes.

title: PocketOne alpha.9: a fix for Pocker hosts
text: Alpha.8 shipped with a bug that only shows up on multisite hosts running Pocker. I found it the hard way, rolling it out to PocketHost's edges this morning. On upgrade, alpha.8 renames the API Tokens tables. On a Pocker instance that rename failed with near "RENAME": syntax error , and the instance wouldn't start. The cause was older than alpha.8. Pocker opens every instance's database through the sandbox's SQL guard, under its own driver name. The database layer picks its SQL dialect by driver name, didn't know that one, and fell back to generic SQL. So renaming any collection on a Pocker instance had been broken all along. The API Tokens rename was just the first one to run at startup. Alpha.9 teaches it the guard's driver is SQLite, with a test that reproduces the exact failure. If you run pocketone serve for a single app, nothing changes for you: it never used the guard. If you run a multisite host on alpha.8, upgrade with brew upgrade pocketone or pocketone upgrade . Release notes

title: PocketPages is now built into PocketOne
text: PocketPages used to be an npm package you installed next to PocketBase and booted from a hook file. As of today it's part of PocketOne, a community fork of PocketBase that PocketHost maintains. Put a pb_pages folder next to pb_data and it's served. brew install pockethost/tap/pocketone pocketone pages create myapp --starter daisyui-docs cd myapp pocketone serve --dir ./pb_data

title: PocketPages is now built into PocketOne
heading: What's new in v1
text: Nothing to install. No node_modules , no pocketpages.pb.js , no plugin packages. Routing, static files and templates run in Go; your page code runs in PocketBase's JS VM, as before. JSX and TSX pages. Write .tsx pages, layouts and components next to your .ejs ones. esbuild is built in, so there's still no build step. +page.ts and the rest of your page code can be TypeScript too. A cleaner ctx API. One ctx object for requests, responses, data, sessions and helpers. ctx.pb() gives you the PocketBase JS SDK in-process, as the visitor, so API rules apply. Auth built in. Password, OTP, OAuth2, anonymous sign-in and the email flows, with cookie sessions. Faster. On the same starter kit pages, v1 serves about 17 times the requests per second of the npm package on a simple page and 11 times on a docs page, and a single request takes 0.2 to 0.4 ms instead of 6 ms. This site runs on v1 now, on a PocketHost edge in Los Angeles.

title: PocketPages is now built into PocketOne
heading: Coming from 0.x
text: v1 keeps the ideas (a folder of files that become routes, EJS, layouts, partials, middleware) and changes the API. Moving from PocketPages 0.x lists every difference. The npm package is retiring: v1 is where new work happens. Apps on 0.x keep running where they run today.

title: This site has no build step anymore
text: PocketPages is all about no-build: write a file, reload, see it. Until this week, our own website didn't follow that rule. Every style change went through the Tailwind CLI and a daisyUI plugin, producing a 136 KB stylesheet we had to remember to rebuild. Now it's one hand-written file. At the switch it was 22 KB, about 5 KB gzipped, with no build.

title: This site has no build step anymore
heading: Modern CSS covers it
text: A few years ago, Tailwind was filling real gaps. Today the browser handles most of what we used it for: Custom properties hold the theme. The whole palette is a dozen --color- variables. When we moved this site from a dark theme to the light one you're reading now, we changed those values and nothing else. Native nesting keeps component styles together without a preprocessor. @layer orders reset, tokens, layout, components and utilities, so specificity fights go away. color-mix() replaces opacity utilities like text-base-content/70 . popover gives us the mobile menu, with light-dismiss and Esc to close, with no JavaScript. Here's what a card looks like now. One variable picks its color, and the tint, border and icon follow: .card { --tone: var(--color-base-content); border: 1px solid color-mix(in oklab, var(--tone) 20%, transparent); background: linear-gradient( to bottom right, color-mix(in oklab, var(--tone) 10%, transparent), color-mix(in oklab, var(--tone) 5%, transparent) ); &.accent { --tone: var(--color-accent); } }

title: This site has no build step anymore
heading: The markup got shorter too
text: Utility classes put the styling in the HTML. The landing page had list items like this one, repeated a dozen times: ... Now it's a plain inside a .checklist , and the dot is a ::before with a radial gradient.

title: This site has no build step anymore
heading: What we gave up
text: Being honest about the trade-offs: No design system for free. daisyUI's components were handy. We rebuilt the handful we used (cards, buttons, alerts, a fake browser window) ourselves. The whole stylesheet came to about 900 lines. No typography plugin. We wrote our own .prose styles for the docs. It took about 120 lines, and they're tuned for what we actually render. That's a fair price for a site you can edit with nothing but a text editor and a browser.

title: This site has no build step anymore
heading: Should you do this?
text: If your project already uses Tailwind and you're happy, keep it. The daisyui starter isn't going anywhere. But if you picked PocketPages to avoid build steps, the CSS doesn't need one either. View source on this page: it's all in site.css .

title: Your coding agent now knows PocketPages
text: This post is about PocketPages 0.x, the npm package. PocketPages v1 is built into PocketOne: see Moving from PocketPages 0.x. Coding agents are great at frameworks they've seen thousands of times. PocketPages isn't one of those yet, and it runs somewhere unusual: inside PocketBase's JavaScript VM (Goja), not Node. Left to their instincts, agents write code that looks right and doesn't run: async / await and fetch() in a runtime that's synchronous record.title instead of record.get('title') treating formData like a plain object inventing a build step So we wrote down how PocketPages actually works, and now it ships with every project.

title: Your coding agent now knows PocketPages
heading: What's new
text: npm create pocketpages now sets up every project for agents. Alongside your starter you get: .claude/skills/pocketpages/ # the skill: SKILL.md + references/ AGENTS.md # short project rules most agents read automatically CLAUDE.md # imports AGENTS.md for Claude Code Claude Code loads the skill from .claude/skills/ when a task needs it. Cursor, Codex and other agents that read AGENTS.md get pointed at the skill from there. Open the project and start asking for features.

title: Your coding agent now knows PocketPages
heading: What the skill teaches
text: The skill is a set of Markdown files written against the PocketPages source and maintained alongside it: The runtime: what Goja supports and what it doesn't, the positional $app query API, records as Go objects, binding user input safely Routing: file conventions, route groups, params, and which files are never routable The request lifecycle: middleware and next() , loaders, how data merges, layouts and slots, redirects Templates: EJS, how include() and resolve() search _private/ , asset() fingerprinting, meta() The full context API with exact signatures, every official plugin, and deploying to PocketHost Where the docs and the skill disagree, trust the skill. It's checked against the code.

title: Your coding agent now knows PocketPages
heading: Already have a project?
text: In Claude Code, install it as a plugin. It works across all your projects and updates with the plugin: /plugin marketplace add benallfree/pocketpages /plugin install pocketpages@pocketpages Or copy the skill into any project, for any agent that supports skills: npx tiged benallfree/pocketpages/packages/claude-plugin/skills/pocketpages .claude/skills/pocketpages For chat assistants without skills, hand them llms.txt.

title: Your coding agent now knows PocketPages
heading: Help us make it better
text: If your agent keeps getting something wrong, a one-line addition to the skill's gotchas usually fixes it for everyone. The skill lives in packages/claude-plugin , and PRs are welcome. Its README has the full setup guide.

title: Teach your coding agent
text: PocketOne is new, so coding agents haven't seen much of it. Two things close that gap. Both are built from these docs, so they change when the docs change.

title: Teach your coding agent
heading: Agent Skills
text: The pocketone plugin has three skills: pocketone: using PocketOne in an app: the pocketone binary and its commands, pocketone.yaml , deploying, and every extension. pocketpages: building PocketPages v1 sites in pb_pages/ : routing, ctx , templates, layouts, auth and deploying. pocketone-extensions: writing your own extension and contributing it as a pull request: contracts, extkit , tests, and the README and changelog CI checks. Each skill carries a copy of the docs in its reference/ folder, so it works offline. Claude Code /plugin marketplace add pocketonehq/pocketone /plugin install pocketone@pocketone /plugin marketplace update pocketone picks up new versions. Other agents that read Agent Skills (Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI and others) npx skills add pocketonehq/pocketone Or copy a skill folder into your project yourself. The skills live in agent/skills/ .

title: Teach your coding agent
heading: llms.txt
text: For agents and tools that read the web: pocketone.dev/llms.txt indexes every docs page with a one-line summary. pocketone.dev/llms-full.txt holds every docs page in one Markdown file. PocketPages' docs are part of this site, under /docs/extensions/pages, so both files include them.

title: PocketBase compatibility
text: PocketBase's own test suite, exactly as PocketBase wrote it, runs against PocketOne's core on every core change and every day.

title: PocketBase compatibility
heading: Known exceptions
text: Tests skipped because PocketOne changes what they check on purpose. Everything else must pass. TestHooksBindsCount plugins/jsvm Counts JS hook binds: 84 with our onFilesystemCreate , 83 upstream

title: PocketBase compatibility
heading: Run it yourself
text: On a scratch checkout (the script rewrites test files): git remote add upstream https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketbase.git git config remote.upstream.tagopt --no-tags git fetch upstream master .github/upstream-tests/run.sh Workflow upstream-tests.yml Script run.sh Exceptions known-deviations.txt Every core change Changes we made to PocketBase

title: pocketone.yaml reference
text: Every section the pocketone binary understands, from pocketone config --json . Each extension owns its own section. pocketone config check checks a file. How the file works (where it's found, .env secrets) is on the Config page.

title: pocketone.yaml reference
heading: agent:
text: The language model PocketOne runs itself for agent/v1 ($agent.complete); on a multisite host, the model every instance shares. enabled bool false turns the extension off on this app ($agent and agent/v1 are gone). model string The model to run: qwen3-0.6b, qwen3-1.7b or qwen3-4b (downloaded once), hf: / / .gguf, or a path to a .gguf file. Empty: none. threads int CPU threads for the model (default: half the cores). parallel int Answers written at once; the rest wait their turn (default 1). prompt_cache_mb int Memory in MB for keeping the start of recent prompts, so one that begins the same way (a preamble, a chat so far) isn't read again (default 256, about 1,100 tokens of a Qwen3 model; -1 turns it off). max_tokens int Longest answer, in tokens, when a call doesn't say (default 512). timeout string Longest a call may take, waiting included (default 2m). cache_dir string Where downloaded models are kept (default: the user cache folder's pocketone/models). thread_memory_mb int Memory in MB for conversations' model state between calls ($agent's thread option), least recently used first (default 512; -1 keeps them on disk only). thread_cache_gb number Disk in GB for conversations' model state, in pb_cache/agent/threads (default 2; -1 turns it off). per_instance.max_tokens int Longest answer per call, in tokens (0: max_tokens). per_instance.concurrency int Calls an instance may have waiting or running at once (default 2). per_instance.pinned_mb int Memory in MB an instance's warmed prompts may hold in the prompt cache (default 64). per_instance.thread_cache_gb number Disk in GB for an instance's conversation state, in its own pb_cache (default 2.5, a quarter of a 10 GB instance). Owned by Agent.

title: pocketone.yaml reference
heading: agent-chat:
text: Turns the agent-chat extension off on a single app ( enabled: false ). On a multisite host it doesn't reach the instances: use pocker's isolate_config, or an instance's extensions.agent-chat . enabled bool On unless false. Extensions that require it turn off too, and the startup lines say why. Owned by Standard Set.

title: pocketone.yaml reference
heading: api-tokens:
text: Turns the api-tokens extension off on a single app ( enabled: false ). On a multisite host it doesn't reach the instances: use pocker's isolate_config, or an instance's extensions.api-tokens . enabled bool On unless false. Extensions that require it turn off too, and the startup lines say why. Owned by Standard Set.

title: pocketone.yaml reference
heading: app:
text: The single app, for every command that opens it: data dir, dev mode, encryption, JS engine, hooks, migrations, and the .env names it may read (env_allow). Not used on a multisite host. dir string The data folder (pb_data). Default: pb_data next to the executable. The --dir flag wins. dev bool Dev mode: logs and SQL statements printed to the console. The --dev flag wins. encryption_env string Name of the environment variable holding a 32-character key that encrypts the app settings. The --encryptionEnv flag wins. query_timeout duration Default timeout for SELECT queries, such as 30s. The --queryTimeout flag wins. hooks_dir string The JS hooks folder. Default: pb_hooks next to pb_data. The --hooksDir flag wins. jsvm string The JS engine for pb_hooks and pb_migrations: quickjs (PocketOne's, the default) or goja (PocketBase's own, for pure PocketBase compatibility: pages, $mcp, $apiTokens and JS contracts are off). The --jsvm flag wins. hooks_pool int Only with jsvm: goja: how many JS runtimes are kept ready for hooks. Default 15. The --hooksPool flag wins. migrations_dir string The migrations folder. Default: pb_migrations next to pb_data. The --migrationsDir flag wins. env_allow list of string Names from the .env the app and its JS hooks may read. Default none. js_limits.memory int The app's JS memory: the JS heap plus the Go objects JS holds, such as 128MiB. Default 64MiB. js_limits.task_time duration JS time one task (a request, a hook, a cron job) may use, Go calls and waits not counted, such as 10s. Default 5s. js_limits.task_wall duration Wall time one task may take, Go calls included, such as 60s. Default 30s.

title: pocketone.yaml reference
heading: autotls:
text: Automatic HTTPS certificates (ACME): auto, email, CA, domains, DNS-01, certificate storage. The --autotls flags win. auto bool Get certificates through ACME (CertMagic). Flag: --autotls. email string ACME account email, for expiry notices from the CA. Flag: --autotlsEmail. ca string letsencrypt (default), letsencrypt-staging, zerossl, or an ACME directory URL. Flag: --autotlsCA. storage string Where certificates are kept. Default pb_data/.autotls. domains list of string Extra domains to get at start; wildcards ( .example.com) need dns. Flag: --autotlsDomains. dns.provider string DNS provider for DNS-01 challenges (needed for wildcards): cloudflare. Flag: --autotlsDNS. dns.api_token string The provider's API token. Write $VAR to read it from the .env beside the file. dns.api_token_env string Or: the environment variable holding the token. Default CF_API_TOKEN. Flag: --autotlsDNSTokenEnv. Owned by Auto TLS.

title: pocketone.yaml reference
heading: backups:
text: Turns the backups extension off on a single app ( enabled: false ). On a multisite host it doesn't reach the instances: use pocker's isolate_config, or an instance's extensions.backups . enabled bool On unless false. Extensions that require it turn off too, and the startup lines say why. Owned by Standard Set.

title: pocketone.yaml reference
heading: bulkmail:
text: Turns the bulkmail extension off on a single app ( enabled: false ). On a multisite host it doesn't reach the instances: use pocker's isolate_config, or an instance's extensions.bulkmail . enabled bool On unless false. Extensions that require it turn off too, and the startup lines say why. Owned by Standard Set.

title: pocketone.yaml reference
heading: cache:
text: The cache (cache/v1): one store for every app in the process (memory, disk tier), and caps per bucket. enabled bool Turns the cache off when false; extensions then run uncached. eviction string Which values leave memory (or disk) first when the store reaches its ceiling: lru, mru, fifo or lifo. max_memory int Memory for every bucket together, such as 512MiB. Default 128MiB. disk bool Turns on a disk tier in pb_cache/cache, next to pb_data (on a multisite host, the host's own pb_cache). disk_path string Puts the disk tier in a cache folder there instead of pb_cache, and turns it on. Relative: to the app's folder (the one holding pb_data) when the app has the process to itself, the working directory when several apps share it (Pocker). max_disk int Size of the disk tier for every bucket together, such as 10GiB. Default 1GiB. defaults.eviction string Which of the bucket's entries go first when it's full: lru, mru, fifo or lifo. defaults.max_items int Most entries the bucket holds. defaults.max_memory int Most bytes of keys and values the bucket holds in memory, such as 32MiB (the default). defaults.max_disk int Most bytes of disk files the bucket's keys point at, each counted in full, such as 256MiB (the default). defaults.ttl int How long an entry lives unless the code says otherwise, such as 10m. buckets map of object Caps per bucket name, over what its code asks for. Owned by Cache.

title: pocketone.yaml reference
heading: deploy:
text: Turns the deploy extension off on a single app ( enabled: false ). On a multisite host it doesn't reach the instances: use pocker's isolate_config, or an instance's extensions.deploy . enabled bool On unless false. Extensions that require it turn off too, and the startup lines say why. Owned by Standard Set.

title: pocketone.yaml reference
heading: desktop:
text: How pocketone desktop build names and sizes the desktop app built from this folder. name string The app's name: the window title and the executable's name. Default: the folder's name. id string Reverse-DNS app id (dev.example.notes): names the app's data folder on each user's machine and its single-instance lock. Default: app.pocketone. . width int The window's starting width. Default: 1024. height int The window's starting height. Default: 768. sign.macos.identity string The signing identity in your keychain, as security find-identity -v -p codesigning shows it: Developer ID Application: Your Name (TEAMID). sign.macos.notary_profile string The notarytool keychain profile (xcrun notarytool store-credentials ). Set: each DMG is notarized and stapled. Empty: signed, not notarized. sign.windows.command string The command that signs one executable in place; {file} is its path. signtool on Windows, osslsigncode anywhere, or your signing service's tool. sign.linux.gpg_key string The GPG key to sign with (its email or id). Each build gets .sha256 and a detached .asc signature. Owned by Desktop.

title: pocketone.yaml reference
heading: docker:
text: Runtime provider docker: each instance in its own container with the PocketBase (pb:) or PocketOne (p1:) binary of its version (image, binary cache and manifest, instance root, default version, idle stop, limits). socket string The Docker socket. Default $DOCKER_HOST when it is unix://, else /var/run/docker.sock. image string Base image the binaries run in, such as alpine:3.20. Required; pulled when missing. binaries string Folder of the release binary cache and its releases.json. Required. versions list of string The minors this host serves, such as pb:0.36 or p1:0.0 (latest patch of each, from docker update). root string Folder with one folder per instance ( / ). Required. home string The instance folder inside the container. Default /home/pockethost. default_version string Version for instances that name none, such as p1:0.0. . Empty: such instances fail. min_upstream string Oldest upstream PocketBase release served. Default 0.23.0; lower it only for releases you cache yourself. idle_ttl duration Stop a container after this long without requests. Default 10m. max_concurrent_starts int Containers starting at once. title: agent.chat/v1
text: A chat is a conversation with the app's language model that the provider stores: the app keeps only its id. Each question goes to agent/v1 with the chat's recent messages and a summary of the older ones, and both turns are saved. Chats aren't tied to users: an app that has them puts the user's id in the chat's meta , lists by it, and decides who may read what. A wire contract at /api/_c/agent.chat/v1 (chat.go), one provider. It requires agent/v1. The agent-chat extension provides it.

title: agent.chat/v1
heading: Use
text: From pb_hooks (the agent extension binds these on $agent when a provider runs): const id = $agent.newChat({ title: "Support", meta: { user: e.auth.id } }) const chat = $agent.chat(id, { system: preamble, context: (q) = findExcerpts(q) }) const answer = chat.send(question) // or await chat.send.async(question), or send(q, { onText }) chat.history({ limit: 20 }) // [{ id, role, content, created }], oldest first $agent.chats.list({ meta: { user: e.auth.id } }) $agent.chats.forget({ meta: { user: deletedUserId } }) Over HTTP (a superuser, or a token with the chat scope): New /api/_c/agent.chat/v1/new {"title": "", "meta": {}} chat Send /api/_c/agent.chat/v1/send {"id": "...", "text": "...", "system": "", "window": 12, "summarizeEvery": 6, "context": ""} chat Send, streamed /api/_c/agent.chat/v1/send-stream as Send; server-sent events of agent/v1 chunks chat Get /api/_c/agent.chat/v1/get {"id": "..."} chat:read History /api/_c/agent.chat/v1/history {"id": "...", "limit": 0, "before": ""} chat:read Update /api/_c/agent.chat/v1/update {"id": "...", "title": "...", "meta": {}} chat List /api/_c/agent.chat/v1/list {"meta": {"user": "..."}, "limit": 50, "offset": 0} chat:read Forget /api/_c/agent.chat/v1/forget {"id": "..."} chat Forget by meta /api/_c/agent.chat/v1/forget-where {"meta": {"user": "..."}} chat send answers {"answer": , "summarized": bool} . A chat is {id, title, summary, meta, messages, created, updated} . meta filters match each top-level key exactly (strings, numbers, true/false, null). context is sent after the question; history shows the question alone, and later turns send it with its context again, so each prompt starts exactly like the last one did (the prompt cache and the chat's thread). Errors: not_found (404) for an unknown chat, and agent/v1's.

title: agent.chat/v1
heading: Provide
text: Implement chatv1.Chats and provide it in Register . Keep chats in the app's own database (each instance of a host has its own), call agent/v1 for answers with the chat's id as the thread , and forget the thread with the chat.

title: agent/v1
text: An app asks a language model for an answer: classify a record, pull JSON out of text, summarize, write a title. App code calls the same thing wherever the app runs; who answers is the provider's business: the app's own API: any OpenAI-compatible endpoint and key the app's admins set (OpenAI, OpenRouter, Groq, a local Ollama or llama-server); a model PocketOne runs itself, named in pocketone.yaml , downloaded once and cached; its host's model: a multisite host may provide this contract for its instances, running one model they all share unless an instance's admins set their own API. A wire contract at /api/_c/agent/v1 (agent.go), one provider. The agent extension provides it.

title: agent/v1
heading: Use
text: From pb_hooks : onRecordCreate((e) = { const r = $agent.complete({ system: "Label the support ticket.", prompt: e.record.get("body"), schema: { type: "object", properties: { label: { enum: ["bug", "billing", "question"] } }, required: ["label"] }, maxTokens: 30, }) e.record.set("label", r.data.label) e.next() }, "tickets") Over HTTP (a superuser, or a token with the agent scope): Complete POST /api/_c/agent/v1/complete with {"prompt": "...", "maxTokens": 100} agent Stream POST /api/_c/agent/v1/stream , same input; server-sent events agent Status GET /api/_c/agent/v1 agent:read Warm POST /api/_c/agent/v1/warm with {"system": "...", "wait": "30s"} agent Forget POST /api/_c/agent/v1/forget with {"id": "w_..."} agent Count POST /api/_c/agent/v1/count with {"text": "..."} or {"system": "...", "messages": [...]} agent:read Threads GET /api/_c/agent/v1/threads agent:read Forget a thread POST /api/_c/agent/v1/threads/forget with {"id": "..."} agent complete takes prompt or messages ( [{"role": "user", "content": "..."}] ), and optionally system , schema (a JSON schema the answer must match; its parsed value comes back as data ), maxTokens , temperature , stop and model (a hint a single-model provider ignores), thread (a conversation's name: the provider keeps the model's state after the call and continues from it when the next call starts the same way, so it reads only what's new; a cache, not storage) and wait (how long to wait for a loading model, as a duration; without it a loading model fails at once). It answers text , data , model , backend ( app , runner or host ), stopReason and usage ( inputTokens , outputTokens , and cachedTokens : how much of the prompt came from a cache of an earlier prompt that started the same way). Errors: not_configured (503), not_ready (503, still downloading or loading), busy (429, the app already has as many calls going as its host allows). stream sends the same answer as it's written: one event: stream per piece, {"text": "..."} , then {"done": true, "result": {...}} with what complete returns. An error before the answer starts is a JSON error response; one during it ends the stream with event: error . In the same process, $agent.stream(opts, onText) runs it with a callback (from Go, call the returned extkit.Stream 's Run ). status says which backend and model answer, and whether the model is ready (with download progress). warm reads the start of later prompts ahead of them (a preamble, say) and keeps it in the prompt cache until forget : calls that start the same way skip reading it. It returns at once with {"id", "warmed": false} and warms in the background, unless wait says how long to wait for it. The id is the same for the same text on the same app (not per model: the provider warms it again after a model change). A provider without a prompt cache (an app's own API, which caches prompts itself) answers warmed: false with a message, never an error. count gives a text's or a conversation's tokens ( exact: false when the provider can only estimate). threads lists the threads whose state is kept ( id , tokens , bytes , where : memory or disk, usedAt ). From Go: agentv1.Contract.Must(app).Complete(ctx, extkit.Internal, agentv1.CompleteInput{...}) .

title: agent/v1
heading: Provide
text: Implement agentv1.Agent and provide it in Register ( agentv1.Contract.Provide(app, a) ), or on a host for every instance ( agentv1.Contract.ProvideForInstances(hostScope, func(id string) agentv1.Agent {...}) ). A host's provider should honor the instance's own API settings, so its admins can leave the shared model without changing code, and keep each instance's warms, threads and prompt cache apart from every other instance's.

title: api-tokens.verify/v1
text: Another server checks one of an app's API tokens. A host in front of an app's accounts (a PocketHost edge in front of the mothership) is handed a token by a client and asks the app that issued it who the token acts as and what it may do. Companion to api-tokens/v1: whatever provides that provides this. A wire contract (verify.go).

title: api-tokens.verify/v1
heading: Use
text: Verify POST /api/_c/api-tokens.verify/v1 {"token", "ip"} superusers ( api_tokens_verify ) ip is the client's address, recorded as the token's last use; leave it out to leave the last use alone. A valid token: {"valid": true, "grant": {"tokenId": "...", "name": "ci", "ownerCollection": "users", "ownerId": "...", "scopes": ["instances=abc123"]}} scopes empty means the owner's full rights; a scope with a value ( instances=abc123 ) holds it for that value only (see api-tokens/v1). A token that isn't valid is an answer, not an error, so a caller can tell a refused token from an outage: {"valid": false, "reason": "invalid"} (unknown, malformed or revoked) or "expired" . In Go, from the other server: c := verifyv1.NewClient("https://app.example.com", superuserToken, nil) res, err := c.Verify(ctx, extkit.Auth{}, verifyv1.Input{Token: token, IP: ip}) if err != nil { / the app is unreachable: don't treat the token as refused / } if !res.Valid { / 401: res.Reason / } if !res.Grant.HasScopeFor("instances", id) { / 403 / } Cache answers briefly if you verify on every request: a revoked token then stops working once its entry expires.

title: api-tokens.verify/v1
heading: Provide
text: Implement verifyv1.Verifier over the same tokens as your api-tokens/v1 provider. Never return an error for a token that isn't valid: return Valid: false and a reason.

title: api-tokens.verify/v1
heading: verify
text: Checks an API token and says who it acts as and what it may do (its scopes, with their values). A token that isn't valid is an answer (Valid false), not an error, so callers can tell a refused token from an outage. REST POST /api/_c/api-tokens.verify/v1 CLI pocketone remote api-tokens verify --token --ip MCP api-tokens_verify_verify Token scope api_tokens_verify token --token string ip --ip string

title: api-tokens/v1
text: An app's API tokens, as other extensions use them. Tokens are scoped: a token limited to scopes works only on the requests those scopes reach. Extensions register their own scopes, read the token a request came with, and limit requests they make on someone's behalf, all through this package. A service with its own API (tokens.go), served at /api/_c/api-tokens/v1 .

title: api-tokens/v1
heading: Use
text: GET /api/_c/api-tokens/v1/scopes the scopes a token may hold, and who may own tokens GET /api/_c/api-tokens/v1 your tokens (superusers: ?owner= , ?ownerCollection= ) POST /api/_c/api-tokens/v1 create one ( {name, scopes, expires\ ttl} ); the secret is shown once DELETE /api/_c/api-tokens/v1/{id} revoke one POST /api/_c/api-tokens/v1/revoke-all revoke all of yours In Go: if tk, ok := tokensv1.Contract.Of(app); ok { tk.RegisterScope(tokensv1.Scope{Name: "notes:write", Description: "Change notes", Paths: []string{"/api/collections/notes/records"}, Methods: []string{"POST", "PATCH", "DELETE"}}) } g := tokensv1.FromRequest(e) // the request's token, or nil (a JWT, or none) ctx = tokensv1.WithScopes(ctx, []string{"notes:read"}) // requests made with ctx count as limited to these scopes A scope registered with Values can be held for some values only: name=value in the token's scopes ( instances=abc123 ), the bare name meaning every value. Paths don't see values, so the route checks them: g := tokensv1.FromRequest(e) if g != nil && !g.HasScopeFor("instances", id) { return e.ForbiddenError("Not this instance.", nil) } vals, all := g.ScopeValues("instances") // all: every value HoldsScope , CoversScope , ValuesOf and IntersectScopes do the same on a plain scope list.

title: cache/v1
text: A place for an app and its extensions to keep what was expensive to compute: rendered pages, API answers, resized images. Code opens a bucket by name with the limits it wants and gets and sets keys in it. Who keeps the bytes (memory and disk in this process, or Redis or Memcached shared between servers) is up to the provider, so a new one replaces the old without any caller changing. A bucket has its own caps, inside whatever room the provider has in all: Eviction Which of the bucket's entries go first when it's full: lru (default), mru , fifo , lifo MaxItems Most entries the bucket holds MaxMemory Most bytes of keys and values the bucket holds TTL How long an entry lives unless Set says otherwise Where entries live (memory, disk, another server) and how much room there is in all are the provider's and the operator's business, not the bucket's. The promise is a cache's: a provider may drop any entry at any time, and a Get may miss. It never returns a value that was deleted, cleared or replaced since, nor one past its TTL. Each app has its own buckets, on a multisite host too, even when the provider keeps every app's entries in one shared store. An app service contract, one provider (cache.go).

title: cache/v1
heading: Use
text: Open a bucket after registration (in a hook or at serve time), keep it, and use it: b, err := cachev1.Open(app, "myext.answers", cachev1.Options{MaxItems: 1000, TTL: 10 time.Minute}) if err != nil { return err } if v, ok, _ := b.Get(ctx, key); ok { return v } v := compute() _ = b.Set(ctx, key, v, 0) // 0 = the bucket's TTL Name buckets after your extension ( myext.answers ) so two extensions never share one. Declare cache/v1 in WorksWith : when nothing provides it, Open returns a bucket that keeps nothing, so the same code runs uncached. When the value is expensive and many requests may ask for the same cold key at once, let cachev1.Load compute it: callers asking for the same key of the same bucket while it runs share one call, and all of them are released only after the value is stored. An error goes to the callers waiting then and is never stored; each caller waits on its own context, and the call keeps running for the others when one gives up (so bound its time yourself). v, err := cachev1.Load(ctx, b, key, func(ctx context.Context) ([]byte, error) { return compute(ctx) }) Items has the same Load for Go values. To empty every bucket the app has (after a change that left stale entries), call cachev1.Clear(ctx, app) ; the app's admins can do the same from outside its code through cache.clear/v1.

title: cache/v1
heading: Go values
text: To cache a Go value (a parsed template, a compiled program) without turning it into bytes on every Set and back on every Get , make it a cachev1.Item and open the bucket with OpenItems : type compiled struct{ / ... / } func (c compiled) CacheSize() int64 { / roughly the bytes it holds in memory / } func (c compiled) MarshalCache() ([]byte, error) { / bytes decode turns back into an equal value / } func (c compiled) CacheVersion() string { return "compiled/2" } // change it when the bytes' format changes items, err := cachev1.OpenItems(app, "myext.compiled", cachev1.Options{MaxMemory: 64 content), and a decoder of another version never sees them: a miss, so a code change that alters the format doesn't decode stale bytes. On a provider that keeps only bytes, Items marshals on Set (with the version in front) and decodes on Get , so the code is the same either way.

title: cache/v1
heading: Provide
text: Implement cachev1.Cache ( Bucket , Clear ) and cachev1.Bucket ( Get , Set , Delete , Clear ), and provide it in Register , as the default if another provider should replace yours: cachev1.Contract.Provide(app, myCache) Cache.Clear empties every bucket the app has, including ones it hasn't opened since it started. Provide cache.clear/v1 beside it. To keep Go values without marshaling them, have your buckets also implement cachev1.ItemBucket ( GetItem , SetItem ). Items and bytes share a bucket's keys: Get of a Marshaler returns its bytes (and misses on an item that can't marshal), and GetItem of bytes of the decoder's version returns them decoded, as the key's item from then on. Never hand one key's item to another key. A bucket that only keeps bytes needs nothing more: Items marshals for it. Keep each app's buckets apart: on a shared store (one per process, or Redis), prefix keys with extkit.AppID(app) and the bucket name. Treat Options as caps you keep as well as your storage allows (Redis has its own eviction), and say in your README which ones you honour.

title: cli.commands/v1
text: The pocketone command tree. Every operation of every wire contract linked into the binary is a command under remote , with no code: pocketone remote restore to --at -2h calls restore/v1's RestoreTo on the project's remote. An extension replaces one of those commands by providing the same path, or adds commands of its own. One provider per path; when two extensions provide the same path, pocketone.yaml picks one. A keyed contract (by command path), in the developer's pocketone process (commands.go).

title: cli.commands/v1
heading: Use
text: The generated commands, for any contract: Path: remote , the contract id's words, then the operation: restore/v1's restore_to is remote restore to , mail.suppression/v1's check is remote mail suppression check , remote/v1's status is remote status ( clicmdv1.PathOf ). Flags: one per field of the operation's input ( --at , --email , --campaign ), plus --json for the whole input ( @file , - for stdin) and --remote (a remote's name or a URL; default: the project's default remote). Times take RFC 3339, a local time ( 2026-11-10 15:00 ) or a duration from now ( -2h ). Output: the answer as JSON; streams print one JSON line per entry until Ctrl-C. Auth: the remote's saved login ( pocketone login ), or P1_TOKEN in CI. Not commands: public operations that take or return a raw body (an unsubscribe page, a mail provider's webhook); they're for browsers and services. A remote that doesn't offer the contract answers "this remote doesn't offer restore/v1".

title: cli.commands/v1
heading: Provide
text: Provide a command in your extension's Register . The same path as a generated command replaces it; a new path adds one: clicmdv1.Contract.Provide(app, clicmdv1.Command{ Path: "remote rehash", Short: "Rehash every stored password", Flags: func(fs pflag.FlagSet) { fs.Bool("dry-run", false, "only count") }, Run: func(c clicmdv1.Ctx, args []string) error { caller, err := c.Caller("rehash/v1") // the command's remote, with its login if err != nil { return err } return caller.Call(c, "POST", "", nil, nil) }, }) and declare Implements: extkit.IDs("cli.commands/v1") . Two providers of one path fail the start until pocketone.yaml picks: providers: cli.commands/v1: remote rehash: rehasher A binary builds its tree with clicmdv1.Mount(app, rootCmd) once the app's contracts are sealed; the standard set does it in Register . Commands already on the tree ( remote add , remote whoami ) stay unless a provider replaces them.

title: Contracts
text: New to the idea? Read How PocketOne fits together first. This page is the list of every contract and how to write one. Every API a PocketOne extension offers is a contract: a versioned Go interface, and the HTTP API, hooks and MCP tools that come with it, at /api/_c/ / . Extensions have no routes of their own. An extension says what it implements , requires and works with in terms of these contracts, never another extension's name, so any extension that implements a contract can stand in for another. PocketOne answers "who provides this contract on this app?" at startup and prints the answer. Every contract lives here, standard or community; extensions live in ext/ . Each contract is a package named for its id and major version: deploy/v1 is pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/deploy/v1 , mail.fallback/v1 is .../mail/fallback/v1 . A change to what a contract promises is a new major version ( v2 ) next to the old one. The table is generated from each contract's README and every extension's Contracts() : run go run ./.github/extensions contracts (CI fails when it's stale). agent.chat/v1 Stored conversations with the app's language model: start a chat, send to it, read its history, find and forget chats by the app's own meta. agent-chat @benallfree agent/v1 Ask a language model for an answer: the app's own API, a model PocketOne runs, or its host's shared model. agent agent-chat @benallfree api-tokens.verify/v1 Another server checks an app's API token: who it acts as and what it may do. api-tokens @benallfree api-tokens/v1 An app's API tokens: check one, register scopes, read a request's token, limit in-process requests; the token API. api-tokens deploy, mcp, remotes @benallfree bulkmail/v1 Run bulk mail campaigns: count an audience; start, pause, resume, cancel, preview and test a campaign. bulkmail @benallfree cache.clear/v1 Emptying an app's cache buckets, one or all, from the dashboard, the CLI or an agent. cache (default) @benallfree cache/v1 Named buckets of bytes an app keeps for a while, with limits and eviction; memory, disk or a shared cache behind it. cache (default) mothership pages @benallfree cli.commands/v1 The pocketone command tree: every contract operation as a remote command by default; extensions replace or add commands. desktop @benallfree deploy/v1 A project's code files on an app: check, upload, commit, list, read, write, delete, tree. deploy (default) @benallfree gate/v1 What admits requests on a multisite host: peer checks, client IPs and rate limits, in order. firewall @benallfree http.wrap/v1 Middleware around everything a multisite host serves, nested in order. servertiming @benallfree instance.fs/v1 An instance's code files on disk: its folder, a cache folder, one writers' lock and a restart around a change. deploy (default), docker, pocker deploy @benallfree instance.lookup/v1 A multisite host asks what a hostname it doesn't know serves. mothership @benallfree instance.resolve/v1 On a control plane: what a hostname serves for an edge, and the records the answer was built from. mothership (default) mothership @benallfree instance.source/v1 The instance record a multisite host serves, and where the records come from. mothership pocker @benallfree instance.tokens/v1 A multisite host checks an API token one of its instances issued, to accept it on the routes it answers. pocker @benallfree instance.watch/v1 An edge follows a control plane lazily: one stream, hostnames watched as requests name them. mothership @benallfree mail.fallback/v1 Where an app's mail goes when SMTP is off: a chain of providers that send it or pass it on. mailrelay, mailtrap @benallfree mail.feedback/v1 Mail providers' reports (bounces, complaints, unsubscribes) received at one place and raised as events any extension can act on. bulkmail (default) @benallfree mail.suppression/v1 Addresses an app must not send bulk mail to, and the unsubscribe link every bulk message carries. bulkmail (default) @benallfree mcp/v1 The app's MCP endpoint at /mcp, with every provided contract's operations as tools. mcp (default) wasm @benallfree oauth/v1 The app's OAuth 2.1 authorization server, so the CLI and MCP clients can sign in. api-tokens mcp @benallfree remote/v1 Remote control of an app: whoami, status, restart, logs. The base every client starts from. docker, remotes (default) deploy @benallfree restore/v1 Put an app's data back as it was at a moment: from continuous history, or the latest backup before it. backups (default), pitr @benallfree runtime/v1 What runs a multisite host's instances (as isolates, in containers): one per host. docker, pocker @benallfree settings/v1 The settings an app's admins change for its extensions, one API for all of them. settings (default) agent, bulkmail, mailrelay, pitr, vacuum @benallfree templates/v1 An extension's own pages as Go templates a project can eject and edit. templates api-tokens @benallfree tls/v1 The TLS of a multisite host's listener: automatic certificates instead of certificate files. autotls @benallfree vacuum/v1 Compacting an app's databases so freed space goes back to the disk, and when it last happened. vacuum @benallfree internal/example/v1 is a test-only wire contract that exercises the generated code.

title: Contracts
heading: Three kinds
text: Service: a Go interface, looked up in the same process ( fallbackv1.Contract.Of(app) ). Wire: a service with an HTTP API under /api/_c/ / , generated from its interface: each method is an operation with its own HTTP method, path and token scope ( //op: POST restart scope=remote ); inputs and results are JSON, uploads ( extkit.RawIn ), downloads ( extkit.RawOut ) or streams ( extkit.Stream , sent as server-sent events: a GET or a POST, pushed as they happen with Run or polled with Poll ). It gets action hooks ( remotev1.OnRestart , onRemoteRestart in pb_hooks ), an MCP tool per JSON operation and a client. Every caller (HTTP, MCP, Go) passes the same scope check and hooks. Routed: a contract whose provider is an http.Handler serving everything under /api/_c/ / as it is, for an API a protocol shapes (OAuth) or an existing API moved under a contract (deploy/v1). A multisite host can provide a wire or routed contract for its instances, so it works for instances that run stock PocketBase. A contract can bring its own dashboard screen ( Contract.UI(name, fsys) ): it shows on every app that provides the contract, whichever extension does, and calls only the contract's API. restore/v1's "Restore to a moment" works this way. An extension that calls a contract for its own work (bulk mail checking whoever keeps the suppression list) passes extkit.Internal as the auth, and can ask who provides it with Contract.Provider(app) .

title: Contracts
heading: Add a contract
text: A contract is a folder ext/contracts/ /vN/ ( mail.fallback/v1 → mail/fallback/v1/ ) with: the Go package: the interface, its //contract: directives and zz_contract.go ; a README.md , its page on pocketone.dev, with front matter and four sections in this order: owners: ["@your-github-handle"] summary: "One line: what the contract promises." # mail.fallback/v1 ## Use how to call it: HTTP, Go, pb_hooks, MCP, CLI ## Provide how to implement it ## Extensions (generated: who provides, requires and works with it) ## License MIT Whoever first creates a contract owns it; an extension author who adds one owns both the contract and the extension that provides it. Ids are unique across PocketOne. Pick a name for what the contract does ( restore/v1 ), not for the extension that first provides it.

title: Contracts
heading: Write the interface
text: A contract is an interface with //contract: directives; contractgen writes the rest ( zz_contract.go ) with go generate ./... . A test fails when a generated file is stale. //go:generate go run pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/cmd/contractgen // Deployer sends a project's code to an app. // //contract:id deploy/v1 //contract:kind wire //contract:scope deploy //contract:host //contract:js hooks type Deployer interface { // Upload writes changed files to the app. Upload(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in UploadInput) (UploadResult, error) } Methods take ctx , then (wire) extkit.Auth , then at most one input; they return error or one value and error . A contract pb_hooks can touch ( //contract:js hooks or open ) also gets zz_contract.d.ts , its TypeScript for types.d.ts : each action hook typed with its operation's input ( onExampleUpload(handler: (e: contracts.CallEvent ) = void) ), and for open the interface e.provide checks ( contracts.Providers["mail.fallback/v1"] ). Hooks see the Go value, so fields carry Go names with the first letter lowered ( maxTokens ); a JS provider gets JSON, so fields carry their json names, omitempty ones optional. The doc comment of a wire method is its MCP tool's description. Contracts are reviewed like PocketOne's core: a contract is a promise every implementation keeps.

title: Contracts
heading: Use one
text: // provide (in Register) deployv1.Contract.ProvideDefault(app, myDeployer{}) // consume (after registration: in hooks, at serve time) d := deployv1.Contract.Must(app) // declare it, so PocketOne can order and switch extensions func (e Extension) Contracts() extkit.Contracts { return extkit.Contracts{Implements: extkit.IDs("deploy/v1"), Defaults: extkit.IDs("deploy/v1")} } Choose between providers in pocketone.yaml : providers: mail.fallback/v1: mailrelay

heading: License
text: MIT

title: instance.fs/v1
text: An instance's code files, for extensions that read and write them: deploy today, a live file drive next. It answers where the instance's folder is, where an extension may keep files it can rebuild (its cache), the one lock every writer takes, whether the instance runs, and how to restart it around a change that mustn't happen under a running app. The code is the pb_ folders except pb_data and pb_cache , package.json and the bun lockfiles at the top, patches/ , and the production node_modules tree at the top. pb_data and pb_cache are never reachable through this contract. A service contract (fs.go), one provider. It holds no request lookup and no auth: callers say which instance by id, and decide for themselves who may call them.

title: instance.fs/v1
heading: Use
text: files := fsv1.Contract.Must(app) // after registration: in a hook or at serve time f, err := files.Instance(ctx, fsv1.Self) // a single app's own files; a host passes the instance's id dir, _ := f.Dir(ctx) // the instance folder rel, path, err := fsv1.Resolve(dir, "pb_hooks/main.pb.js") // a client path, checked unlock, _ := f.Lock(ctx) // every write holds it defer unlock() startErr, err := f.Restart(ctx, func(ctx context.Context) error { / swap files in / return nil }) The package also holds the code-path rules every user shares: IsCodePath(p) : what a deploy may write or delete (never pb_data or pb_cache ). IsReachable(p) : what a file API may read or write (the code, node_modules , patches/ ; never pb_data , pb_cache or .git ). Resolve(dir, p) : a client path to a file inside dir , refusing unreachable paths, symlink crossings and anything that lands outside the folder ( PathError ). CacheDir(ctx, name) is the extension's folder for files it can rebuild, following PocketOne's pb_cache convention ( pb_cache/ in the app's folder on a single app; Pocker and Docker hosts keep it outside the instance folder, in the host's pb_cache/instances/ / ): anything in it may be deleted at any time, it is never code and never reachable, and it is on the same filesystem as Dir , so an extension can stage files there and rename them in atomically.

title: instance.fs/v1
heading: Provide
text: Implement fsv1.Files : Instance(ctx, id) returns an fsv1.FS for each instance ( fsv1.Self on a single app), or fsv1.ErrNoInstance . Return the same FS for the same instance every time: its Lock must be shared by every caller. fsv1.Local is an FS over a local folder to build on: give it the folder, and optionally a cache folder, whether it runs, how to stop it and how to start it again. Single app: deploy provides it as the default: the app's own folder. The app can't stop itself, so Restart applies the change while it runs (each rename is atomic) and then restarts the app. Host: the host's runtime provides it on the host scope ( fsv1.Contract.ProvideIn ), one per host since a host runs one runtime: pocker ( Manager.Files() : stops the instance's app, starts it again) and docker ( Runtime.Files(dir) : stops the container; the next request starts a fresh one). fsv1.Instances is the Files they build on: one Local per known instance, kept so its lock is shared. instance.fs/v1 isn't host-providable, so code inside an instance never reaches the host's provider.

title: instance.resolve/v1
text: How a control plane (a mothership) decides what a hostname serves for a given edge, from its own records. The watch server (instance.watch/v1) asks it on every watch and asks again after every write to a record an answer depends on, so a resolver only has to be right; it never tracks changes. A service contract on the mothership app (resolve.go).

title: instance.resolve/v1
heading: Use
text: resolvev1.Contract.Must(app) after registration: Resolve(ctx, Query{Edge, Host}) : the instance ( nil : no such host) and its Deps . Standing(ctx, edge) : instances the edge must hold whatever its traffic, with their deps. Edges(ctx) : every edge, with the list's deps. Touches(ctx, record) : the deps a write of the record touches besides its own record and collection. Deps are strings built with resolvev1.Record(collection, id) , Collection(name) (any record of it), Host(name) (whoever claims the name) and Key(name) (the resolver's own, such as which record is edge lax-1 ).

title: instance.resolve/v1
heading: Provide
text: Implement resolvev1.Resolver and provide it on the mothership app. ext/mothership's Schema provides the default over its edges and instances collections; a control plane with its own collections provides its own, and one that only adds to the default's answers wraps it ( Contract.Wrap ). Touches should report only what a write changed (compare rec.Original() ): a record written often, such as an edge's heartbeat, mustn't re-resolve every answer that merely looked it up.

text: mothership provides (default) mothership requires

title: instance.source/v1

title: instance.tokens/v1
text: A multisite host checks an API token one of its instances issued. pocketone login and pocketone clone sign in to the instance (its oauth/v1) and get the instance's own token. Where the host, not the instance, answers deploy/v1 and remote/v1, the host checks that token with this contract, so signing in works the same way on every host. A service contract (tokens.go), one provider, on the host's scope. It holds no auth of its own: the host decides what an instance token may do there (for example, only the instance's superusers may deploy).

title: instance.tokens/v1
heading: Use
text: tk, ok := tokensv1.Contract.In(host.Scope) // after the host's seal res, err := tk.Verify(ctx, tokensv1.Input{Instance: id, Token: token}) switch { case errors.Is(err, tokensv1.ErrNoInstance): // not one of this runtime's instances, or it has no API tokens case err != nil: // the instance failed to start: not a refusal case !res.Valid: // res.Reason: "invalid" or "expired" default: // res.Grant: the owner (collection, id) and scopes, as api-tokens/v1 says } The answer is api-tokens.verify/v1's Result . A token the instance didn't issue is Valid: false , never an error, so a host can tell a refused token from an instance that won't start. Verifying may start an instance that isn't running.

title: instance.tokens/v1
heading: Provide
text: A runtime that can reach inside its instances provides it on the host scope ( ProvideIn ): look up the instance's app and ask its api-tokens/v1 ( Verify ), mapping apitokensv1.ErrInvalid and ErrExpired to Valid: false . A runtime that can't (stock PocketBase images) doesn't provide it.

title: instance.watch/v1
text: An edge follows a mothership without holding every instance. It opens one stream; the first time a request names a hostname, it asks for it; from then on it hears every change to what that hostname serves, until it stops caring. Nothing is sent that no edge asked for, except the list of edges and the edge's standing set (instances it must hold whatever its traffic, such as a copy waiting to be made). A wire contract (watch.go) at /api/_c/instance.watch/v1/ . Superusers only (scope fleet ).

title: instance.watch/v1
heading: Use
text: stream GET /stream?edge= Server-sent events, each {kind, seq, ...} : hello first ( conn , self , edges , standing ), then host ( host , answer ), edges , standing , and ping when idle watch POST /watch {conn, edge, host} Registers host on the stream conn and sends its answer there. With no live conn , the answer comes in the reply and nothing is watched unwatch POST /unwatch {conn, host} Stops changes for host on conn The promise is in the order: The hostname is registered before it is read, so no write between the two is missed. The answer goes on the stream, never in the reply, so the answer and every later change arrive in the order they happened. A host event with no answer means the hostname couldn't be resolved (an error, not "not found"). "No such host" is an answer ( found: false ), watched like any other: the instance that later takes the name arrives. A change is sent only when the answer differs from the one sent last on that stream. seq numbers a stream's events from 1; a gap means something was lost and the edge reconnects. A dropped stream forgets every watch. An edge starts over on its next stream; what it cached before is unwatched. In Go, ext/mothership/client is the edge side: it is a multisite host's instance.source/v1 and instance.lookup/v1.

title: instance.watch/v1
heading: Provide
text: Implement watchv1.Watcher and provide it on the mothership app. ext/mothership's Server is the provider: it keeps each stream's watches in memory, indexes them by the deps instance.resolve/v1 returns, and resolves again after every committed write that touches them.

title: instance.watch/v1

title: mail.fallback/v1
text: Where an app's mail goes when its SMTP is off. Providers form an ordered chain: each sends a message or passes it on; when all pass, PocketBase sends it its own way ( sendmail ). An app with SMTP on never reaches the chain. A service (fallback.go), many providers, open to pb_hooks .

title: mail.fallback/v1
heading: Use

title: mail.fallback/v1
heading: Provide

title: mail.feedback/v1
text: What mail providers report back about mail an app sent: bounces, spam complaints, unsubscribes. The provider of this contract receives the reports and raises one event per address; any number of extensions act on them through one hook. A suppression list adds the address, a CRM marks the contact, pb_hooks logs it. A wire contract (feedback.go). Its operations are public: SES messages are checked by their SNS signature, webhook calls by a shared secret.

title: mcp/v1
text: The app's Model Context Protocol endpoint, so agents (a Claude connector, Claude Code, any Streamable HTTP client) can work with it. It stays at /mcp : people paste that URL, MCP versions itself in the protocol, and OAuth tokens are bound to the resource URL. What every provider serves the same way, the contract owns: The routes: /mcp , and its protected resource metadata at /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp . The tools: every wire contract the app provides, one tool per operation ( restore_points , bulkmail_start , ...), with an input schema from the operation's types and called through the contract, so the same superuser check, scopes and hooks apply as over HTTP; and tools extensions add with AddTool . A provider brings the protocol, sign-in and any tools of its own (MCP adds pb_ tools over the REST API). Replace it and the contract tools stay. A service (mcp.go).

title: mcp/v1
heading: Use
text: Add https:// /mcp to an MCP client and sign in. In Go, an extension adds a tool that isn't a contract operation, and tells agents what its tools are for: mcpv1.AddTool(app, mcpv1.Tool{ Name: "notes_summarize_week", Description: "Summarizes this week's notes.", ReadOnly: true, Call: func(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, args json.RawMessage) (any, error) { ... }, }) mcpv1.AddInstructions(app, "Use notes_summarize_week for weekly reviews.") mcpv1.Tools(app) lists what every provider serves.

title: mcp/v1
heading: Provide
text: Implement mcpv1.Endpoint ( ServeMCP for requests to /mcp , Metadata for the protected resource metadata), provide it, and bind the routes once: mcpv1.Contract.ProvideDefault(app, myServer{}) mcpv1.Bind(app) Serve mcpv1.Tools(app) in tools/list and tools/call , calling each tool as the signed-in caller. /mcp skips PocketBase's pbRejectUnknownToken , so the provider rejects a bad token itself: a request with an Authorization header and no signed-in caller ( e.Auth is nil) gets 401 with a WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token" challenge, never a guest's answer.

title: oauth/v1
text: An OAuth 2.1 authorization server for the app: authorization code with PKCE, device code, refresh, revocation, and client registration (dynamic, or by a client metadata document). The CLI's browser login and MCP clients such as Claude sign in through it, and get API tokens (api-tokens/v1). A routed contract (oauth.go): the OAuth specs fix its API's shape, so its provider serves it as it is.

title: oauth/v1
heading: Use
text: GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server the server's metadata (RFC 8414 puts it at the root) GET / POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/authorize sign in and consent (browser) POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/token codes and refresh tokens for access tokens POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/device start a device-code sign-in GET / POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/device/verify enter the device code (browser) POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/revoke revoke a token POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/register dynamic client registration (when on) GET / POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/provider/callback sign-in through an OAuth2 provider (Google, Apple, ...) authorize and device take an optional account : the auth collection the client needs the token from (the CLI sends _superusers ). The sign-in shows only that form, and no other collection is issued a token. In Go, another extension (MCP) turns on dynamic registration and sets token lifetimes: oauthv1.Contract.Of(app) → EnableDynamicRegistration() , SetAccessTTL(path, ttl) , Issuer(e) .

title: remote/v1
text: Remote control of an app from afar: who your credential is and what the app offers, its status, a restart, and its log. Every client starts here: GET /api/_c/remote/v1 is the one fixed path, and its answer lists every other contract the app offers. Contracts that add an area (deploy/v1) require this one. title: restore/v1
text: Put an app's data back as it was at a moment. You ask for a moment ("Tuesday 15:00"); the app restores the closest point it has at or before it and tells you which one it used. Providers differ only in how close they get: pitr keeps continuous history: any second inside its window. backups, the default, uses PocketBase's own backups (local or S3): the latest backup made at or before the moment. It steps aside when pitr is on for the app. The app restarts to apply a restore; its data from before the restore is kept until the next one. A wire contract (restore.go); a multisite host may provide it for its instances (from host-level snapshots).

title: restore/v1
heading: Use
text: Points: what can be restored GET /api/_c/restore/v1 restore:read RestoreTo a moment POST /api/_c/restore/v1/restore with {"at": " "} restore Points answers with the provider's name and either a window ( kind: "continuous" ) or a list of snapshots ( kind: "snapshots" , newest first), whether a restore is running, and the last restore. RestoreTo answers with the point it restores from; 422 no_point when there's nothing at or before the moment, 409 busy while another restore runs. Only superusers may call either. Dashboard: Settings → Backups gets a "Restore to a moment" section from this contract (ui/main.js), whichever extension provides it: a time picker over pitr's window, or one that says which backup a moment uses. Go: restorev1.Contract.Must(app).RestoreTo(ctx, auth, restorev1.RestoreInput{At: t}) , or restorev1.NewClient(url, token, http) from outside. Hooks: restorev1.OnRestoreTo(app, fn) in Go, onRestoreRestoreTo in pb_hooks : refuse or log a restore. MCP: restore_points and restore_restore_to .

title: restore/v1
heading: Provide

title: runtime/v1
text: What runs a multisite host's instances: pocker as isolates, docker in containers. A host runs exactly one, and every instance runs on it; an instance it can't serve (by PocketBase version, for example) is refused. Having a multisite section makes the binary a host; its runtime is this contract's provider. A host-scope service contract, one provider (runtime.go).

title: settings/v1
text: The settings an app's own superusers change for its extensions (PITR's S3 bucket, Bulk Mail's sending limits), behind one API: list them, read one, save one, test one without saving. Each extension keeps its settings its own way and registers a section; the provider serves them all. Settings an operator sets for a whole host stay in pocketone.yaml . A wire contract (settings.go).

title: settings/v1
heading: Use
text: List GET /api/_c/settings/v1 settings:read Get GET /api/_c/settings/v1/get?extension=pitr settings:read Save POST /api/_c/settings/v1/save with {"extension": "pitr", "values": {...}} settings Test POST /api/_c/settings/v1/test with {"extension": "pitr", "values": {...}} settings Each extension's values are its own shape (see its README). Secrets come back empty with a flag that they're set; saving an empty secret keeps the saved one. Test answers {"ok": false, "message": ...} when the settings don't work. Only superusers may call any of them.

title: settings/v1

A provider of the API (ext/settings by default) implements settingsv1.Settings over settingsv1.Sections(app) .

title: templates/v1
text: An extension that serves pages of its own (tokens' OAuth sign-in, consent and MFA screens) keeps them as a set of Go html/template files, usually embedded in the binary. A project themes them by ejecting the set and editing its copy: any file it has replaces the built-in one, and anything it leaves out falls back. The format is always Go templates, so the built-in pages and the ejected ones are the same files. A set is every .tpl file in an fs.FS , at any depth. Each file is one template named by its path without .tpl ( signin , parts/head ), so pages include shared pieces with {{template "parts/head" .}} . An app service contract, one provider (templates.go).

title: templates/v1
heading: Use
text: Add your set in Register , then render a page through the provider at request time, falling back to your own set when nothing provides the contract: //go:embed templates/oauth var oauthFiles embed.FS files, _ := fs.Sub(oauthFiles, "templates/oauth") templatesv1.Add(app, "oauth", files) // in a handler if t, ok := templatesv1.Contract.Of(app); ok { return t.Render(e, "oauth", "signin", http.StatusOK, data) } set, err := templatesv1.Parse(files, nil) if err != nil { return err } return templatesv1.Write(e, set, "signin", http.StatusOK, data) Declare the contract in WorksWith . Pass anything that must not be escaped (ready-made HTML) as template.HTML .

Read the sets with templatesv1.Set and templatesv1.Names , and build each page with templatesv1.Parse(set, projectCopy) and templatesv1.Write , so every provider renders the same way: templatesv1.Contract.Provide(app, myTemplates)

title: vacuum/v1
text: SQLite keeps a database file as big as it ever was; compacting it ( VACUUM ) gives the space freed by deleted records back to the disk. This contract says who does that for an app, how often, and how the last run went. A wire contract at /api/_c/vacuum/v1 (vacuum.go), one provider. On a single app the vacuum extension provides it, on the schedule the app's admins set. A multisite host may provide it for its instances instead: then the host compacts them on its own schedule, the app's vacuum extension steps aside (no settings, no schedule of its own), and the app's admins see the host's status.

heading: Use
