title: Agent Chat
text: Version 0.0.2 · Owners: @benallfree Agent Chat keeps conversations with your app's language model. Start a chat, keep its id, and send it questions: it stores every turn, sends the model the recent ones with each new question, folds older ones into a summary so long chats stay fast, and with the built-in model keeps each chat's state between turns, so a turn reads only what's new. const id: string = $agent.newChat({ meta: { user: ctx.auth.id } }) const answer: AgentAnswer = $agent.chat(id, { system: preamble }).send("How do I export my notes?") In Go: chats := chatv1.Contract.Must(app) // agent.chat/v1, from pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/agent/chat/v1 c, err := chats.New(ctx, extkit.Internal, chatv1.NewInput{Meta: json.RawMessage( {"user":" + e.Auth.Id + "} )}) res, err := chats.Send(ctx, extkit.Internal, chatv1.SendInput{ID: c.ID, System: preamble, Text: "How do I export my notes?"}) It needs the Agent extension (agent/v1), which answers. Chats aren't tied to users: your app keeps the id (on its own records, or in its frontend) and may put anything in a chat's meta to find it again. Install · Configure · Use · Integrations · Example

title: Agent Chat
heading: Install
text: Agent Chat is built into pocketone and on by default, in every app and every instance of a host (a standard member). In your own Go build, next to Agent: extkit.Setup(app, []extkit.Extension{agent.New(), agentchat.New()}, nil, nil) The module is pocketone.dev/ext/agent-chat . Its two collections come from its own migration, 0001_chats in schema.go, which runs on the first start ( pocketone extensions migrations lists it). They stay empty until your app starts a chat.

title: Agent Chat
heading: Configure
text: There's nothing to configure. Each send can say how much of the chat to send (below). Turn it off on a single app with agent-chat: {enabled: false} in pocketone.yaml (on a host, an instance's extensions.agent-chat ); its collections and their data stay. pocketone extensions migrate down agent-chat removes them, data included.

title: Agent Chat
heading: Use
text: $agent.newChat({ title?, meta? }) returns a new chat's id. $agent.chat(id, options) returns the chat: send(text, { onText?, onWait?, schema? }) Asks, saves both turns, returns agent/v1's answer ( text , usage , ...). With onText , streams the answer to it as it's written. send.async(text, { schema? }) The same in async page code, waiting for a model that's still loading. history({ limit?, before? }) The chat's messages, oldest first: { id, role, content, created } . summary() What the older messages were folded into. title(text?) , meta(object?) Read, or set and return. forget() Deletes the chat, its messages and the model's state for it. Options for $agent.chat(id, ...) , used by every send: system The preamble, first on every turn (Writing a preamble). context Text, or a function of the question returning text, sent after the question: the passages that answer it. history() shows the question alone; later turns send it with its context again, so the model's state for the chat still matches. window 12 Messages sent before the summary takes over. summarizeEvery 6 Once that many messages have piled up past the window, the oldest are folded into the summary (a second, short call). maxTokens , temperature , wait agent's As in $agent.complete . $agent.chats.list({ meta?, limit?, offset? }) lists chats, most recently updated first; meta keeps those whose meta has each of its top-level keys with that value. $agent.chats.forget({ meta }) deletes every match and returns how many. The chats are in _agent_chat_chats and _agent_chat_messages , superuser-only: your routes decide what users see. A typical route checks that the chat's meta.user is the caller before sending: // pb_pages/ask/[chat]/+api.ts: POST /ask/ {"question": "..."} export function post(ctx: any) { const chat = $agent.chat(ctx.params.chat, { system: preamble(ctx) }) if (!ctx.auth chat.meta().user !== ctx.auth.id) throw ctx.httpError(404, "no such chat") return ctx.res.json(chat.send(ctx.req.body().question)) } How a send is built: the system text, then the summary (when there is one), then every message since the last fold, then the question with its context. That start stays the same from one turn to the next until the next fold, which is what the built-in model's prompt cache and its per-chat thread need to skip re-reading the conversation.

title: Agent Chat
heading: Example
text: // Command example is a PocketBase app with stored chats: the agent extension answers, agent-chat keeps the // conversations. Name a model in pocketone.yaml ( agent: {model: qwen3-0.6b} ) or choose one in Settings → LLM, run // go run . serve , and ask over HTTP as a superuser: // // POST /api/_c/agent.chat/v1/new {"title": "Support"} - {"id": "..."} // POST /api/_c/agent.chat/v1/send {"id": "...", "text": "Hello"} - {"answer": {"text": "..."}} // // In page code the same is $agent.newChat() and $agent.chat(id).send(text). package main import ( "log" "ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase" "pocketone.dev/ext/agent" agentchat "pocketone.dev/ext/agent-chat" "pocketone.dev/ext/devusers" "pocketone.dev/ext/extkit" ) func main() { app := pocketbase.New() devusers.Register(app) if _, err := extkit.Setup(app, []extkit.Extension{agent.New(), agentchat.New()}, nil, nil); err != nil { log.Fatal(err) } if err := app.Start(); err != nil { log.Fatal(err) } }

title: Choosing a model
text: Settings → LLM in the dashboard decides what answers $agent : Off nothing: $agent throws not_configured apps that don't use it Built-in a model PocketOne downloads once and runs on your server's CPU short, focused jobs, with nothing to pay for and nothing leaving your server API your own OpenAI-compatible endpoint, key and model long answers, chat, the best models Until you choose there, pocketone.yaml decides: the model its agent section names runs built in, and without one the LLM is off. Reset to pocketone.yaml on the same page goes back to it.

title: Choosing a model
heading: Built-in models
text: qwen3-0.6b 640 MB about 1 GB tags, yes/no, short extraction; the fastest qwen3-1.7b 1.8 GB about 2 GB a good default: labels, extraction, short summaries and answers qwen3-4b 2.5 GB about 3 GB better answers, slower They come from Qwen's own repository and are checked against their SHA-256 when they download. Switching models downloads the new one and unloads the old one once its answers finish. Nothing downloads for a command such as pocketone superuser ; only serve starts the model. The built-in engine is pure Go with tuned assembly for Apple silicon and other ARM CPUs and for x86 (AVX2). It runs small models about as fast as Ollama does on the CPU, and faster on a one-core server: Apple M1 Max, 4 threads qwen3-1.7b (4-bit) about 140 tokens/s about 55 tokens/s Apple M1 Max, 4 threads qwen3-0.6b (4-bit) about 380 tokens/s about 120 tokens/s 1 vCPU x86 VPS (Skylake) qwen3-0.6b (4-bit) about 35 tokens/s about 9 tokens/s A word is roughly 1.3 tokens. So on a laptop a short answer takes a second or two; on a one-core server, a label takes about a second and a paragraph ten or more. Keep answers short with maxTokens , and do long jobs in a cron rather than in a request. agent.threads in pocketone.yaml sets how many CPU threads the model uses (default: half your cores), and agent.parallel how many answers it writes at once (default 1; the rest wait their turn). The model also keeps the start of recent prompts so a repeated preamble isn't read again ( agent.prompt_cache_mb , see Prompt caching).

title: Choosing a model
heading: Your own API
text: Choose API and fill in: Endpoint: the API's base URL with its version: https://api.openai.com/v1 , https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 , https://api.groq.com/openai/v1 , or http://localhost:11434/v1 for Ollama on your machine. Key: your API key. It's never shown again; leave the field empty to keep it. Change the endpoint and you need to enter the key again, so a key never goes to a server it wasn't meant for. Model: the provider's model name, such as gpt-4o-mini . Test sends a one-word prompt without saving, and shows the provider's error if there is one. A schema goes to the API as response_format , which most providers honor; streaming works with any provider that streams OpenAI-style.

title: Agent
text: Version 0.0.2 · Owners: @benallfree Agent gives your app a language model to call: $agent.complete() from your pages' code, or the agent/v1 contract from Go ( agentv1.Contract.Must(app).Complete(...) ). Use it for the small jobs that come up around data: label a support ticket, pull a JSON object out of an email, summarize a record, write a title or an alt text. The model can come from two places, and your code doesn't change between them: Your own API. Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint: OpenAI, OpenRouter, Groq, or a model you run yourself with Ollama or llama-server. A model PocketOne runs itself. Name one in pocketone.yaml and PocketOne downloads it once, checks it and runs it on your server's CPU, in the same binary (no Python, no GPU, no other program to install). These are small models: good at short, focused jobs, not at long conversations. Install · Configure · Use · Integrations · Example

title: Agent
heading: Install
text: Agent is built into pocketone . In your own Go build: extkit.Setup(app, []extkit.Extension{agent.New()}, nil, nil)

title: Agent
heading: Configure
text: In the dashboard, Settings → LLM (under System) picks what answers: Off: $agent answers with an error. Built-in: a model PocketOne runs, chosen from the list below. Choosing another one downloads it (the page shows the progress) and unloads the one before. API: your own OpenAI-compatible endpoint (the API's base URL with its version, like https://api.openai.com/v1 , or http://localhost:11434/v1 for Ollama), its key and the model. Test sends a one-word prompt. The key is never shown again; leave it empty to keep it (a new endpoint needs the key entered again). Until you choose there, pocketone.yaml decides: the model it names runs built in, and without one the LLM is off. Reset to pocketone.yaml on the same page goes back to it. To name the model there: agent: model: qwen3-1.7b # qwen3-0.6b, qwen3-1.7b, qwen3-4b, hf: / / .gguf, or a path to a .gguf file threads: 4 # default: half your CPU cores prompt_cache_mb: 256 # keeps the start of recent prompts so a repeated one isn't read again (-1: off) thread_memory_mb: 512 # conversations' state between calls, in memory (the thread option) thread_cache_gb: 2 # and on disk, in pb_cache/agent/threads (-1: off) qwen3-0.6b 640 MB about 1 GB tags, yes/no, short extraction qwen3-1.7b 1.8 GB about 2 GB a good default for a small server qwen3-4b 2.5 GB about 3 GB better answers, slower The first start downloads the model into your user cache folder ( cache_dir to change it) and checks its SHA-256; the app serves meanwhile, and $agent answers "still loading" until the model is ready. Nothing downloads for a command ( superuser , migrate ); only serve starts the model.

title: Agent
heading: agent:
text: The language model PocketOne runs itself for agent/v1 ($agent.complete); on a multisite host, the model every instance shares. enabled bool false turns the extension off on this app ($agent and agent/v1 are gone). model string The model to run: qwen3-0.6b, qwen3-1.7b or qwen3-4b (downloaded once), hf: / / .gguf, or a path to a .gguf file. Empty: none. threads int CPU threads for the model (default: half the cores). parallel int Answers written at once; the rest wait their turn (default 1). prompt_cache_mb int Memory in MB for keeping the start of recent prompts, so one that begins the same way (a preamble, a chat so far) isn't read again (default 256, about 1,100 tokens of a Qwen3 model; -1 turns it off). max_tokens int Longest answer, in tokens, when a call doesn't say (default 512). timeout string Longest a call may take, waiting included (default 2m). cache_dir string Where downloaded models are kept (default: the user cache folder's pocketone/models). thread_memory_mb int Memory in MB for conversations' model state between calls ($agent's thread option), least recently used first (default 512; -1 keeps them on disk only). thread_cache_gb number Disk in GB for conversations' model state, in pb_cache/agent/threads (default 2; -1 turns it off). per_instance.max_tokens int Longest answer per call, in tokens (0: max_tokens). per_instance.concurrency int Calls an instance may have waiting or running at once (default 2). per_instance.pinned_mb int Memory in MB an instance's warmed prompts may hold in the prompt cache (default 64). per_instance.thread_cache_gb number Disk in GB for an instance's conversation state, in its own pb_cache (default 2.5, a quarter of a 10 GB instance).

title: Agent
heading: Use
text: // pb_pages/tickets/+api.ts: POST /tickets {"body": "..."} export function post(ctx: any) { const { body } = ctx.req.body() const r: AgentAnswer = $agent.complete({ system: "Label the support ticket.", prompt: body, schema: { type: "object", properties: { label: { enum: ["bug", "billing", "question"] } }, required: ["label"] }, maxTokens: 30, }) const ticket = new Record(ctx.app.findCollectionByNameOrId("tickets")) ticket.set("body", body) ticket.set("label", r.data.label) ctx.app.save(ticket) return ctx.res.json(201, { id: ticket.id, label: r.data.label }) } In Go: // POST /tickets {"body": "..."}, in your app's Go code se.Router.POST("/tickets", func(e core.RequestEvent) error { var in struct{ Body string } if err := e.BindBody(&in); err != nil { return e.BadRequestError("send {body}", err) } r, err := agentv1.Contract.Must(e.App).Complete(e.Request.Context(), extkit.Internal, agentv1.CompleteInput{ System: "Label the support ticket.", Prompt: in.Body, Schema: json.RawMessage( {"type":"object","properties":{"label":{"enum":["bug","billing","question"]}},"required":["label"]} ), MaxTokens: 30, }) if err != nil { return err } var out struct{ Label string } if err := json.Unmarshal(r.Data, &out); err != nil { return err } col, err := e.App.FindCollectionByNameOrId("tickets") if err != nil { return err } ticket := core.NewRecord(col) ticket.Set("body", in.Body) ticket.Set("label", out.Label) if err := e.App.Save(ticket); err != nil { return err } return e.JSON(201, map[string]string{"id": ticket.Id, "label": out.Label}) }) In Go, every option below is a field of agentv1.CompleteInput ( Prompt , Messages , Schema , Thread , Wait , ...) and every $agent call is a method of agentv1.Agent ( Complete , Stream , Status , Warm , Count , Threads ); pass extkit.Internal to call with the app's own rights. The .async forms are JS only: Go passes Wait instead. prompt , or messages for a conversation; system , maxTokens , temperature , stop . schema : a JSON schema; the parsed answer comes back as data . With a model PocketOne runs, the answer can only be JSON matching it: the model is kept to it token by token (type, enum, const, properties, required, items, minItems, maxItems, anyOf), so even the smallest model fills in the schema instead of describing it. Your own API gets it as response_format , which most providers honor. The answer: text , data , model , backend ( app or runner , or host on a multisite host), usage . $agent.stream(opts, onText) answers the same way, calling onText(piece) as the answer is written (return false to stop); forward the pieces to the browser with ctx.res.sse() in a page. $agent.status() says which model answers and whether it's ready. thread: " " keeps a conversation's state between calls: the next call that sends the same conversation plus a new question reads only the new question (Threads). $agent.warm({ system }) reads a preamble ahead of the calls that start with it, and $agent.count(text) counts tokens, for budgeting what you send. For stored chats with history and summaries, add Agent Chat: $agent.chat(id).send(text) . $agent.complete waits for the answer, like $http.send . A model on your CPU writes maybe 5 to 30 words a second, so keep answers short ( maxTokens ) and do long jobs in a cron, not while a request waits. While the model downloads or loads, $agent.complete fails at once with not_ready . In async page code, await $agent.complete.async(opts) waits for it instead (up to opts.wait , default timeout ), and $agent.stream(opts, onText, { onWait }) with wait calls onWait(status) while it waits, to show progress (When the model is loading). It's agent/v1, also over HTTP ( POST /api/_c/agent/v1/complete , or /api/_c/agent/v1/stream for server-sent events, with a superuser or a token with the agent scope), on the command line ( pocketone remote agent complete --prompt "..." ) and as an MCP tool.
