title: Mothership
text: Version 0.0.1 · Owners: @benallfree A control plane for a fleet of edges. The mothership is a PocketOne app that records which edges exist and which instances run where. Each edge asks it about a hostname the first time a request names one, follows changes to that hostname on one stream, serves its own instances and forwards requests for the rest to the edge that runs them. One operator, no users: owners and accounts are the tenants extension (planned), which adds its collections and wraps instance.resolve/v1. Each layer is optional: an edge runs without a mothership, and a mothership without tenants. Install · Configure · Use · Integrations · Example

title: Mothership
heading: Install
text: Both sides are built into pocketone ; pocketone.yaml 's mothership section picks one. The mothership is a single app with serve: true . It keeps the edges and instances collections ( Schema ) and serves instance.watch/v1 to the edges ( Server ). An edge is a multisite host with url and self . It takes its instances from the mothership (instance.source/v1 and instance.lookup/v1) and the other edges from it. The module is pocketone.dev/ext/mothership . In your own build: extkit registers mothership.NewSchema() and mothership.NewServer() on the mothership app (a control plane with its own collections registers only the server, beside its own instance.resolve/v1); on an edge, client.FromSection(log) returns the client for the config (nil without a url ), a multisite host extension, as examples/pocketone/multi.go does. The client keeps its answers in the host's cache/v1, so the host provides one ( cache.Extension.Host(scope) ).

title: Mothership
heading: Configure
text: On the mothership: mothership: serve: true apex: example.com # .example.com routes to each instance On each edge, with logins from the private .env : multisite: {} mothership: url: http://10.88.0.10:8090 email: $MOTHERSHIP_EMAIL password: $MOTHERSHIP_PASSWORD self: lax-1 # this edge's edge_id (or edges.self) internal_url: http://10.88.0.5:8080 region: lax max_hosts: 50000 # hostnames the edge keeps answers for (cache bucket mothership.hosts) url and self are required on an edge. The edge logs in as a superuser of the mothership.

title: Mothership
heading: mothership:
text: A community mothership: serve: true makes this app one; url, login and self make a host follow one. serve bool This app is the mothership: it serves instance.watch/v1 to its edges (and keeps the edges and instances collections). apex string On the mothership: makes . a hostname of every instance. Empty: hosts only. url string On an edge: the mothership's URL. Required there. email string Superuser email this edge logs in with; use a $VAR from the .env. password string Superuser password; use a $VAR from the .env. self string This edge's edge_id, such as lax-1. Default: the edges section's self. Required on an edge. internal_url string Where other edges reach this one. Set: the edge registers itself when the mothership has no record for it. region string Region recorded when the edge registers itself. heartbeat duration How often this edge marks itself online. Default 15s; negative: never. max_hosts int Most hostnames an edge keeps answers for (its cache bucket mothership.hosts). Default 50000.

title: Mothership
heading: Use
text: You manage the fleet in the mothership's dashboard, in two collections only superusers can read or write: edges : edge_id (such as lax-1 ), internal_url , region , status ( online , draining , offline ) and last_seen . An edge with internal_url set registers itself when it has no record, and marks itself online every 15 s. instances : name ( . routes to it), hosts (extra hostnames), edge (where it runs), power (off answers 409 "instance is powered off"), suspension (non-empty answers 403 with that message), dev , version , secrets , encryption_key , access , limits , plugins (extension settings; the field keeps its old name) and status . A change reaches every edge that has served the hostname within moments, on its stream; there's no polling and no full copy. To move an instance, change its edge . An instance with no edge isn't served anywhere; a hostname no instance has answers 404, and the edge hears when one takes it.

title: Mothership
heading: Commands and APIs
text: Generated from the pocketone binary and the contracts this extension provides.

title: Mothership
heading: instance.watch/v1
text: stream pocketone remote instance watch stream --edge GET /api/_c/instance.watch/v1/stream instance_watch_stream watch pocketone remote instance watch --conn --edge --host POST /api/_c/instance.watch/v1/watch instance_watch_watch unwatch pocketone remote instance watch unwatch --conn --host POST /api/_c/instance.watch/v1/unwatch instance_watch_unwatch

title: Mothership
heading: Works with
text: Multisite The client is the host's instance source and lookup: which instance a hostname serves, asked on first use. Edge The client is also an edge source: where the other edges are, so requests for their instances are forwarded. It combines with a fixed edges list. Cache The client keeps answers in the host's bucket mothership.hosts (required). Docker and Pocker Run the instances this edge owns, with the version, secrets, limits and extension settings from each record. Tenants (planned) Adds owners and accounts by wrapping instance.resolve/v1.

title: Mothership
heading: Building on Mothership
text: Your own fields and collections. EnsureCollections leaves fields an extension added alone. Your own answers. Wrap instance.resolve/v1 ( resolvev1.Contract.Wrap ) to adjust what a hostname serves (block a suspended owner's instances, add an owner's trusted IPs), or provide your own over your own collections. List the records an answer read in its deps, and report from Touches the names and keys a write changes. The standing set. Standing(edge) lists instances an edge must hold without traffic (work addressed to it); they arrive in the stream's hello and whenever the set changes. Go API. client.New(client.Config{...}) builds an edge client without the config file; Standing() , EdgeRecords() and SelfRecord() read what the stream sent.

title: Mothership
heading: Example
text: There's no example/main.go yet. The stock binary is both sides: examples/pocketone/main.go registers the mothership, and its multi-instance mode, examples/pocketone/multi.go , follows one; examples/pocketone/mothership_test.go runs a mothership and two edges.

title: Mothership
heading: How it works
text: One stream per edge ( GET /api/_c/instance.watch/v1/stream?edge= ). Its hello carries the connection id, every edge and the edge's standing set. Lookup on a miss. A hostname the edge's cache doesn't hold is watched on the stream; the mothership registers the watch, then resolves, and sends the answer on the stream. Requests for one hostname share one ask. Changes. After every committed write, the mothership resolves again each watch whose deps the record touches, and sends only answers that changed. A cached hostname is updated; one the cache dropped is unwatched. Stream down. The edge keeps serving what it cached; a miss is answered in the reply, used once and not cached. Reconnect. A new stream is a new generation: the cache key carries it, so everything from before is ignored (and cleared). A mothership restart drops every stream, and every edge starts over. Edges log in as superusers today, so the edge names itself on the stream; a per-edge credential will carry it instead.

title: Mothership
heading: Status
text: Early. Built: the collections, the watch server, the default resolver and the edge client. Not yet: the mothership's own endpoints (placement, moves), instance status reports, per-edge credentials.

title: Mothership
heading: License
text: MIT

title: Multisite
text: Version 0.0.2 · Owners: @benallfree Walkthrough: PocketBase isolates. This page is the technical reference. Many PocketOne instances behind one listener, routed by hostname. Each request's hostname picks an instance, the request passes the gates (such as the firewall), and a runtime serves it: pocker runs instances as isolates in its own process, docker runs each in its own container. A host runs one of them, and every instance runs on it. Everything a host plugs in is a host-scope contract: runtime/v1, gate/v1, tls/v1, http.wrap/v1 and instance.source/v1. Install · Configure · Use · Integrations · Example

title: Multisite
heading: Install
text: Multisite is built into pocketone . It takes over serve when pocketone.yaml has a multisite section; without one, pocketone serve runs a single app as usual. multisite: {} # pocker, unless there's a docker section (then docker) In your own Go build, pass the host extensions you link (one runtime), build the host from the config and run it. examples/pocketone/multi.go is the stock binary's version: h, err := multisite.FromConfig(multisite.Options{Resolve: cfg.ResolvePath, Choices: providersSection, Extensions: []multisite.Extension{servertiming.New(), autotls.New(), &pocker.Provider{Resolve: cfg.ResolvePath}}}) if errors.Is(err, multisite.ErrNoProvider) { // no multisite section in pocketone.yaml: serve a single app instead } err = h.Run(ctx) At startup the host logs who provides each host contract, e.g. multisite: runtime/v1 ← pocker . Registering two runtimes is a conflict at startup unless providers: { runtime/v1: docker } picks one. The module is pocketone.dev/ext/multisite .

title: Multisite
heading: Configure
text: A host reads these pocketone.yaml sections: multisite: {} # host mode server: https: ":443" # the main address http: ":80" # redirects to https (alone: serves plain HTTP) plain: [":8080"] # extra plain-HTTP addresses, no redirect (e.g. a private network) tls: { cert: cert.pem, key: key.pem } # reloaded when the files change; or the autotls section instances: file: ./instances.yaml # where the instances come from dev: false # also serve unknown hostnames pocker: { root: ./pb_root } # a runtime's own section (pocker; docker only runs with its section) firewall: { allow_cidrs: [10.0.0.0/8] } # any gate's section turns that gate on server belongs to Config; providers is the contracts' section. With no https or http , the host listens on 127.0.0.1:8090 . The instances section is this extension's (keys below). In production the instances file is required; with dev: true it's optional. The app section is for a single app and is refused on a multisite host: each instance has its own folder under its runtime's root.

title: Multisite
heading: instances:
text: Where a multi-instance host's instances come from (a YAML file), and dev mode (serve unknown hostnames). file string instances.yaml The instances file (id, hosts and settings for each instance), reloaded when it changes. dev bool Also serve unknown hostnames: each becomes an instance named after it, in dev mode, with its folder made on first use.

title: Multisite
heading: multisite:
text: Serve many instances (a multisite host) instead of a single app. The runtimes are the providers of runtime/v1.

title: Multisite
heading: The instances file
text: instances: id: blog # also the folder name: /blog hosts: [blog.example.com, www.blog.example.com] id: shop hosts: [shop.example.com] secrets: { STRIPE_KEY: sk_live_... } # the app's environment, seen by its JS hooks encryption_key: 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef # encrypts the app's stored settings access: { cors_origins: [https://shop.example.com] } limits: { max_js_execution: 60s } # over the runtime's defaults extensions: { firewall: { trusted_ips: [203.0.113.0/24] } } # settings for extensions, by name id: old hosts: [old.example.com] blocked: { status: 402, message: "Payment required" } The file is checked for changes every 2 seconds; edits apply without restarting the host. Ids are lowercase letters, digits, dots and dashes. Other fields: version and runtime (which release or runtime runs it), dir (another folder), dev , superusers (pocker upserts them when the app starts), private (for host Go code, never seen by JS) and remote (another server runs it).

title: Multisite
heading: What a request gets
text: A hostname no instance maps gets 404, and no folder is created. In dev mode it becomes a new instance named after the hostname, in dev mode. A blocked instance answers every request with its status and message. An instance with remote set is forwarded there after the gates (a plain proxy to the URL, or Edge for a fleet). Contracts the host provides for its instances (docker's remote/v1) answer after the gates and the blocked check, so the firewall, rate limits and a powered-off answer apply to them too. GET /.well-known/health on any hostname reports the host's status, how many instances it knows and how many are running.

title: Multisite
heading: Switching runtime
text: Switching between pocker and docker is a config change (add or remove the docker section, or providers: { runtime/v1: docker } ): both keep instances in / . Stop the containers first when leaving docker (they keep running across a host restart on purpose). Data only moves forward: an instance started on a newer version than wrote its data is upgraded.

title: Multisite
heading: Works with
text: Pocker runtime/v1: every instance runs in this process. Docker runtime/v1: each instance runs in its own container (with a docker section). Firewall A gate: peer allow-list, client IPs and rate limits. On when the config has firewall or rate_limits . Edge Forwards requests for instances another edge runs (the edges section). Mothership Its mirror is instance.source/v1 instead of the instances file, and lists the other edges. Auto TLS Certificates for the main listener, issued for the hostnames instances map. Stats Measures disk use and last request for each instance. Server Timing Server-Timing headers for each step of a request.

title: Multisite
heading: Building on Host
text: Host extensions. A multisite.Extension ( Name , RegisterHost(h) ) provides host-scope contracts on h.Scope : a runtime ( runtimev1.Contract.ProvideIn(h.Scope, rt) ), a gate, TLS, a wrapper, an instance source. It provides nothing when it isn't configured (no section). Pass it in Options.Extensions , or multisite.Link it from an init so linking the package is enough (the firewall does). By hand: h.Use(exts...) , then h.Setup(choices) . Runtime. runtimev1.Runtime ( Name , Serves , ServeInstance , Ready ), with optional Prechecker , Syncer , Starter , Statser and Shutdowner . Each instance runs on the runtime it names, else the first that serves it. Instance source. sourcev1.Source ( Snapshot , Watch ) feeds instances from anywhere, such as a control plane. The instances file ( YAMLSource ) is the default and steps aside for any other provider. Gates. A gatev1.Gate checks the peer ( AllowPeer ) and admits each request ( Admit ); ClientIPResolver passes the real client IP on to the app. Gates set on h.Gates directly run after the contract's. Forwarding. multisite.Options.Forward serves requests for instances with remote set (Edge fills it). Instance routes. Host.InstanceRoutes wrap the runtime for instances this host runs: they run after the peer check, the blocked answer and the gates, and before the runtime (never for forwarded instances). multisite.InstanceOf(r) is the resolved instance and multisite.InstanceID fits extkit's host handlers, so a contract the host provides for its instances goes here: remotev1.Contract.ProvideForInstances(h.Scope, myRemote) h.InstanceRoutes = append(h.InstanceRoutes, func(next http.Handler) http.Handler { return remotev1.W.HostHandler(h.Scope, multisite.InstanceID, myAuth, next) }) Listeners and wrappers. tls/v1 (or Host.TLS ) sets the listener's TLS, http.wrap/v1 providers wrap the whole handler (outside Host.Wrappers ), and Host.Background runs jobs until shutdown. Per-instance settings. An extension reads its own extensions. with inst.ExtensionConfig(name) and multisite.DecodeExtensionConfig .

title: Multisite
heading: Example
text: A toy host: instances from a YAML file, served by a runtime that answers with the instance it resolved. Run it from this folder with go run ./example --instances instances.yaml , then curl -H 'Host: blog.localhost' localhost:8090/ . // A minimal host: instances from a YAML file, routed by hostname, served by a toy runtime that answers with the // instance it resolved. Real hosts plug in a provider instead (ext/pocker as isolates, ext/docker in containers). // // go run ./example --instances instances.yaml // curl -H 'Host: blog.localhost' localhost:8090/ package main import ( "context" "flag" "fmt" "net/http" "os" "os/signal" "syscall" "pocketone.dev/ext/multisite" ) type echoRuntime struct{} func (echoRuntime) Name() string { return "echo" } func (echoRuntime) Serves(inst multisite.Instance) bool { return true } func (echoRuntime) Ready() bool { return true } func (echoRuntime) ServeInstance(w http.ResponseWriter, r http.Request, inst multisite.Instance) { fmt.Fprintf(w, "instance %s (%s%s)\n", inst.ID, r.Host, r.URL.Path) } func main() { instances := flag.String("instances", "instances.yaml", "instances file: instances: [{id: blog, hosts: [blog.localhost]}]") listen := flag.String("listen", "127.0.0.1:8090", "listen address") flag.Parse() ctx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM) defer stop() h := &multisite.Host{Source: &multisite.YAMLSource{Path: instances}, Runtime: echoRuntime{}, Listeners: multisite.Listeners{Listen: listen}} if err := h.Run(ctx); err != nil { fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err) os.Exit(1) } }

title: Multisite
heading: How it works
text: Instance , InstanceSource , YAMLSource The instance record (instance.source/v1) and where instances come from. Directory Instances by hostname and id, kept current from the source. Handler Health path, peer check, hostname, blocked, then remote (the Forward hook) or local (the instance routes, then the runtime), with the gates. Runtime runtime/v1: what runs instances. One per host. Gate , ChainGates , HostGate Request gates (gate/v1). Extension , Link , Host.Use , Host.Setup Host extensions and the host's contract scope. Serve , TLSProvider Listeners: plain, TLS (a provider such as autotls, or cert files reloaded on change), redirect, graceful shutdown. Host , FromConfig All of the above assembled, by hand or from pocketone.yaml .

title: Multisite
heading: License
text: MIT

title: Coding agents
text: Coding agents tend to write PocketPages as if it were a Node framework, or as if it were the 0.x npm package. The pocketpages Agent Skill teaches them v1: pb_pages/ , ctx , routing, templates, layouts, auth and deploying. It's built from these docs and the v1 spec, so it changes when they change. Claude Code /plugin marketplace add pocketonehq/pocketone /plugin install pocketone@pocketone The plugin also has the pocketone skill, for the binary, pocketone.yaml and its extensions. Other agents that read Agent Skills (Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI and others) npx skills add pocketonehq/pocketone Or copy agent/skills/pocketpages into your project.

title: Coding agents
heading: llms.txt
text: pocketone.dev/llms.txt indexes every docs page, these PocketPages pages included, with a one-line summary. pocketone.dev/llms-full.txt holds every docs page in one Markdown file.

title: API Routes and JSON
text: A +api.ts file serves its folder's URL without a template. Use it for JSON, feeds, webhooks and anything else that isn't an HTML page. // pb_pages/feeds/latest/+api.ts module.exports = { get(ctx) { const posts = ctx.app.findRecordsByFilter('posts', 'published = true', '-created', 20) return ctx.res.json(posts.map((p) = ({ id: p.id, title: p.getString('title') }))) }, } A request to /feeds/latest returns: [{ "id": "abc123", "title": "Hello" }]

title: API Routes and JSON
heading: How it works
text: +api.ts has the same exports as +page.ts : load , get , post , put , patch , delete . There is no template, so a handler must send a response. Returning without one is a 500 . [param] folders work as for pages: products/[id]/+api.ts serves /products/123 . A folder can't have both a +api.ts and an index page. Middleware runs for API routes too. ctx.httpError() thrown in a +api.ts answers with JSON: { "status": 404, "message": "..." } . Handlers can be async . The response is sent once the handler settles.

title: API Routes and JSON
heading: Async handlers
text: // pb_pages/stats/+api.ts module.exports = { async get(ctx) { const orders = await ctx.app.countRecords.async('orders') return ctx.res.json({ orders }) }, } An async handler still has to send a response. Returning a value without calling ctx.res.json (or another ctx.res method) is a 500 , as it is for a sync handler.

title: API Routes and JSON
heading: Sending responses
text: ctx.res.json(data) / ctx.res.json(status, data) JSON ctx.res.text(text) / ctx.res.text(status, text) Plain text ctx.res.html(html) / ctx.res.html(status, html) HTML as-is, without layouts ctx.res.file(path) A file from pb_pages ctx.res.redirect(location) A redirect ctx.res.sse() A text/event-stream See res.

title: API Routes and JSON
heading: JSON from a page
text: JSON is only sent through ctx.res.json (or a +api.ts ). Template output is never parsed as JSON, even if it looks like JSON. A page's +page.ts can still answer with JSON for one method: // pb_pages/products/[id]/+page.ts module.exports = { post(ctx) { const product = ctx.app.findRecordById('products', ctx.params.id) return ctx.res.json({ id: product.id, name: product.getString('name') }) }, }

title: API Routes and JSON
heading: Keep /api/ free
text: /api/ belongs to PocketBase. Pages never see it, and a pb_pages/api/ folder is an error at startup. Put your routes somewhere else, such as feeds/ , xapi/ or hooks/ .

title: Asset Management
text: Static files in pb_pages (images, CSS, JS, fonts) can be served with fingerprinted URLs that change when the file changes.

title: Asset Management
heading: Where to put assets
text: Anywhere in pb_pages , next to the pages that use them or in a shared folder: pb_pages/ assets/ app.css logo.png feature/ index.md header.jpg

title: Asset Management
heading: In templates
text: Use asset() (the same as ctx.asset() ): " " asset('/assets/app.css') returns something like /assets/app.3f9a1c2b7d4e.css . Relative paths resolve from the current file's folder; / -paths from pb_pages . A path that isn't a file in pb_pages is returned unchanged.

title: Asset Management
heading: In Markdown
text: Relative image paths go through asset() automatically: Header

title: Asset Management
heading: How it works
text: A fingerprinted name carries the first 12 hex characters of the file's SHA-256: name. .ext . Fingerprinted URLs are served with Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable . When the file changes, its hash and URL change, so browsers and CDNs fetch the new one. See asset and Caching.

title: Authentication
text: PocketPages keeps PocketBase auth in a cookie with the built-in auth plugin. Turn it on: // pb_pages/+config.ts module.exports = { plugins: ['auth'], }

title: Authentication
heading: How a request is authenticated
text: If the request has PocketBase's own Authorization header, ctx.auth is that record. Otherwise, the auth plugin reads the pb_auth cookie, validates the token and sets ctx.auth (or clears a bad cookie). With neither, ctx.auth is null . Every ctx.session sign-in method sets the cookie, sets ctx.auth for the rest of the request, and returns { token, record } . ctx.session.signOut() clears it.

title: Authentication
heading: Protecting pages
text: // pb_pages/account/+middleware.ts module.exports = (ctx, next) = { if (!ctx.auth) return ctx.res.redirect('/login') return next() } Welcome, Log out Log in

title: Authentication
heading: Passwords
text: // pb_pages/login/+page.ts module.exports = { post(ctx) { const { email, password } = ctx.req.body() try { ctx.session.signInWithPassword(email, password) } catch (e) { return { error: e.message, email } } return ctx.res.redirect('/') }, } Email " / Password Log in

title: Authentication
heading: Registration
text: // pb_pages/register/+page.ts module.exports = { post(ctx) { const { email, password, name } = ctx.req.body() try { ctx.session.register(email, password, { data: { name } }) } catch (e) { return { error: Error registering: ${e.message} } } return ctx.res.redirect('/', { flash: 'Welcome!' }) }, }

title: Authentication
heading: One-time passwords
text: A two-step form: request a code, then sign in with it. Turn on OTP for the collection in the dashboard and set up mail (Settings Mail settings). // pb_pages/login/otp/+page.ts module.exports = { post(ctx) { const { step, email, otpId, code } = ctx.req.body() try { if (step === 'request') { return { otpId: ctx.session.requestOTP(email), email } } ctx.session.signInWithOTP(otpId, code) return ctx.res.redirect('/', { flash: 'Signed in' }) } catch (e) { return { error: e.message, otpId, email } } }, } Send code Check your email for the code. " / Sign in

title: Authentication
heading: OAuth2
text: Configure the provider in the dashboard (Collections users Options OAuth2). Then start the flow from a form: Sign in with Google // pb_pages/auth/oauth/+page.ts module.exports = { post(ctx) { ctx.session.requestOAuth2(ctx.req.body().provider) }, } requestOAuth2 stores its state in a cookie and redirects to the provider. The provider sends the user back to /auth/oauth/confirm (change it with { redirectPath } ): // pb_pages/auth/oauth/confirm/+page.ts module.exports = { load(ctx) { try { ctx.session.signInWithOAuth2(ctx.req.query('state'), ctx.req.query('code')) } catch (e) { return { error: e.message } } return ctx.res.redirect('/') }, } See the Google OAuth2 speedrun for setting up Google.

title: Authentication
heading: Anonymous sign-in
text: // pb_pages/try/+page.ts module.exports = { post(ctx) { ctx.session.signInAnonymously() return ctx.res.redirect('/dashboard') }, }

title: Authentication
heading: Your own auth flow
text: If you authenticate a record yourself, set the session cookie with ctx.session.signIn(record) .

title: Authentication
heading: Signing out
text: // pb_pages/logout/+page.ts module.exports = { post(ctx) { ctx.session.signOut() return ctx.res.redirect('/') }, }

title: Authentication
heading: Security
text: Serve over HTTPS in production. Turn on PocketBase's rate limiting. Turn on email verification for your auth collection.

title: Understanding Caching in PocketPages
heading: Fingerprinted assets
text: asset() adds a content hash to a file's URL: " The hash is the first 12 hex characters of the file's SHA-256. Fingerprinted URLs are served with Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable , so browsers and CDNs keep them for a year. When the file changes, the hash changes, and so does the URL. Old copies are never served for the new URL. A path that isn't a file in pb_pages is returned unchanged (and not fingerprinted).

title: Understanding Caching in PocketPages
heading: Static files
text: Every static file gets an ETag from its content hash. A request with a matching If-None-Match gets 304 Not Modified .

title: Understanding Caching in PocketPages
heading: Templates
text: A template is compiled once per content hash and reused. Edit a file and the next request uses the new version, in every mode.

title: Understanding Caching in PocketPages
heading: Routes
text: The route table is built at startup and rebuilt whenever anything in pb_pages changes. A rebuild never restarts the app.

title: Understanding Caching in PocketPages
heading: Pages
text: Rendered pages aren't cached. To let browsers or a CDN cache a page, set a header in a handler or middleware: module.exports = (ctx, next) = { ctx.res.header('Cache-Control', 'public, max-age=60') return next() }

title: Configuration with +config.ts
text: Create pb_pages/+config.ts to configure PocketPages for the app. It's only allowed at the top of pb_pages ; a +config.ts in a subfolder is an error at startup. // pb_pages/+config.ts module.exports = { plugins: ['auth', 'realtime', 'datastar'], debug: false, }

title: Configuration with +config.ts
heading: Options
text: plugins [] Built-in plugins by name, or custom plugin factories. ETS templates and Markdown are always on. debug false Detailed error pages and ctx.log.debug output even outside dev mode. +config.ts must export an object; exporting a function (0.x's (api) = ({...}) form) is an error. +config.ts runs on each page request, so these aren't caught at startup: unknown keys, names that are neither a module nor a built-in, or a plugin listed twice make every page answer with an error (a 500; dev mode shows the reason on the page), and the reason goes to the log.

title: Configuration with +config.ts
heading: Plugins
text: Each entry in plugins is one of: A name , loaded with require : a _private/ file ( 'datastar' for the Datastar add-on), then a package in node_modules , then a built-in ( 'auth' or 'realtime' ). It must export a plugin factory. See Plugins. A custom plugin factory : a function that returns hooks, such as require('./_private/my-plugin.ts') . A require with a path loads exactly that file, skipping the name lookup, so it's how you choose one copy over another. An object with a factory and options : { factory, ...options } . The object is passed to the factory as its config . module.exports = { plugins: [ 'auth', 'realtime', { factory: require('./_private/banner.ts'), text: 'Hello' }, ], } Plugin hooks run in the order the plugins are listed. See Plugin Authoring.

title: Configuration with +config.ts
heading: Debug
text: debug: true turns on what dev mode ( --dev ) turns on: detailed error pages and ctx.log.debug output. See Debugging.

title: Creating a PocketPages Page
text: A page is a template file, .ets or .md , anywhere in pb_pages/ . Its path becomes its URL. (A .tsx component works too; see File types.)

title: Creating a PocketPages Page
heading: Creating pages
text: Create a file : inside pb_pages/ , create an .ets file. For example, an "About" page: pb_pages/about.ets - serves "/about" index files : index maps to its folder. pb_pages/index.ets - serves "/" pb_pages/products/index.ets - serves "/products" (and "/products/") Nested pages : folders become URL segments. pb_pages/ ├── index.ets - "/" ├── about.ets - "/about" ├── contact.ets - "/contact" └── products/ ├── index.ets - "/products" └── details.ets - "/products/details" Markdown pages : a .md file works the same way. Its tags run first (plain JavaScript), then Markdown. See Markdown. pb_pages/docs/routing.md - "/docs/routing" The extension is always dropped from the URL. To add data or handle forms, put a +page.ts next to the page; see Loading Data.

title: ctx.app
text: The app ( $app ): records, collections, settings. Page code calls it directly, with no HTTP round trip. module.exports = { load(ctx) { return { product: ctx.app.findRecordById('products', ctx.params.id), latest: ctx.app.findRecordsByFilter('posts', 'published = true', '-created', 10), } }, } Everything in PocketBase's JavaScript records and database docs that uses $app works on ctx.app . Calls through ctx.app don't apply collection API rules: page code is trusted server code. Check ctx.auth yourself before reading or changing data on a user's behalf.

title: ctx.asset
text: Returns the URL for a static file in pb_pages , with its content hash. In templates it's also available as asset . " Relative paths resolve from the current file's folder; / -paths from pb_pages . A path that isn't a file in pb_pages is returned unchanged. The hash is the first 12 hex characters of the file's SHA-256: name. .ext . Fingerprinted URLs are served with Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable . Relative image paths in Markdown pages go through ctx.asset automatically. See Asset Management.

title: ctx.auth
text: The authenticated record, or null . It's set by: PocketBase's own auth, when the request has an Authorization header; the auth plugin, from its pb_auth cookie. Welcome, Please verify your email. Log in ctx.auth is a PocketBase record, so the usual record methods work: get(field) , getString(field) , email() , verified() , isSuperuser() , collection() .

title: ctx.auth
heading: Protecting pages
text: // pb_pages/account/+middleware.ts module.exports = (ctx, next) = { if (!ctx.auth) return ctx.res.redirect('/login') return next() }

title: ctx.data, ctx.params, ctx.route
heading: ctx.data
text: A plain object shared by middleware, handlers and templates. It starts as {} . In templates it's also available as data . // +middleware.ts module.exports = (ctx, next) = { ctx.data.user = ctx.auth return next() } // +page.ts module.exports = { load(ctx) { return { products: ctx.app.findAllRecords('products') } // Object.assign'd into ctx.data }, } A handler's returned object is shallow-assigned into ctx.data . There is no deep merge.

title: ctx.data, ctx.params, ctx.route
heading: ctx.params
text: Route parameters from [name] segments, as strings. Never includes query parameters (use ctx.req.query() ). In templates it's also available as params . /

title: ctx.data, ctx.params, ctx.route
heading: ctx.route
text: { path, name, file } : the route pattern, the page name and its file relative to pb_pages . products/[id].ets /products/[id] [id] docs/index.md /docs index A +page.ts applies to every page in its folder; use ctx.route.name to tell them apart.

title: ctx.env
text: Returns an environment variable, or '' if it's unset. const key = ctx.env('STRIPE_SECRET_KEY') It reads the app's environment. Under a multitenant host's sandbox, it reads the instance's environment. See Managing Secrets.

title: ctx.flash
text: A flash is a one-time message that survives one redirect, such as "Saved" after a form post.

title: ctx.flash
heading: Setting a flash
text: return ctx.res.redirect('/account', { flash: 'Saved' }) The message is stored as JSON in a cookie ( pp_flash , HttpOnly , Max-Age=300 ). It can be any JSON value: return ctx.res.redirect('/cart', { flash: { type: 'success', text: 'Added to cart' } })

title: ctx.flash
heading: Reading it
text: On the next request, ctx.flash() returns the message and clears the cookie. It returns undefined when there is none. Calling it again in the same request returns the same value. " Read it in your layout to show flashes on every page.

title: The ctx Object
text: PocketPages creates one ctx object per request and passes it to middleware, handlers, templates and plugins. // +middleware.ts module.exports = (ctx, next) = next() // +page.ts / +api.ts module.exports = { load(ctx) {} } In templates, data , params , asset and meta are shortcuts for ctx.data , ctx.params , ctx.asset and ctx.meta .

title: The ctx Object
heading: Members
text: ctx.req The request: method, URL, query, headers, cookies, body, files ctx.res The response: status, headers, cookies, redirects, JSON, HTML, text, files, SSE ctx.data Plain object shared by middleware, handlers and templates ctx.params Route parameters ctx.route The matched route: { path, name, file } ctx.flash() The one-time message from the previous redirect ctx.auth The authenticated record, or null ctx.app The app ( $app ) ctx.pb() A JS SDK client acting as the visitor (API rules apply) ctx.env(name) Environment variable ctx.log debug , info , warn , error ctx.meta(key, value?) Per-request page metadata ctx.asset(path) Fingerprinted URL for a static file ctx.include(name, locals?) Render a _private/ partial from JS and get its text (same lookup as include , from the route's folder) ctx.resolve(name, { mode }?) Load a module from _private/ ctx.store(name, value?) The app's in-memory store ctx.pagesDir Absolute path of the app's pb_pages folder (read-only), e.g. for $os.readDir ctx.dev true in dev mode ctx.httpError(status, message) An error to throw for a specific status ctx.error { status, message } , in +error.ets

title: The ctx Object
heading: Added by plugins
text: ctx.session auth ctx.realtime realtime ctx.datastar datastar Custom plugins can add their own members with extendContext .

title: ctx.log
text: Writes to the app's log. ctx.log.debug('cart', ctx.data.cart) ctx.log.info('order placed') ctx.log.warn('stock is low') ctx.log.error('payment failed') debug only shows in dev mode ( --dev ) or with debug: true in +config.ts . See Debugging.

title: ctx.meta
text: A per-request key/value store for page metadata (title, description). Set with two arguments, read with one. In templates it's also available as meta . " Layouts render after the page, so they see what the page set.

title: ctx.meta
heading: Front matter
text: In a .md page, each top-level key of the YAML front matter is passed to ctx.meta(key, value) : title: About us description: Who we are

title: ctx.pb() (JS SDK)
text: ctx.pb() returns a PocketBase JS SDK client, the same API you use in the browser: // pb_pages/posts/+page.ts module.exports = { load(ctx) { const page = ctx.pb().collection('posts').getList(1, 20, { filter: 'published = true', sort: '-created', expand: 'author', }) return { posts: page.items } }, } It acts as the visitor. When someone is signed in ( ctx.auth , for example through the auth plugin), the client is authenticated as them; otherwise it's a guest. Your collections' API rules, expand and hidden fields apply exactly as they would in the browser. It's synchronous. Calls return their result directly; no await . No network. Requests go straight to your app's own API, in-process. There's no host or port to set, and it works the same on any server. Errors throw the SDK's ClientResponseError : try { const post = ctx.pb().collection('posts').getOne(ctx.params.id) } catch (e) { if (e.status === 404) throw ctx.httpError(404, 'No such post') throw e } Limits: only /api/ routes; file uploads through the SDK aren't supported, so use ctx.app for those.

title: ctx.pb() (JS SDK)
heading: ctx.pb() or ctx.app?
text: Permissions the visitor's: API rules apply full access, no rules API the JS SDK, same as the browser PocketBase's JSVM API ( findRecordsByFilter , save , ...) Use it for reading and writing on the visitor's behalf admin work, background jobs, anything rules shouldn't limit When in doubt, use ctx.pb() : if a page shows something, the visitor is allowed to see it.

title: ctx.req
text: method "GET" , "POST" , ... url { href, origin, pathname, search } query(name) First value of a query parameter as a string, or undefined query(name, { all: true }) Every value, as an array of strings query() { name: firstValue } for every parameter header(name) Request header, '' if absent cookie(name) Cookie value as a string, or undefined cookie(name, { json: true }) Cookie parsed as JSON ( undefined if absent or not JSON) cookies() { name: value } , strings body() Parsed body: a JSON object, or form fields as { name: value } (repeated names as arrays) files(name) Uploaded files for a multipart field, as PocketBase filesystem.File values ready for a record field ip Client IP as PocketBase resolves it (trusted proxy settings apply) event The underlying PocketBase RequestEvent , for anything not covered here Query values and cookies are strings unless you ask for JSON. Nothing is parsed for you.

title: ctx.req
heading: Examples
text: You asked for Page Browser:

title: ctx.req
heading: Forms
text: body() parses JSON, application/x-www-form-urlencoded and multipart/form-data : // pb_pages/contact/+page.ts module.exports = { post(ctx) { const { email, message } = ctx.req.body() // ... }, }

title: ctx.req
heading: File uploads
text: Upload module.exports = { post(ctx) { const record = ctx.app.findRecordById('users', ctx.auth.id) record.set('avatar', ctx.req.files('avatar')[0]) ctx.app.save(record) return ctx.res.redirect('/account') }, }

title: ctx.req
heading: Cookies
text: const theme = ctx.req.cookie('theme') // 'dark' or undefined const prefs = ctx.req.cookie('prefs', { json: true }) ?? {} Set cookies with ctx.res.cookie() .

title: ctx.res
text: status(code) Status for the rendered page. Returns ctx.res . header(name, value) Set a response header. header(name) reads it back. cookie(name, value, options?) Set a cookie. clearCookie(name, options?) Expire a cookie (same path / domain as when set). redirect(location, { status = 302, flash }?) or redirect(location, status) Send a redirect. status must be a 3xx code. flash sets a one-time message. json(data) / json(status, data) Send JSON. html(html) / html(status, html) Send HTML as-is (no layouts). text(text) / text(status, text) Send plain text. file(path) Send a file from pb_pages (path relative to pb_pages ). sse() Start a text/event-stream response. layout(false) Render this page without layouts (e.g. an HTML fragment for htmx). Returns ctx.res . sent true once a response has been sent. Once a response is sent, the later steps of the request (handlers, template, layouts) are skipped.

title: ctx.res
heading: Status and headers
text: Not here

title: ctx.res
heading: Redirects
text: return ctx.res.redirect('/login') return ctx.res.redirect('/account', { flash: 'Saved' }) return ctx.res.redirect('/new-home', 301) // or { status: 301 }

title: ctx.res
heading: Cookies
text: ctx.res.cookie('theme', 'dark', { maxAge: 60 60 24 365 }) ctx.res.cookie('prefs', { compact: true }) // objects are JSON.stringify'd ctx.res.clearCookie('theme') Non-string values are JSON.stringify 'd. The value is then percent-encoded ( encodeURIComponent ), and ctx.req.cookie decodes it. Defaults: path=/ , HttpOnly , SameSite=Lax , and Secure when the request is HTTPS. Options: path , domain , maxAge (seconds), expires (a Date , milliseconds since the epoch, or a date string; with maxAge too, browsers use maxAge ), httpOnly , secure , sameSite .

title: ctx.res
heading: JSON, HTML, text and files
text: return ctx.res.json({ ok: true }) return ctx.res.json(201, { id: record.id }) return ctx.res.html(' Fragment ') return ctx.res.text(404, 'Not found') return ctx.res.file('downloads/manual.pdf')

title: ctx.res
heading: Server-sent events
text: sse() starts a text/event-stream response and returns { send(event, data, { id, retry }?), comment(text), close() } : // pb_pages/clock/+api.ts module.exports = { get(ctx) { const stream = ctx.res.sse() stream.send('time', new Date().toISOString()) stream.close() }, } Streaming is only available through sse() . Templates return their text all at once.

title: ctx.resolve
text: Loads a module from a _private/ folder. The lookup starts at the route's folder (the page being served), wherever ctx.resolve is called from, so a layout or partial gets the same answer as the page: _private/ in the route's folder, then each parent folder up to pb_pages/ . A name starting with / looks only in pb_pages/_private/ . Without an extension, the name, then .js , .ts and .json are tried. // pb_pages/_private/shout.ts module.exports = (s) = String(s).toUpperCase()

title: ctx.resolve
heading: Modes
text: require (default) The module's exports raw The file's text script The text wrapped in style The text wrapped in

title: ctx.resolve
heading: Modules from node_modules
text: Page code can also require() by name: _private/ folders first (nearest to the file calling require ), then packages from pb_pages/node_modules , then the app's usual module paths. See JavaScript Runtime.

title: ctx.store
text: The app's in-memory store ( $app.store() ). Set with two arguments, read with one. ctx.store('visits', (ctx.store('visits') 0) + 1) Visits since start: Values are shared by every request to the app. The store lives in memory: it's empty again after the app restarts. Keep anything that must last in a collection.

title: Debugging in PocketPages
heading: Dev mode
text: Run pocketone with --dev : pocketone serve --dev Dev mode turns on: detailed error pages (message, file and line, trimmed stack; see Errors); ctx.log.debug output.

title: Debugging in PocketPages
heading: debug: true
text: To get the same in production, set debug: true in +config.ts : module.exports = { debug: true, } Turn it off again when you're done. Detailed error pages show error messages, file paths and stack traces to anyone who triggers an error.

title: Debugging in PocketPages
heading: Logging
text: ctx.log writes to the app's log: ctx.log.debug('loaded product', ctx.params.id) // only in dev mode or with debug: true ctx.log.info('order placed') ctx.log.warn('stock is low') ctx.log.error('payment failed') See log.

title: Debugging in PocketPages
heading: Template changes
text: Templates are cached by content hash and the route table is rebuilt on any file change, in every mode. If a change doesn't show, check the app's log for a startup error (bad file name, route conflict): the previous route table keeps serving until the error is fixed.

title: Going Live
text: A PocketPages app is a pb_pages folder. To go live, run PocketOne on your server (pages is built in) and put pb_pages next to pb_data , along with your other pb_ folders: pb_data/ pb_hooks/ pb_migrations/ pb_public/ pb_pages/ Or point pocketone at it with --pagesDir .

title: Going Live
heading: Updating
text: Copy the changed files into pb_pages . The route table is rebuilt on any change, and templates are cached by content hash, so updates show on the next request without restarting the app. If an update has a startup error (a bad name or a route conflict), it's logged with the file path and the previous route table keeps serving.

title: Going Live
heading: Before you go live
text: Run without --dev , and keep debug: false in +config.ts . Set secrets as environment variables (see Managing Secrets). Serve over HTTPS. Cookies set with ctx.res.cookie are marked Secure on HTTPS requests.

title: Going Live
heading: Multitenant hosts
text: Under a multitenant PocketOne host, every instance has its own pb_pages , and page code runs with the same limits as the rest of the instance's JS.

title: Directory Structure
text: All pages live in the pb_pages/ folder, next to pb_data/ : myapp/ pb_data/ pb_hooks/ pb_migrations/ pb_public/ pb_pages/ +config.ts +layout.ets index.ets about.ets _private/ nav.ets assets/ app.css products/ [id]/ +page.ts index.ets

title: Directory Structure
heading: Special names
text: A file or folder name starting with one of these characters is never a URL: + Framework file: +layout.ets (or +layout.tsx ), +middleware.ts , +page.ts , +api.ts , one of each per folder. +config.ts , +error.ets and +404.ets are allowed only at the top of pb_pages . Any other + name, any other extension (such as +layout.md ), and a top-only file in a subfolder are errors at startup. _ Private. _private/ folders hold partials and modules for include() and ctx.resolve() . Other _ names are ignored. - Ignored (drafts, notes). . Ignored (dotfiles), except a top-level .well-known/ , which is served as static files (ACME challenges, security.txt , app links). node_modules/ is never routed either.

title: Directory Structure
heading: Groups
text: A folder named (name) groups files without adding a URL segment: (marketing)/pricing.ets serves /pricing . A group can have its own +layout.ets , +middleware.ts and _private/ .

title: Directory Structure
heading: What else
text: Every other file is a static file, served as-is. Page code can require() modules by name from _private/ folders (nearest first), then pb_pages/node_modules , then pb_hooks/node_modules and the app folder's node_modules , then the app's usual module paths. Pages' own file access (routes, static files, includes, assets) never leaves pb_pages . A pb_pages/api/ folder is an error at startup, because /api/ belongs to PocketBase.

title: Errors
heading: Thrown errors
text: Anything thrown in middleware, a handler or a template becomes a 500 . Dev mode or debug: true : an HTML error page with the message, the file and line (template lines map to the .ets or .md source), and the stack trimmed to pb_pages -relative paths. Otherwise: a plain "Something went wrong" page. The full error always goes to the app's log.

title: Errors
heading: ctx.httpError(status, message)
text: Throw ctx.httpError() to answer with a specific status: // pb_pages/products/[id]/+page.ts module.exports = { load(ctx) { let product try { product = ctx.app.findFirstRecordByData('products', 'slug', ctx.params.id) } catch (e) { throw ctx.httpError(404, 'No such product') // findFirstRecordByData throws when nothing matches } ctx.data.product = product }, } In a page, it sends that status with a plain page showing message . In a +api.ts , it sends JSON: { "status": 404, "message": "No such product" } .

title: Errors
heading: A custom error page
text: Create pb_pages/+error.ets . It renders for every ctx.httpError and for every 500 outside dev mode, inside the root layout, with ctx.error = { status, message } : { % Error +error and +404 live only at the top of pb_pages . Either may be .ets or .tsx .

title: Errors
heading: A custom 404 page
text: Create pb_pages/+404.ets . It renders inside the root layout, with status 404 , for a GET or HEAD that nothing answers: no page, no file in pb_public and no PocketBase route. It never renders for /api/ or /_/ . The root +middleware.ts runs first, and page code can still change the status. { % Not found Not found Nothing lives at .

title: ETS templates
text: An .ets file is an HTML page with TypeScript in it. The tags are EJS's, and the code inside them is TypeScript: PocketOne strips the types when it compiles the template, with esbuild built into the binary. Types are stripped, not checked, so they document your code and help your editor without ever stopping a page. There is nothing to install or configure, and no build step. : $ Nothing checks the types inside an .ets file, your editor included: editors don't know .ets yet, so associate it with EJS for highlighting. For checked types, keep logic in a +page.ts or a _private/ module (see TypeScript). What you write is what the browser gets, with the tags filled in. ETS is the template style these docs use throughout. Components with TSX is the alternative; pick one style per app (see File types).

title: ETS templates
heading: Tags
text: Run code, no output Output, HTML-escaped Output, raw Nothing Also remove the newline right after the tag Also remove whitespace before / after the tag on its line ' % code Same as

title: ETS templates
heading: Escaping
text: replaces & " ' with & < > " ' . null and undefined output as an empty string. "x" ' % raw ' % Use <%- only for HTML you trust, such as the output of include() or slot() .

title: ETS templates
heading: In scope
text: Inside a template you can use: ctx The request context data ctx.data params ctx.params include Render a partial slot Define or read a slot asset ctx.asset meta ctx.meta require Load a module: a path, or a name looked up in _private/ then node_modules (see JavaScript Runtime)

title: ETS templates
heading: Output
text: A template returns its text. There is no echo() ; anything you want in the output goes through a tag.

title: ETS templates
heading: await
text: A template can await . Any tag that uses await turns the template into an async one, and PocketPages waits for it before it sends the page: orders Including a partial that uses await gives you a promise. Print it with . Printing a promise without await is an error, so you won't get [object Promise] in your page. A slot whose content awaits takes an async function: { % ... . A template without await runs as a plain function, so sync templates cost nothing extra.

title: ETS templates
heading: Errors
text: A TypeScript syntax error names the file and the template line, like any other template error: index.ets: line 3: TypeScript: Unexpected "=" . A type that's wrong but well formed isn't an error at all, since nothing checks it.

title: ETS templates
heading: Caching
text: A template is compiled once per content hash and reused, so an edited file is recompiled on the next request.

title: Pages
text: Version 0.1.2 · Owners: @benallfree Walkthrough for app owners: PocketPages sites. This page is the technical reference. Server-rendered pages from a pb_pages folder, next to your pb_data . Each file becomes a route: .ets templates (EJS tags holding TypeScript) or TSX components, Markdown pages, layouts, .ts middleware and API routes, plus static files. Every file type is listed in File types. Page code runs in your app's JS VM, so it can use your data directly. This is PocketPages v1, formerly the npm PocketPages package. Install · Configure · Use · Integrations · Example

title: Pages
heading: Install
text: Pages is built into pocketone and on whenever a pb_pages folder exists next to pb_data . There's no switch: no folder, no pages. If the folder appears while the app runs, it starts serving it. In your own Go build, register it after the JS VM (ext/jsvm), since page code runs there: app := pocketbase.New() jsvm.MustRegister(app, jsvm.Config{}) // page code runs in the app's JS VM pages.MustRegister(app, pages.Config{}) // serves pb_pages next to pb_data pages.RegisterCommand(app.RootCmd) // the pages create and pages starters commands app.Start() The module is pocketone.dev/ext/pages . See example/main.go and Create your own extension.

title: Pages
heading: Where the folder is
text: By default the folder is pb_pages next to pb_data . To use another one: pocketone serve --pagesDir /path/to/pb_pages A relative path resolves against the working directory, like --hooksDir . Its pocketone.yaml key is server.pages_dir .

title: Pages
heading: +config.ts
text: Settings for your pages live in the folder itself, in pb_pages/+config.ts : module.exports = { plugins: ['auth', 'realtime', 'datastar'], debug: false, } plugins [] Module names (a _private/ file, a node_modules package or a path, loaded with require ), built-in plugins by name ( auth , realtime , used when no module by that name is found), or custom plugins such as the add-ons. ETS and Markdown are always on. debug false Detailed error pages and ctx.log.debug output even outside dev mode. +config.ts runs on each page request. Unknown keys, names that are neither a module nor a built-in, or a plugin listed twice make every page answer with an error, and the reason goes to the log.

title: Pages
heading: Dev mode
text: When the app runs in dev mode ( --dev , or app.dev in pocketone.yaml ), or +config.ts sets debug: true , you get detailed error pages with the file and line, and ctx.log.debug output. Otherwise visitors see a plain "Something went wrong" page and the full error goes to the log.

title: Pages
heading: Start from a starter kit
text: pocketone pages starters # list the kits pocketone pages create myapp --starter daisyui-docs cd myapp pocketone serve --dir ./pb_data Then open http://127.0.0.1:8090. pages create makes a new folder (it must not exist yet) with pb_pages and anything the kit needs beside it, such as pb_migrations . Without --starter you get minimal . minimal One page, no layout, no build step (the default). mvp One page styled with MVP.css. htmx A realtime chat and counter with htmx and the realtime plugin. daisyui A navbar and drawer layout with Tailwind CSS and DaisyUI. daisyui-docs A docs site from Markdown pages. datastar A realtime chat with rooms, with Datastar. auth Sign-up, sign-in (password, OTP, OAuth2, anonymous), email flows and a protected account page.

title: Pages
heading: Write pages
text: Add or edit files in pb_pages and reload the browser; no restart is needed. A few examples of what the folder holds: pb_pages/ +config.ts settings (above) +layout.ets wraps every page +error.ets your error page index.ets / about.md /about blog/[slug].ets /blog/anything feeds/rss/+api.ts /feeds/rss, a route without a template _private/ partials, never served assets/app.css a static file The full contract is in SPEC.md: routes and precedence, middleware, +page.ts and +api.ts , ETS, partials, slots and layouts, Markdown, JSX and TSX, the ctx object, errors, the built-in auth and realtime plugins, custom plugins, add-ons and the changes from 0.x. Highlights: Static files get ETags and fingerprinted URLs through asset() . ctx.pb() is the bundled PocketBase JS SDK, called in-process as the visitor. ctx.res.sse() streams server-sent events. The auth plugin gives cookie sessions on PocketBase auth: password, OTP, anonymous, register, OAuth2 and the email flows (verification, password reset, email change). Accounts that need MFA (the collection's MFA is on and its rule matches) are refused by every pages sign-in method; pages has no second sign-in step yet.

title: Pages
heading: What you'll see in the log
text: Problems in the folder (a bad file name, two files claiming the same route) are logged as pages: ... errors. If the site served cleanly before, pages keeps the previous routes until the folder builds cleanly again. Errors thrown by page code are logged in full.

title: Pages
heading: Try the demo
text: example/ is a demo app with ETS, Markdown, TSX, auth, ctx.pb() , SSE and a JSON route. It has a live speed check at /speed . cd example && go run . serve --dir=./pb_data

title: Pages
heading: Commands and APIs
text: Generated from the pocketone binary and the contracts this extension provides.

title: Pages
heading: Commands
text: What it adds to the pocketone binary (CLI reference): pocketone pages create Create a folder with a starter kit (pb\_pages and anything it needs) pocketone pages starters List the starter kits

title: Pages
heading: Works with
text: Multisite Pages is in the standard set, so every instance that runs PocketOne serves its own pb_pages (below). Cache Compiled templates and modules go in the pages.compiled bucket (cache/v1, at most 32 MiB per app), keyed by content, so old versions are evicted instead of piling up. On a multisite host, instances serving the same files share one compiled copy. On a multisite host they also outlive an instance's restarts, since the cache belongs to the host. With the cache off, each JS VM compiles a file the first time it meets it. Deploy pb_pages deploys with your other pb_ folders. pull doesn't fetch it by default; name it: pocketone pull prod pb_pages .

title: Pages
heading: On a multisite host
text: Pages is a member of the standard set, so every instance serves its own /pb_pages , in the stock pocketone binary and in any host built on standard.New() . With an isolate runtime (Pocker), where instances are isolates in one process: Each start of an instance's app gets its own route table, compiled templates (in its own pages.compiled bucket; identical files share one copy in the host's cache) and caches. An instance that sleeps drops them; nothing is shared between instances. Page code runs in the instance's own sandboxed JS VM (jsvm), under its limits (execution time, memory, stack). include , require , ctx.resolve , ctx.res.file and asset never reach outside the instance's pb_pages ; $os file access stays inside the instance folder. Tests: multiinstance_test.go. An instance turns pages off in its settings with extensions: { pages: { enabled: false } } . Measured on the earlier goja engine (same machine as Speed, docs kit; not yet re-measured on jsvm): each awake instance added about 2.3 MB (50 instances: 41 MB idle to 155 MB), and one instance under pocker served about 4,000 requests/s (p50 5.6 ms, p99 80 ms at 50 concurrent). To try it: copy sites into multiinstance/example/pb_root/ .localhost/pb_pages , run go run ./multiinstance/example , and open http:// .localhost:8791 .

title: Pages
heading: Building on pages
text: Read the routes. pages.For(app) returns the service: Dir() is the folder, Table() the current route table, Errors() the problems from the last build. Custom plugins. A factory in +config.ts can add to ctx , run on each request and transform rendered HTML (SPEC.md, section 9.2). Add-ons are built this way.

title: Pages
heading: Example
text: example/main.go serves the demo in example/pb_pages : ETS, Markdown, TSX, auth, SSE and a JSON route. Run go run . serve --dir=./pb_data in example/ and open http://127.0.0.1:8090. // Command example runs one PocketOne app that serves the demo in ./pb_pages (ETS templates and TypeScript, Markdown, // a TSX page, auth, ctx.pb(), SSE, a JSON route, +404). ./pb_migrations creates a "notes" collection with three seed // notes. From this folder: // // go run . serve --dir=./pb_data // // Then open http://127.0.0.1:8090. Edit anything in pb_pages and reload; no restart needed. // // Logins (ext/devusers, local testing only): dashboard admin@example.com / password, app user user@example.com / // password. package main import ( "log" "ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase" "pocketone.dev/ext/devusers" "pocketone.dev/ext/jsvm" "pocketone.dev/ext/pages" ) func main() { app := pocketbase.New() devusers.Register(app) // local testing: superuser admin@example.com and user user@example.com, password "password" jsvm.MustRegister(app, jsvm.Config{}) // page code runs in the app's JS VM pages.MustRegister(app, pages.Config{}) if err := app.Start(); err != nil { log.Fatal(err) } }

title: Pages
heading: Speed
text: ext/pages against npm PocketPages 0.22.5 (the last 0.x release), serving the same starter kit pages: the 0.x kits in pb_hooks/pages on stock PocketBase 0.41.1, the v1 ports in pb_pages on the PocketOne binary. minimal / (EJS) npm 0.22.5 620 30 ms 670 ms 5.7 ms ext/pages 10,850 1.8 ms 37 ms 0.2 ms daisyui-docs /docs/overview (layouts, Markdown, partial) npm 0.22.5 580 28 ms 1.1 s 6.5 ms ext/pages 6,510 4.1 ms 49 ms 0.4 ms PocketBase's own /api/health (the ceiling) PocketOne 55,000 0.9 ms 2.4 ms 0.1 ms About 17.5× more requests per second on the simple page and 11× on the docs page, with p99 latency 20× lower. Single requests take 0.2 to 0.4 ms instead of 6 ms. Memory after each run was similar (170 to 350 MB for both). Why: 0.x parsed routes, ran EJS through a JS implementation and loaded its plugins inside the JS VM on every request. v1 builds the route table once, compiles each template once (EJS to JS in Go, Markdown with goldmark) and enters the JS VM once per request. How it was measured (2026-11-11): Apple M1 Max, 10 cores, macOS 27, Go 1.27.4, hey against 127.0.0.1 . Each server was warmed with 500 requests, then hey -z 10s -c 50 and hey -n 2000 -c 1 ; two rounds, which agreed within 5%. Every response was a 200 with the full page. The 0.x docs kit inlines about 6 KB of CSS into each page where v1 links app.css . Rerun it with bench/run.sh : cp -R starters/daisyui-docs /tmp/v1-docs pocketone superuser upsert admin@example.com password --dir=/tmp/v1-docs/pb_data bench/run.sh v1-docs 8804 /docs/overview "$(which pocketone)" /tmp/v1-docs

title: File types
text: PocketPages apps are server-rendered pages with no build step. Every file in pb_pages is either code, a template or a static file, and you write code and templates in TypeScript. PocketOne strips the types when it first uses a file, with esbuild built into the binary; it never checks them.

title: File types
heading: Code
text: +page.ts , +api.ts , +middleware.ts , +config.ts and the modules in _private/ are TypeScript files. They export functions and objects, and never produce HTML themselves. To check their types with your editor or tsc , see TypeScript.

title: File types
heading: Templates: pick one style
text: A template turns data into HTML. There are two styles, and an app uses one of them: A file is HTML with code in tags a function that returns markup Pages about.ets about.tsx Layouts, error pages +layout.ets , +error.ets , +404.ets +layout.tsx , +error.tsx , +404.tsx Partials _private/card.ets , include('card', { item }) _private/Card.tsx , Good for HTML-first apps, HTMX, Datastar, content sites apps built from components, typed props Read more ETS templates Components with TSX These docs use ETS. It's the closest to what the browser gets: open the file and you see the page. Both styles render on the server and send plain HTML. Neither has a client runtime, hydration or state; interactivity comes from links, forms, HTMX, Datastar or a . The styles can include each other, which helps when you move an app from one to the other, but an app that mixes them is harder to read. Markdown pages are the exception every app shares: a .md file runs EJS tags with plain JavaScript inside, as a small escape hatch in content.

title: File types
heading: JavaScript works too
text: Every TypeScript file type has a JavaScript twin that behaves the same, without types. Rename a file and nothing else changes: .ts .js .ets .ejs .tsx .jsx Apps written for PocketPages 0.x use .js and .ejs , and keep doing so. A folder can't have two framework files with the same name, such as +layout.ets beside +layout.ejs .

title: File types
heading: Everything else
text: .md A Markdown page or partial .json Data you can require any other file A static file, served as-is

title: HTMX Integration
text: HTMX lets HTML elements fetch HTML from the server and swap it into the page. PocketPages renders that HTML.

title: HTMX Integration
heading: Setting up HTMX
text: Add HTMX to your layout:

title: HTMX Integration
heading: Route organization
text: HTMX requests want HTML fragments, not whole pages wrapped in your layout. Put the layout in a group, and the fragment routes outside it: pb_pages/ (site)/ # Pages with layouts +layout.ets # Main site layout index.ets # / products/ index.ets # /products xapi/ # HTMX endpoints (no layouts) products/ search.ets # /xapi/products/search create/ +page.ts index.ets # /xapi/products/create (site) holds full pages. Its +layout.ets wraps them, and the group adds nothing to the URL. xapi/ holds fragments. No layout applies to them, because there is no +layout.ets at the root. Don't name the folder api/ : /api/ belongs to PocketBase. A handler can also send a fragment directly with ctx.res.html() , which never applies layouts.

title: HTMX Integration
heading: Sharing partials
text: Render the same fragment on the first page load and in HTMX responses by keeping it in a _private/ partial: pb_pages/ _private/ product-card.ets # shared partial (site)/ products/ index.ets # includes the partial xapi/ products/ more.ets # includes the same partial " Load More

title: HTMX Integration
heading: Forms
text: Create Product // pb_pages/xapi/products/create/+page.ts module.exports = { post(ctx) { const { name, description } = ctx.req.body() const product = new Record(ctx.app.findCollectionByNameOrId('products')) product.set('name', name) product.set('description', description) ctx.app.save(product) return { product } }, }

title: HTMX Integration
heading: Out-of-band updates
text: Update more than one element with a single response: Products

title: HTMX Integration
heading: Realtime updates
text: With the realtime plugin, a page can push rendered HTML to every subscriber. A template has include() , so render the partial there and send it: // pb_pages/+config.ts module.exports = { plugins: ['realtime'] } // pb_pages/xapi/chat/+page.ts module.exports = { post() {}, // accept POST; the page below does the work } Send In the browser, subscribe to the topic with the PocketBase JS SDK and append what arrives: const pb = new PocketBase(location.origin) pb.realtime.subscribe('chat', (html) = { document.getElementById('chat').insertAdjacentHTML('beforeend', html) })

title: HTMX Integration
heading: Best practices
text: Route organization : keep fragment routes outside the layout group, in a folder like xapi/ . Response size : return only the HTML the swap needs. Loading states : use hx-indicator to show progress. Security : check ctx.auth in middleware before changing data, validate input on the server, and debounce triggers like search inputs.

title: Installation
text: PocketPages v1 is built into PocketOne as the pages extension ( ext/pages ). There is nothing to install from npm: the standard pocketone binary includes it. pocketone pages create myapp creates a new app. Add --starter to start from a starter kit. _Note: --dir tells pocketone where pb_data is. PocketPages looks for pb_pages next to it. Create the superuser before the first serve ; otherwise PocketBase opens its superuser installer in your browser._ Browse to http://localhost:8090 and you'll see the starter's home page. The default minimal kit is one splash page: PocketPages }) % To start editing, open myapp/pb_pages/index.ets Changes appear on the next refresh. The app doesn't restart.

title: Installation
heading: Where pages live
text: Pages live in their own folder next to PocketBase's others: myapp/ pb_data/ pb_hooks/ pb_migrations/ pb_public/ pb_pages/ PocketPages finds the folder at pb_pages next to pb_data , or wherever --pagesDir points. If the folder doesn't exist, the extension does nothing for that app. Under a multitenant host, every instance has its own pb_pages .

title: Installation
heading: How does it work?
text: PocketPages is a multi-page app server for PocketOne. It listens for requests and renders pages using file-based routing rules, like old-school PHP. URLs under /api/ and /_/ always belong to PocketBase. A URL nothing in pb_pages matches goes on to pb_public , then to PocketBase.

title: JavaScript Runtime
text: Middleware, handlers, templates and plugins run in PocketBase's JavaScript runtime. It is neither a browser nor Node.js, so there are no Web APIs or Node APIs such as Buffer and require('fs') . Each request runs as one unit under the app's usual JS limits (execution time, memory). Under a multitenant host, that's the instance's sandbox.

title: JavaScript Runtime
heading: Talking to the app
text: Use ctx.app , which is $app . PocketBase's JS docs cover database operations and record operations: const records = ctx.app.findRecordsByFilter( 'articles', 'status = {:status} && author = {:author}', '-created', 20, 0, { status: 'pending', author: ctx.auth.id } )

title: JavaScript Runtime
heading: Can I use my favorite npm package?
text: Maybe. Page code can require() modules by name from _private/ folders (nearest first), then from pb_pages/node_modules , then pb_hooks/node_modules and the app folder's node_modules , then from the app's usual module paths. A _private/ file with the same name as a package wins. Packages that are plain CommonJS JavaScript, with no Node or browser APIs, have the best chance of working. Install packages in the app folder (next to pb_pages ), not inside pb_pages . Every file in pb_pages that isn't private is served, so a package.json there would be public: cd myapp npm install some-package const somePackage = require('some-package') Your own modules go in _private/ and load with ctx.resolve() .

title: Components with TSX
text: PocketPages has two template styles. ETS is HTML with code in it, and it's the one these docs use. TSX is code that returns HTML: every page, layout and partial is a function component. Pick TSX if you think in components and want typed props. Either way the page is rendered on the server and sent as plain HTML; nothing runs in the browser. A .tsx file can be a page, a layout ( +layout.tsx ), an error page ( +error.tsx , +404.tsx ) or a partial in _private/ . PocketOne compiles it the first time it's used, with esbuild built into the binary: no Node, no npm install , no build step. TypeScript types are stripped, not checked; to check them, see TypeScript. The tsx starter kit begins an app in this style. // pb_pages/products/[id].tsx import Price from './_private/Price' export default function Product({ data, slot }: pages.Props) { slot('title', data.product.getString('name')) return ( {data.product.getString('name')} ) } // pb_pages/products/_private/Price.tsx export default ({ cents }: { cents: number }) = ${(cents / 100).toFixed(2)}

title: Components with TSX
heading: Props
text: The file's default export is a component: a function from props to markup. It gets: ctx The request context. data , params , meta The same as ctx.data , ctx.params and ctx.meta . asset , include The same helpers EJS templates have. include(name, locals) returns HTML you can put in JSX. slot slot(name) reads a named slot, slot(name, content) sets one, slot() is the inner content. children In a layout, the inner content. A partial also gets the locals it was included with, as props. In TypeScript, these props are pages.Props (a partial's locals: pages.Props ). A component you import and use as gets only the props you pass it. See TypeScript.

title: Components with TSX
heading: Server-rendered HTML only
text: TSX looks like React, but it isn't: it renders straight to HTML on the server. There's no virtual DOM, no hydration, no state and no client-side React. Interactivity comes from the same places as in an ETS app: links, forms, HTMX, Datastar or a . Event handler props (functions) are dropped. Use plain attributes: onclick="..." , hx-get , data-on:click . Text and attribute values are escaped. dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: html }} inserts raw HTML. class and className both work, as do for and htmlFor . style takes a string or an object: { marginTop: 4 } renders margin-top:4 . true renders a bare attribute. false , null and undefined leave it out. gets in front of it, since JSX can't write a doctype.

title: Components with TSX
heading: Async components
text: Any component can be async , including the file's default export. The render waits for every async component in the tree, and sibling components run at the same time: // pb_pages/dashboard.tsx async function Count({ collection }: { collection: string }) { const n = await $app.countRecords.async(collection) return {n} } export default async function Dashboard({ ctx }: pages.Props) { const user = ctx.auth ? await ctx.app.findRecordById.async('users', ctx.auth.id) : null return ( Hi {user ? user.getString('name') : 'there'} orders, users ) } include() of a partial that awaits, and slot(name, content) with async content, work the same way.

title: Components with TSX
heading: Layouts
text: // pb_pages/+layout.tsx export default function Layout({ children, slot }: pages.Props) { return ( {slot('title')} {children} ) }

title: Components with TSX
heading: One style per app
text: Use TSX for every template in an app: pages, layouts, partials and error pages. Code files ( +page.ts , +api.ts , +middleware.ts , +config.ts ) are the same in both styles. The two styles can include each other, so you can move an app from one to the other a folder at a time: an ETS page can sit inside a TSX layout, and include() returns a partial's HTML in either style. Markdown pages are the one mix you can't avoid, since .md files always run EJS tags (see Markdown).

title: Components with TSX
heading: Imports
text: Components are ordinary modules, so import Card from './_private/Card' resolves the same way as require . A module whose only export is export default behaves like module.exports = ... . include('card') without an extension tries .ets , .ejs , .md , .jsx and .tsx , in that order. .jsx works exactly like .tsx , without types; see File types.

title: Layouts and Slots
text: +layout.ets files wrap pages. A page's layouts are every +layout from its own folder up to pb_pages/ , applied innermost first. A folder may have one layout, written as +layout.ets (or +layout.tsx , see TSX). A layout can't be Markdown: +layout.md is an error at startup. pb_pages/ +layout.ets # applied last (outermost) products/ +layout.ets # applied first [id].ets For /products/123 , [id].ets renders, then products/+layout.ets wraps it, then +layout.ets wraps that.

title: Layouts and Slots
heading: slot()
text: In a layout, slot() returns the content being wrapped: the page, or the inner layout. My Application © My Application without parentheses prints the same content, so 0.x layouts that wrote it still work.

title: Layouts and Slots
heading: Named slots
text: A page (or an inner layout) defines a named slot with slot(name, fn) . fn 's output is captured and nothing is output in place. A layout reads it with slot(name) , which returns '' if it isn't defined. { % Named slots defined by the page or by any inner layout are visible to every outer layout. Defining the same name again replaces it. Inside the new definition's fn , slot(name) still returns the previous content, so a layout can wrap it: { % Docs:

title: Layouts and Slots
heading: Data in layouts
text: Layouts render after the page, with the same ctx . Everything middleware, +page.ts and the page put on ctx.data or ctx.meta is there.

title: Layouts and Slots
heading: When layouts are skipped
text: When the response isn't HTML (a handler set another Content-Type ). When a handler or middleware sent the response itself ( ctx.res.json , ctx.res.html , ctx.res.redirect , ...). For +api.ts routes, which have no template. After ctx.res.layout(false) , called from middleware, +page.ts or the page itself. With the Datastar add-on, for requests that carry Datastar-Request: true . To serve HTML fragments without the site layout, call ctx.res.layout(false) , put the layout in a group ( (site)/+layout.ets ) and the fragments outside it, or send them with ctx.res.html() .

title: Loading Data in PocketPages
text: You can load data right in a template, or in a +page.ts file next to it.

title: Loading Data in PocketPages
heading: Inline data loading
text: The simplest way is a block at the top of your template: Products

title: Loading Data in PocketPages
heading: Server script blocks
text: For better formatting support in editors, you can write ' % instead of . They mean the same thing: ' % const products = ctx.app.findRecordsByFilter('products', 'active = true', 'name', 100) const categories = ctx.app.findAllRecords('categories') Products by Category

title: Loading Data in PocketPages
heading: Structured loading with +page.ts
text: A +page.ts file keeps data loading and form handling out of the template: // pb_pages/products/[id]/+page.ts module.exports = { load(ctx) { ctx.data.product = ctx.app.findRecordById('products', ctx.params.id) }, post(ctx) { const { qty } = ctx.req.body() // ... return ctx.res.redirect( /products/${ctx.params.id} , { flash: 'Added to cart' }) }, }

title: Loading Data in PocketPages
heading: Exports
text: +page.ts exports any of load , get , post , put , patch and delete . load runs first, for every method. Then the handler for the request method runs, if there is one. Then the page renders. A handler can set fields on ctx.data , or return a plain object. A returned object is shallow-assigned into ctx.data ( Object.assign ); there is no deep merge. module.exports = { load(ctx) { return { departments: ctx.app.findAllRecords('departments') } }, get(ctx) { ctx.data.mode = 'view' }, } If a handler sends a response ( ctx.res.redirect , json , html , text , file , sse ), the page doesn't render.

title: Loading Data in PocketPages
heading: Async loading
text: load and the method handlers can be async . PocketPages waits for them before it renders. Every Go function has an .async twin that does its work outside the JS VM, so other requests keep running while it waits: // pb_pages/dashboard/+page.ts module.exports = { async load(ctx) { const [orders, users] = await Promise.all([ ctx.app.countRecords.async('orders'), ctx.app.countRecords.async('users'), ]) return { orders, users } }, } What an async handler returns is used just like a returned object, and an error it throws (or a rejected promise) fails the request like any other error. You can also await right in a template: see ETS and JSX.

title: Loading Data in PocketPages
heading: One +page.ts per folder
