text: A +page.ts applies to every page in its folder. Use ctx.route.name to tell them apart: module.exports = { load(ctx) { if (ctx.route.name === 'details') { ctx.data.reviews = ctx.app.findRecordsByFilter('reviews', 'product = {:id}', '-created', 20, 0, { id: ctx.params.id }) } }, }

title: Loading Data in PocketPages
heading: Methods without a handler
text: Every handler is optional. A page renders for any method, like PHP, so a template can handle a form on its own: Thanks, ! Send A post (or put , ...) handler in +page.ts is the tidier place for form logic as a page grows, but you don't need one. Only routes with nothing to render, +api.ts and a +page.ts without a page, answer 405 for a method they have no handler for.

title: Loading Data in PocketPages
heading: Example: a contact form
text: // pb_pages/contact/+page.ts module.exports = { load(ctx) { return { departments: ctx.app.findAllRecords('departments') } }, post(ctx) { const { email, message, department } = ctx.req.body() try { const record = new Record(ctx.app.findCollectionByNameOrId('messages')) record.set('email', email) record.set('message', message) record.set('department', department) ctx.app.save(record) } catch (e) { return { error: 'Failed to send message', values: { email, message, department } } } return ctx.res.redirect('/contact', { flash: 'Thanks, we got your message.' }) }, } " / " Send

title: Loading Data in PocketPages
heading: Pages without a template
text: A +page.ts in a folder with no page file serves the folder's URL from code. Use it for a page you'd rather build in code, or for a URL that only acts and redirects: // pb_pages/logout/+page.ts module.exports = { post(ctx) { ctx.session.signOut() return ctx.res.redirect('/') }, } // pb_pages/hello/+page.ts module.exports = { get(ctx) { return ctx.res.html( Hello ${ctx.auth ? ctx.auth.getString('name') : 'there'} ) }, } With no template to render, each handler must send a response; returning without one is a 500. Methods without a handler answer 405 , GET included: /logout above only takes POST . Folder middleware runs; layouts don't, so wrap HTML yourself (or render a partial with ctx.include ). Errors show your +error.ets page. For JSON responses and JSON errors, use +api.ts instead.

title: Loading Data in PocketPages
heading: Middleware or +page.ts?
text: Only the route's own folder's +page.ts runs. Every +middleware.ts from pb_pages/ down to the route's folder runs, root first. Use middleware for data or checks that a whole section of the site shares.

title: Markdown Support
text: A .md file is a page, just like an .ets file. Markdown is always on.

title: Markdown Support
heading: How it works
text: Tags first : the file runs through EJS, so the same tags as ETS work in Markdown. Markdown is content, and its tags are a small escape hatch: plain JavaScript inside, with no TypeScript stripping. Then Markdown : the result is rendered as Markdown: CommonMark plus GFM tables, strikethrough, task lists and autolinks.

title: Markdown Support
heading: Front matter
text: YAML between lines at the top of the file is front matter. Each top-level key is passed to ctx.meta(key, value) : title: My Blog Post description: A detailed guide about something interesting # Content starts here... Read the values in a layout with meta : "

title: Markdown Support
heading: Headings
text: Headings get id s, so you can link to them: the text is lowercased, characters other than a-z , 0-9 , - , _ and space are removed, and spaces become - . ## Front matter gets id="front-matter" .

title: Markdown Support
heading: Images
text: Relative image paths go through ctx.asset , so they get fingerprinted URLs: Logo

title: Markdown Support
heading: Markdown partials
text: A .md file in a _private/ folder can be included from an .ets template with include() . It's rendered the same way, tags then Markdown:

title: Markdown Support
heading: Notes
text: Layouts are +layout.ets (or +layout.tsx , see TSX). A layout can't be Markdown: +layout.md is an error at startup. A Markdown page is still wrapped by the layouts above it.

title: Using Middleware in PocketPages
text: Middleware files ( +middleware.ts ) run before your handlers and templates. Use them to: Check authentication Load data a whole section shares Set headers Validate requests

title: Using Middleware in PocketPages
heading: Basic example
text: // pb_pages/admin/+middleware.ts module.exports = (ctx, next) = { if (!ctx.auth) return ctx.res.redirect('/login') ctx.data.section = 'admin' return next() } One signature: (ctx, next) . Call next() to continue, and return its result. Returning without calling next() ends the request. If no response was sent, that's an error (a 500 ; in dev mode the error page names the middleware file). Share data through ctx.data . Middleware can be async . await next() returns once the rest of the request has run, and throws what it threw. // pb_pages/+middleware.ts module.exports = async (ctx, next) = { ctx.data.unread = await ctx.app.countRecords.async('notifications', $dbx.hashExp({ read: false })) const started = Date.now() await next() ctx.log.info('rendered', ctx.route.path, Date.now() - started, 'ms') }

title: Using Middleware in PocketPages
heading: Order
text: Every +middleware.ts from pb_pages/ down to the route's folder runs, root first. Groups count too. pb_pages/ +middleware.ts # runs first (all routes) products/ +middleware.ts # runs second (/products/...) [id]/ +middleware.ts # runs third (/products/[id]) The full order for a request is: Plugins' onRequest Middleware, root first The folder's +page.ts or +api.ts ( load , then the method's handler) The template, then layouts, innermost first The response If any step sends a response, the later steps are skipped.

title: Using Middleware in PocketPages
heading: Auth guard
text: module.exports = (ctx, next) = { if (!ctx.auth) return ctx.res.redirect('/login') return next() }

title: Using Middleware in PocketPages
heading: Request validation
text: // pb_pages/products/[id]/+middleware.ts module.exports = (ctx, next) = { if (!/^[a-z0-9]+$/.test(ctx.params.id)) throw ctx.httpError(400, 'Invalid ID') return next() }

title: Using Middleware in PocketPages
heading: Shared data
text: // pb_pages/+middleware.ts module.exports = (ctx, next) = { ctx.data.categories = ctx.app.findRecordsByFilter('categories', 'active = true', 'name', 100) return next() } "

title: Using Middleware in PocketPages
heading: Headers
text: module.exports = (ctx, next) = { ctx.res.header('X-Frame-Options', 'DENY') return next() }

title: Moving from PocketPages 0.x
text: PocketPages v1 is part of PocketOne (the pages extension). It keeps the ideas of the npm package (a folder of files that become routes, EJS, layouts, middleware, private partials) and changes the shapes. Apps written for 0.x don't run unchanged. There is no migration tool. Start a new app with pocketone pages create , then move your pages over using the list below. The npm package is being retired.

title: Moving from PocketPages 0.x
heading: Folder and boot
text: pb_hooks/pages/ , booted by require('pocketpages') in a .pb.js file pb_pages/ next to pb_data . No boot file, no npm install. create-pocketpages pocketone pages create [--starter ] Delete the .pb.js boot file and the pocketpages dependencies, and move the contents of pb_hooks/pages/ to pb_pages/ .

title: Moving from PocketPages 0.x
heading: JavaScript or TypeScript
text: Your .js and .ejs files stay as they are. v1 also runs TypeScript ( .ts code and .ets templates, types stripped, never checked), and the rest of these docs use it. Renaming a file from .js to .ts or .ejs to .ets changes nothing else, so you can switch a file at a time or not at all. This guide shows v1 code as .js to match yours. See File types.

title: Moving from PocketPages 0.x
heading: The context object
text: 0.x passed an api object and spread its members into each template. v1 passes one ctx object with req , res , data , params , route and helpers. See the ctx reference. request , response ctx.req , ctx.res body() , formData ctx.req.body() redirect(path) ctx.res.redirect(path) response.redirect(path, status) ctx.res.redirect(path, status) (unchanged) env() , store() , dbg() , info() , warn() , error() ctx.env() , ctx.store() , ctx.log.debug() / info() / warn() / error() auth , request.auth ctx.auth resolve(name) ctx.resolve(name) Inside templates, data , params , asset and meta are still available without the ctx. prefix. The other 0.x template globals are gone, including resolve , redirect and env : use ctx.resolve() , ctx.res.redirect() and ctx.env() .

title: Moving from PocketPages 0.x
heading: Parameters, query strings and cookies
text: Query parameters are no longer mixed into params , and nothing is JSON-parsed for you. ctx.params holds route parameters only; read the query string with ctx.req.query(name) , which returns strings. Cookies are strings. Pass { json: true } to parse one: ctx.req.cookie('prefs', { json: true }) .

title: Moving from PocketPages 0.x
heading: Middleware
text: 0.x middleware either returned a value or called next(extra) , depending on how many arguments it declared. v1 has one signature: module.exports = (ctx, next) = { ctx.data.user = ctx.auth return next() } Put shared data on ctx.data . See Middleware.

title: Moving from PocketPages 0.x
heading: Loaders
text: +load.js , +get.js , +post.js and friends are replaced by one +page.js per folder that exports load , get , post , put , patch and delete . Returned objects are shallow-assigned into ctx.data (no deep merge). As in 0.x, every handler is optional and a page renders for any method, so templates that check the request method keep working ( request.method becomes ctx.req.method ). // 0.x: +load.js module.exports = (api) = ({ products: $app.findAllRecords('products') }) // v1: +page.js module.exports = { load(ctx) { return { products: ctx.app.findAllRecords('products') } }, } See Loading Data.

title: Moving from PocketPages 0.x
heading: JSON
text: 0.x sent template output as JSON if it parsed as JSON. v1 never does. Send JSON with ctx.res.json() , usually from a +api.js file. See API Routes and JSON.

title: Moving from PocketPages 0.x
heading: Layouts and slots
text: comments in the page slot('name', () = { % ...<% }) slot and slots.name in layouts slot() and slot('name') See Layouts and Slots.

title: Moving from PocketPages 0.x
heading: Output
text: echo() is gone. A template returns its text; anything you want in the output goes through a tag. For streaming, use ctx.res.sse() .

title: Moving from PocketPages 0.x
heading: Flash messages
text: 0.x put the message in a ?__flash= query parameter with redirect(path, { message }) . v1 uses a one-time cookie: return ctx.res.redirect('/account', { flash: 'Saved' }) Read it on the next request with ctx.flash() . See flash.

title: Moving from PocketPages 0.x
heading: Assets
text: asset() URLs now carry the first 12 hex characters of the file's SHA-256, not the full hash.

title: Moving from PocketPages 0.x
heading: Configuration and plugins
text: +config.js still takes plugin package names, which are loaded with require as before, but the packages must be v1 plugins: the 0.x pocketpages-plugin- packages don't run on v1. auth and realtime are built in, EJS and Markdown are always on, and Datastar is an add-on you copy into pb_pages/_private/ and list as 'datastar' . Its API is 0.x's, with signals() added alongside readSignals . npm plugin package names and EJS options are gone. +config.js must export an object ( module.exports = { ... } ). 0.x's function form, module.exports = (api) = ({ ... }) , is an error. A package.json at the app's root still works: bare require('pkg') looks in the app folder's node_modules after pb_pages . EJS and Markdown are always on. pocketpages-plugin-ejs and pocketpages-plugin-marked have no v1 equivalent because they aren't needed. The auth plugin no longer goes through the JS SDK over HTTP ( api.pb() ). Use ctx.session. , which calls the app directly. See Authentication. See +config.js and Plugins.

title: Moving from PocketPages 0.x
heading: Behavior that changed quietly
text: These don't fail with an error, so check for them when porting: Cookies are HttpOnly by default. Pass { httpOnly: false } to ctx.res.cookie for a cookie your page's JS reads. The pb_auth cookie stays HttpOnly , so pb.authStore.loadFromCookie(document.cookie) in the browser no longer works. Realtime messages are JSON-encoded. ctx.realtime.send(topic, data) sends JSON.stringify(data) , so a string (such as an HTML fragment) arrives in quotes: JSON.parse it on the client. A filter now gets one argument, the client, and only narrows clients already subscribed to the topic. .md , .jsx and .tsx files are always pages , never served as static files. Front matter is plain YAML. EJS tags inside it aren't run. require never leaves pb_pages . To load code from pb_hooks , use require(__hooks + '/lib/x') . Hook files ( .pb.js ) go in pb_hooks . In pb_pages they're an error and aren't served.

title: Moving from PocketPages 0.x
heading: Removed globals
text: url() ctx.req.url stringify() JSON.stringify micro-dash plain JavaScript pb() (JS SDK plugin) ctx.pb() , built in: same SDK, no host setting, runs in-process as the signed-in user

title: Moving from PocketPages 0.x
heading: Routing
text: A route with fewer segments no longer matches a longer URL. Segment counts must match: products/[id].ejs serves /products/123 but not /products/123/reviews .

title: Overview of PocketPages
text: PocketPages turns a folder of files into a server-rendered website, inside PocketOne. It is built in as the pages extension ( ext/pages ): no npm package, no boot file, no build step. Use PocketPages to create slim and modern web apps: Start small and iterate SEO-first principles No build step Fast server-side rendering

title: Overview of PocketPages
heading: Hello world in just one file
text: Inside you write TypeScript; types are stripped, never checked, so plain JavaScript works too. Every page gets a ctx object with the request, the response, your data, and the app itself ( ctx.app ), so you can read and write records directly.

title: Overview of PocketPages
heading: Retro file-based routing
text: Files become URLs, and +layout.ets files wrap the pages below them:

title: Overview of PocketPages
heading: Coming from the npm package?
text: PocketPages v1 is a clean API. Apps written for PocketPages 0.x (the npm package) don't run unchanged. See Moving from PocketPages 0.x.

title: Route and Query Parameters
text: Route parameters come from the URL path. Query parameters come from the query string. v1 keeps them apart.

title: Route and Query Parameters
heading: Route parameters
text: Use square brackets in file or folder names to capture a URL segment: pb_pages/ products/ [productId]/ index.ets reviews/ [reviewId].ets This handles URLs like /products/123 and /products/123/reviews/456 . Read them through params (the same object as ctx.params ): Product: Review: Route parameters are always strings. ctx.params never includes query parameters.

title: Route and Query Parameters
heading: Query parameters
text: Read the query string with ctx.req.query() : /products/123?sort=latest&tag=red&tag=blue Sort by: Tags: ctx.req.query(name) First value as a string, or undefined ctx.req.query(name, { all: true }) Every value, as an array of strings ctx.req.query() { name: firstValue } for every parameter Values are strings. Nothing is parsed for you; if you pass JSON in a query parameter, parse it yourself: const filters = JSON.parse(ctx.req.query('filters') ?? '{}')

title: Route and Query Parameters
heading: The route itself
text: ctx.route describes the matched route: { path, name, file } . For products/[productId]/index.ets , path is /products/[productId] , name is index , and file is products/[productId]/index.ets .

title: Using Partials in PocketPages
text: Partials are reusable templates that you include from other templates. They live in _private/ folders, which are never routed.

title: Using Partials in PocketPages
heading: Including a partial
text: include(name, locals?) renders a template from a _private/ folder and returns its text. Use throws if title wasn't passed, but doesn't. Including more than 32 levels deep is an error.

title: Using Partials in PocketPages
heading: Where partials are found
text: pb_pages/ _private/ header.ets footer.ets blog/ _private/ sidebar.ets posts/ _private/ post-card.ets index.ets PocketPages looks in _private/ in the current template's folder, then in each parent folder up to pb_pages/ . A name starting with / looks only in pb_pages/_private/ : The extension is optional. A dotted name such as include('nav.main') finds nav.main.ets . This means you can: Keep section-specific partials in that section's _private/ . Hoist a shared partial up to a common parent. Override a parent's partial with a local one of the same name, and still reach the root one with /name .

title: Using Partials in PocketPages
heading: Passing data
text: Pass only what the partial needs: Joined Partials can also read ctx , data and params directly. Passing values explicitly keeps them easy to reuse.

title: Using Partials in PocketPages
heading: Markdown partials
text: A .md partial is rendered like a Markdown page: its tags run as plain JavaScript, then Markdown (see Markdown):

title: Using Partials in PocketPages
heading: JavaScript modules
text: _private/ folders also hold TypeScript modules. Load them with ctx.resolve() , which uses the same lookup.

title: Authentication Plugin
text: The auth plugin gives you cookie sessions on PocketBase auth. It calls the app directly, not over HTTP. // pb_pages/+config.ts module.exports = { plugins: ['auth'], }

title: Authentication Plugin
heading: What it does on every request
text: It reads the pb_auth cookie, validates the token and sets ctx.auth to the authenticated record. A bad cookie is cleared. ctx.auth is also set without the plugin when a request carries PocketBase's own Authorization header.

title: Authentication Plugin
heading: ctx.session
text: register(email, password, { collection = 'users', data, verify = true, signIn = true }?) Create an auth record. data holds extra fields. verify sends the verification email; signIn signs the new account in (returns { token: '', record } when false ). signInWithPassword(email, password, { collection }?) Sign in with a password. requestOTP(email, { collection, create = false }?) Send a one-time password. Returns the otpId . An unknown email still gets an id, one that never validates; with create: true the account is created first. signInWithOTP(otpId, code, { collection }?) Sign in with a one-time password. signInAnonymously({ collection }?) Sign in as a new anonymous user. requestOAuth2(provider, { collection, redirectPath = '/auth/oauth/confirm', redirect = true }?) Store state in a cookie and return the provider's URL. With redirect it also sends the redirect; pass redirect: false to send the URL some other way. redirectPath must be a path on this site. signInWithOAuth2(state, code, { createData }?) Complete an OAuth2 sign-in on the redirect path. Returns { token, record, meta } ; meta.isNew is true for a new account. signIn(record) Set the cookie for a record you authenticated yourself. It skips the MFA check below. signOut() Sign out. authMethods({ collection }?) The sign-in methods a collection has turned on: { password: { enabled, identityFields }, otp: { enabled }, mfa: { enabled }, oauth2: { enabled, providers: [{ name, displayName }] } } , as PocketBase's auth-methods API.

title: Authentication Plugin
heading: MFA
text: Pages doesn't have a second sign-in step yet. If a collection has MFA turned on (Collections → users → Options → Multi-factor authentication) and its MFA rule matches the account, every sign-in method above refuses it with "This account needs a second sign-in step (MFA), which pages doesn't support yet." An empty rule matches every account. To use pages sign-in, turn MFA off for the collection, or give it a rule that leaves out the accounts that sign in here. Every sign-in method sets ctx.auth for the rest of the request and returns { token, record } .

title: Authentication Plugin
heading: Email flows
text: These use PocketBase's own checks and mail templates. The request methods never reveal whether an email exists. requestVerification(email, { collection }?) Send the verification email (skipped for an account that's already verified). confirmVerification(token) Mark the account verified. Returns the record. requestPasswordReset(email, { collection }?) Send the password reset email. confirmPasswordReset(token, password, passwordConfirm) Set the new password (and mark the account verified). Returns the record. requestEmailChange(newEmail) Send a confirmation email to newEmail . Needs a signed-in user ( ctx.auth ). confirmEmailChange(token, password) Change the email after checking the current password. Returns the record. A bad or expired token throws an error.

title: Authentication Plugin
heading: Example
text: // pb_pages/login/+page.ts module.exports = { post(ctx) { const { email, password } = ctx.req.body() try { ctx.session.signInWithPassword(email, password) } catch (e) { return { error: 'Invalid email or password', email } } return ctx.res.redirect('/') }, } // pb_pages/logout/+page.ts module.exports = { post(ctx) { ctx.session.signOut() return ctx.res.redirect('/') }, } See the Authentication guide for complete flows: registration, one-time passwords, OAuth2 and anonymous sign-in.

title: Plugin Authoring Guide
text: A custom plugin is a factory that returns hooks: // pb_pages/_private/my-plugin.ts module.exports = (config) = ({ name: 'my-plugin', onRequest(ctx) {}, // before middleware extendContext(ctx) { ctx.hello = () = 'hi' }, transform({ html, ctx, file }) { return html }, // after each template or layout renders }) Turn it on in +config.ts : module.exports = { plugins: ['my-plugin'], // pb_pages/_private/my-plugin.ts }

title: Plugin Authoring Guide
heading: config
text: config is the plugin's entry in +config.ts when that entry is an object ( { factory, ...options } ), else {} : module.exports = { plugins: [{ factory: require('./_private/banner.ts'), text: 'Beta' }], } // pb_pages/_private/banner.ts module.exports = (config) = ({ name: 'banner', transform({ html }) { return html.replace(' ', ${config.text} ) }, })

title: Plugin Authoring Guide
heading: Hooks
text: Every hook is optional. Hooks run in the order plugins are listed in +config.ts . name The plugin's name. onRequest(ctx) At the start of each request, before middleware. extendContext(ctx) Add members to ctx . transform({ html, ctx, file }) After each template or layout renders. Return the new HTML.

title: Plugin Authoring Guide
heading: Example: a context helper
text: module.exports = () = ({ name: 'format', extendContext(ctx) { ctx.formatDate = (d) = new Date(d).toLocaleDateString() }, }) Posted

title: Plugin Authoring Guide
heading: Permissions
text: Custom plugins run with the same permissions as the rest of the app's code. Under a multitenant host, that means the instance's sandbox.

title: Datastar Add-on
text: The Datastar add-on adds helpers for Datastar. It's a custom plugin that ships with PocketPages rather than a built-in: copy addons/datastar.js into pb_pages/_private/ (the datastar starter kit already has it) and list it in +config.ts by name: // pb_pages/+config.ts module.exports = { plugins: ['datastar'], } Add the script tags to your root layout's . They load Datastar v1.0.5. Datastar 1.0 uses a colon between the attribute name and its key ( data-on:click , data-bind:name , data-signals:count , data-class:active , data-attr:href ); the older hyphen form ( data-on-click ) is ignored. See the Datastar attribute reference.

title: Datastar Add-on
heading: ctx.datastar
text: scripts({ spa, realtime }?) Returns the script tags. patchElements(html, { selector, mode, useViewTransition, viewTransitionSelector, namespace }?) Sends a patch-elements SSE event on the current response. mode is outer (default), inner , replace , prepend , append , before , after or remove ; namespace is html (default), svg or mathml . patchSignals(signals, { onlyIfMissing }?) Sends a patch-signals SSE event (JSON Merge Patch: null removes a signal). executeScript(js, { autoRemove, attributes }?) Sends a script to run in the browser. consoleLog(msg) / consoleError(err) Logs to the browser console. redirect(url) Sends the browser to url (a full page load). A Datastar fetch can't follow ctx.res.redirect , so use this from @get / @post handlers. dispatchCustomEvent(name, detail, { selector }?) Fires a CustomEvent on document , or on the elements matching selector . replaceURL(url) Changes the address bar without a navigation ( history.replaceState ). prefetch(urls) Adds speculation rules so the browser prefetches urls . signals() Reads the request's signals as an object: from the datastar query parameter for GET and DELETE, from the body otherwise. readSignals(target) Merges the request's signals into target and returns it (0.x's readSignals(request, target) also works). realtime. Sends the same patches to realtime subscribers. Needs the realtime plugin. Every send also takes eventId and retryDuration (in ms; the default 1000 isn't sent).

title: Datastar Add-on
heading: Pages as patches
text: When a request has the Datastar-Request: true header, the rendered page is sent without layouts, as a patchElements event. If the request has a Datastar-Selector header, the patch goes into that element. This is how this site navigates between docs pages: the layout calls so links in the table of contents fetch the page and patch it into #content . Plain left-clicks are intercepted; modified clicks (Cmd/Ctrl/Shift/Alt, middle-click), links with a target attribute and links to other origins navigate normally. Back/Forward work, including back to the page you landed on: each page opens at the top, and Back/Forward return you to where you were scrolled.

title: Datastar Add-on
heading: Example: a counter
text: Count: // pb_pages/counter/+page.ts module.exports = { post(ctx) { const count = (ctx.store('count') 0) + 1 ctx.store('count', count) ctx.datastar.patchElements( ${count} ) }, }

title: Datastar Add-on
heading: Example: reading signals
text: module.exports = { post(ctx) { const { name, email } = ctx.datastar.signals() if (!name !email) { ctx.datastar.patchSignals({ error: 'Please fill all fields' }) return } ctx.datastar.patchElements(' Thanks! ') }, }

title: Datastar Add-on
heading: Broadcasting
text: With the realtime plugin on, ctx.datastar.realtime. sends patches to every realtime subscriber instead of the current response: // pb_pages/+config.ts module.exports = { plugins: ['realtime', 'datastar'] } ctx.datastar.realtime.patchElements( ${count} )

title: Plugins
text: Plugins add features to ctx and hook into each request. Turn them on in +config.ts : // pb_pages/+config.ts module.exports = { plugins: ['auth', 'realtime', 'datastar'], } Each entry is one of: A name in quotes. It's loaded with require , which looks in this order: a _private/ folder in pb_pages ( 'datastar' finds _private/datastar.js ) pb_pages/node_modules , for a package from your package.json the built-in plugins, 'auth' and 'realtime' A path such as './plugins/my-plugin.ts' works too. A plugin factory , usually require('./_private/my-plugin.ts') . Writing the require yourself with a path skips the lookup above and loads exactly that file, which is how you pick one copy over another: 'datastar' would find _private/datastar.js first, while require('./node_modules/datastar') always loads the package. Datastar isn't built in. It's an add-on file you copy into pb_pages/_private/ and list by name. ETS templates and Markdown are always on; they aren't plugins.

title: Plugins
heading: Built-in plugins
text: auth Cookie sessions on PocketBase auth: sets ctx.auth from the pb_auth cookie and adds ctx.session. sign-in methods. realtime ctx.realtime.send() to PocketBase realtime subscribers.

title: Plugins
heading: Custom plugins
text: A custom plugin is a module that exports a factory returning hooks. List it by name, or require() it yourself, which you need for options ( { factory, ...options } ): module.exports = { plugins: ['auth', 'my-plugin', { factory: require('./_private/other-plugin.ts'), color: 'blue' }], } See Plugin Authoring. Datastar ctx.datastar. helpers for Datastar. Copy addons/datastar.js into pb_pages/_private/ ; the datastar starter kit already has it.

title: Plugins
heading: Order
text: Plugins' hooks run in the order they're listed, and onRequest hooks run before any middleware.

title: Realtime Plugin
text: The realtime plugin sends messages to PocketBase realtime subscribers. // pb_pages/+config.ts module.exports = { plugins: ['realtime'], }

title: Realtime Plugin
heading: ctx.realtime.send(topic, data, { filter }?)
text: Sends data to the subscribers of topic . filter(client) may limit the recipients. // pb_pages/ping/+api.ts module.exports = { post(ctx) { ctx.realtime.send('ping', { at: new Date().toISOString() }) return ctx.res.json({ ok: true }) }, } On the client, subscribe with the PocketBase JS SDK: const pb = new PocketBase(location.origin) pb.realtime.subscribe('ping', (data) = console.log('Received:', data))

title: Realtime Plugin
heading: Filtering recipients
text: ctx.realtime.send('alerts', 'Maintenance at 10:00', { filter: (client) = !!client.get('auth'), })

title: Realtime Plugin
heading: Sending HTML
text: For hypermedia libraries (HTMX, Datastar), send rendered HTML. include() is available in templates, so render the partial there: // pb_pages/xapi/chat/+page.ts module.exports = { post() {}, // accept POST; the page renders and sends } See Realtime Events and the Datastar add-on, which can send Datastar patches over realtime.

title: Working with Private Files and Directories in PocketPages
heading: Names that are never routed
text: + Framework file ( +layout.ets , +page.ts , ...) _ Private. _private/ folders hold partials and modules. Other _ names are ignored. - Ignored (drafts, notes) . Ignored (dotfiles) pb_pages/ _private/ # private (not routable) -drafts/ # ignored helpers/ # normal folder (routable) +page.ts # framework file (not routable) +layout.ets # framework file (not routable) index.ets # page

title: Working with Private Files and Directories in PocketPages
heading: The _private folder
text: _private/ folders serve two purposes: Template partials, rendered with include() TypeScript modules and other files, loaded with ctx.resolve() Both use the same lookup: _private/ in the current template's folder, then each parent folder up to pb_pages/ . A name starting with / looks only in pb_pages/_private/ . pb_pages/ _private/ header.ets format.ts products/ _private/ product-card.ets queries.ts index.ets

title: Working with Private Files and Directories in PocketPages
heading: Modules
text: A module in _private/ is a CommonJS file: // pb_pages/products/_private/queries.ts module.exports = { featured: (app) = app.findRecordsByFilter('products', 'featured = true', '-created', 10), }

title: Working with Private Files and Directories in PocketPages
heading: Notes
text: Files in _private/ are never served. Keep secrets in environment variables (see Managing Secrets), not in files. Keep private files close to where they're used, and hoist them up when several sections share them.

title: Realtime Events
text: PocketBase pushes realtime messages to browsers over server-sent events. In PocketPages, page code sends, and browsers receive.

title: Realtime Events
heading: Sending from a page
text: Turn on the realtime plugin and call ctx.realtime.send() : // pb_pages/+config.ts module.exports = { plugins: ['realtime'] } // pb_pages/rooms/[id]/+api.ts module.exports = { post(ctx) { ctx.realtime.send( rooms/${ctx.params.id}/delta , ctx.req.body()) return ctx.res.json({ ok: true }) }, } Limit recipients with a filter: ctx.realtime.send('alerts', 'Hi', { filter: (client) = !!client.get('auth') }) Page code can't subscribe to realtime topics itself; it only sends.

title: Realtime Events
heading: Receiving in the browser
text: Use the PocketBase JS SDK: const pb = new PocketBase(location.origin) const unsubscribe = await pb.realtime.subscribe( rooms/${ROOM_ID}/delta , (e) = { console.log('Received delta:', e) }) // Later unsubscribe() The SDK reconnects on its own and resubscribes to its topics after a reconnect.

title: Realtime Events
heading: Hypermedia
text: To push HTML instead of data, see HTMX Integration and the Datastar add-on.

title: File-Based Routing
text: URLs come from the files and folders in pb_pages/ .

title: File-Based Routing
heading: Pages
text: index.ets / about.ets /about docs/index.md /docs (and /docs/ ) docs/routing.md /docs/routing products/[id].ets /products/123 , with ctx.params.id = "123" [org]/[repo]/index.ets /acme/web , with ctx.params = { org: "acme", repo: "web" } The extension is dropped. index maps to its folder. [name] matches exactly one non-empty segment. A parameter must be the whole segment: post-[id].ets is an error at startup. Segment counts must match: products/[id].ets doesn't match /products/123/reviews . A URL with a trailing slash matches the same route as without it. Pages never redirect to add or remove one. Matching is case-sensitive. See Accessing Parameters.

title: File-Based Routing
heading: Groups
text: A folder named (name) doesn't add a URL segment. Use groups to give part of the site its own layout or middleware: pb_pages/ (site)/ +layout.ets # wraps everything in (site) index.ets # / about.ets # /about xapi/ count.ets # /xapi/count, outside the (site) layout

title: File-Based Routing
heading: API routes
text: A +api.ts file serves its folder's URL without a template: feeds/rss/+api.ts serves /feeds/rss . [param] folders work as for pages. A folder can't have both a +api.ts and an index page. See API Routes and JSON. A +page.ts in a folder with no page serves the folder's URL from JS too: logout/+page.ts serves /logout . See Pages without a template.

title: File-Based Routing
heading: Static files
text: Every other file is served as-is at its path, with groups removed: assets/app.css serves /assets/app.css . See Static content.

title: File-Based Routing
heading: Which route wins
text: /api/... and /_/... belong to PocketBase. Pages never see them. Among matching routes the most specific wins: segments are compared from the left, and a literal segment beats a [param] . So products/new.ets beats products/[id].ets for /products/new . A static file and a page can't claim the same URL (startup error). A URL nothing in pb_pages matches goes on to pb_public , then to PocketBase.

title: File-Based Routing
heading: When routes change
text: The route table is built when the app starts and rebuilt whenever anything in pb_pages changes. A rebuild never restarts the app or reloads pb_hooks . Startup errors (bad names, conflicts) are logged with the file path, and the previous route table keeps serving.

title: Managing Secrets in PocketPages
text: Keep API keys, passwords and other secrets in environment variables, and read them with ctx.env(name) . It returns '' when the variable is unset. // pb_pages/checkout/+page.ts module.exports = { post(ctx) { const key = ctx.env('STRIPE_SECRET_KEY') if (!key) throw new Error('STRIPE_SECRET_KEY is not set') // ... }, } ctx.env reads the app's environment. Under a multitenant host's sandbox, it reads the instance's environment.

title: Managing Secrets in PocketPages
heading: Best practices
text: Never put secrets in the page. Anything a template outputs goes to the browser. " " Check for required variables and fail clearly when one is missing. Use descriptive names : STRIPE_SECRET_KEY , not KEY . Never commit secrets to version control, and use different values in development and production.

title: Managing Secrets in PocketPages
heading: Setting environment variables
text: # Shell export STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_test_... pocketone serve # Docker ENV STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_test_...

title: PocketPages v1 specification
text: The contract for ext/pages , PocketOne's server-rendered multi-page app extension. The test fixtures ( fixtures/ ), the starter kits and the PocketPages site are written against this document. Where the implementation and this document disagree, one of them is a bug. v1 is a clean API. It keeps PocketPages' ideas (a folder of files that become routes, EJS, layouts, middleware, private partials) and changes the shapes. Apps written for the npm package (0.x) don't run unchanged; "Changes from 0.x" (section 12) lists every difference. Code files and templates come in TypeScript ( .ts , .ets , .tsx ) and plain JavaScript ( .js , .ejs , .jsx ), which behave the same apart from types. Samples here use whichever is shortest; the user docs use .ts and .ets .

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 1. The pb_pages folder
text: Pages live in their own folder next to PocketBase's others: myapp/ pb_data/ pb_hooks/ pb_migrations/ pb_public/ pb_pages/ A single app finds it at pb_pages next to pb_data , or at --pagesDir (a relative path resolves against the working directory, like --hooksDir ). Serving is automatic: the standard PocketOne binary includes pages, and an app serves its pb_pages whenever the folder exists (it starts serving if the folder appears later). There is no on/off switch; no folder, no pages. Under the multitenant host every instance has its own pb_pages . If the folder doesn't exist, the extension does nothing for that app. Page code can require() modules from pb_pages ( _private/ folders, then node_modules ), then from the app's usual module paths. The same require works in modules, JSX/TSX components and EJS templates: ./x and ../x are files in pb_pages , relative to the requiring file, never above pb_pages . Without an extension, .js , .ts , .tsx , .jsx , .json and .cjs are tried, then a folder's package.json or index . A bare name ( pkg , pkg/sub , @scope/pkg ) is looked up first in _private/ folders, from the requiring file's folder up to the top of pb_pages , the same lookup as include (4.2; the extensions above are tried). Then it's looked up in the nearest node_modules folder, the same way up. A package resolves through its package.json : exports (a string, or conditions, where require , then node , then default are used), else main , else index.js . With exports , only what it lists can be required, and no entry may point outside the package. Then pb_hooks/node_modules , then the app folder's node_modules (the folder that holds pb_pages , where 0.x sites keep package.json ). Anything not found that way goes to the app's own module loader. If that fails too, the error lists the folders searched. A require cycle ( a requires b , which requires a ) gets the exports as they are so far, as in Node. node_modules is never routed or served, and isn't watched: after changing files in it, change any file in pb_pages (or restart) to reload. Page code runs in the app's JS VM, so PocketBase's JSVM globals ( $app , Record , $dbx , $security , ...) are available, as far as the sandbox allows for untrusted apps. Deploying: pb_pages is part of an app's code, next to pb_hooks and pb_migrations (the deploy extension uploads it the same way). Pages' own file access (routes, static files, includes, assets) never leaves pb_pages .

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 1.1 Special names
text: A path segment (file or folder name) starting with one of these characters is never a URL: + Framework file: +config , +middleware , +page , +api ( .js or .ts ); +layout , +error , +404 ( .ets , .ejs , .jsx or .tsx ). +middleware , +page , +api and +layout : one of each per folder. +config , +error and +404 : only at the top of pb_pages (in a subfolder they're an error at startup). Any other + name is an error at startup. _ Private. _private/ folders hold partials and modules for include() and ctx.resolve() . Other _ names are ignored. - Ignored (drafts, notes). . Ignored (dotfiles), except a top-level .well-known/ , which is served as static files (ACME challenges, security.txt , app links). node_modules/ is never routed. Hook files ( .pb.js , .pb.ts ) belong in pb_hooks : in pb_pages they're a startup error and never served.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 1.2 Groups
text: A folder named (name) groups files without adding a URL segment: (marketing)/about.ejs serves /about . Groups can carry their own +layout.ejs , +middleware.js and _private/ .

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 2.1 Pages
text: A page is a template file: .ets , .ejs , .md , .jsx or .tsx (4.1, 4.5). index.ejs / about.ejs /about docs/index.md /docs (and /docs/ ) docs/routing.md /docs/routing products/[id].ejs /products/123 , with ctx.params.id = "123" [org]/[repo]/index.ejs /acme/web , with ctx.params = { org: "acme", repo: "web" } The extension is dropped. index maps to its folder. [name] matches exactly one non-empty segment. A segment may mix text and a parameter only as the whole segment; post-[id].ejs is an error at startup. A URL with a trailing slash matches the same route as without it. Pages never redirect to add or remove one. Matching is case-sensitive.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 2.2 API routes
text: A +api.js file serves its folder's URL without a template: feeds/rss/+api.js serves /feeds/rss . [param] folders work as for pages. If a folder has both +api.js and an index page, startup fails. A +page.js in a folder with no page (no template file) and no +api.js serves the folder's URL the same way, from JS: logout/+page.js serves /logout (3.2).

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 2.3 Static files
text: Every other file is served as-is at its path (groups removed): assets/app.css serves /assets/app.css . Files that mustn't be served (build inputs such as a Tailwind source) take a - prefix: assets/-app.tailwind.css . Content type from the extension. ETag from the content hash; If-None-Match answers 304 . Fingerprinted URLs (see ctx.asset , 6.5) are served with Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable .

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 2.4 Precedence
text: /api/... and /_/... are PocketBase's. Pages never see them, and a pb_pages/api/ folder is an error at startup. Among matching routes the most specific wins: compare segment by segment from the left; a literal segment beats a [param] . So products/new.ejs beats products/[id].ejs for /products/new . A static file and a page can't claim the same URL (startup error). A URL nothing in pb_pages matches goes on to pb_public , then to PocketBase. If pb_pages/+404.ejs exists, a GET / HEAD that nothing (pages, pb_public , PocketBase) answers renders it inside the root layout with status 404 (never for /api/ or /_/ ). The root +middleware.js runs first; page code can still change the status. The route table is built when the app starts and rebuilt when anything in pb_pages changes. A rebuild never restarts the app or reloads pb_hooks . Startup errors (bad names, conflicts) are logged with the file path; the previous table keeps serving if there was one.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 3. Request flow
text: For a URL that matches a page or API route, one JS call does all of this, in order: Plugins: every plugin's extendContext , then every plugin's onRequest (built-in and custom plugins, in config order), so an onRequest can use what any plugin added to ctx . Middleware , root first: every +middleware.js from pb_pages/ down to the route's folder (groups included). Handlers : the folder's +page.js (or +api.js ): load , then the handler for the request method. Template (pages only), then layouts , innermost first. Response. The call runs under the app's usual JS limits (execution time, memory), as one unit. If any step sends a response ( ctx.res.redirect , json , html , text , file , sse ), the later steps are skipped. Async. Middleware, load , method handlers, templates and components may be async (or return a promise). Each step waits for the one before it to settle, while the app's event loop runs, so await works on the .async twin of any Go function ( await ctx.app.countRecords.async('orders') ) and on any other promise. A rejected promise fails the request like a thrown error. Sync code never makes a promise, so it runs exactly as it would without this.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 3.1 Middleware
text: // pb_pages/admin/+middleware.js module.exports = (ctx, next) = { if (!ctx.auth) return ctx.res.redirect('/login') ctx.data.section = 'admin' return next() } One signature: (ctx, next) . Call next() to continue; return its result. Returning without calling next() ends the request. If no response was sent, that's an error (500, and in dev the error page names the middleware file). Middleware may be async: await next() returns once the rest of the request (later middleware, handlers, template, layouts) has finished, and throws what it threw, so code after it can act on the outcome. A sync middleware that calls next() without returning it still has the rest of the request awaited after it. Share data through ctx.data .

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 3.2 Handlers: +page.js
text: // pb_pages/products/[id]/+page.js module.exports = { load(ctx) { ctx.data.product = ctx.app.findRecordById('products', ctx.params.id) }, post(ctx) { const { qty } = ctx.req.body() // ... return ctx.res.redirect( /products/${ctx.params.id} , { flash: 'Added to cart' }) }, } Exports any of load , get , post , put , patch , delete . All are optional: a page renders for any method. load runs for every method; then the method's handler, if there is one. HEAD runs load and get like GET (only the body is dropped), so keep side effects in post / put / patch / delete . A handler may set ctx.data fields, or return a plain object, which is shallow-assigned into ctx.data ( Object.assign ). There is no deep merge. Handlers may be async. A returned promise is awaited, and what it settles to is treated as a returned value. A +page.js applies to every page in its folder. ctx.route.name tells them apart. A method with no handler still renders the page, for every method (like PHP): a template can handle a form itself by checking ctx.req.method , with no +page.js . Only routes with nothing to render ( +api.js , and a +page.js without a page) answer 405 for a method with no handler, with an Allow header listing the methods that have handlers ( GET, HEAD when there's a get ), in the order GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE . Without a page. A +page.js in a folder with no template serves the folder's URL from JS (2.2): there's nothing to render, so a handler must send a response ( ctx.res.html , ctx.res.redirect , ctx.res.json , ...), and returning without one is a 500. Methods without a handler answer 405 , GET included. Unlike +api.js , errors are pages ( +error.ejs or the HTML error page), not JSON. Folder middleware runs; layouts don't.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 3.3 API handlers: +api.js
text: Same exports as +page.js . There is no template, so a handler must send a response; returning without one is a // pb_pages/feeds/latest/+api.js module.exports = { get(ctx) { const posts = ctx.app.findRecordsByFilter('posts', 'published = true', '-created', 20) return ctx.res.json(posts.map((p) = ({ id: p.id, title: p.getString('title') }))) }, }

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 4.1 EJS and ETS
text: .ets is EJS whose tags hold TypeScript; .ejs is the same with plain JavaScript. An .ets template is compiled like an .ejs one, then esbuild (built into the binary) strips the types from the whole compiled function, since one tag's code ( if (x) { ) is rarely valid on its own. Types are stripped, not checked. A TypeScript syntax error names the template line (from the nearest line marker before it). Everything below applies to both. Run code, no output Output, HTML-escaped Output, raw Nothing Also remove the newline right after the tag Also remove whitespace before / after the tag on its line script server code Same as Escaping replaces & " ' with & < > " ' . null and undefined output as an empty string. A template is compiled once per content hash and reused. await . A template whose code uses await (in any tag) is compiled as an async function, so works. Including an async partial returns a promise: print it with , which makes the including template async too. Printing a promise without await is an error, not [object Promise] . await slot('name', async () = { % ...<% }) defines a slot whose content awaits. Templates without await stay plain functions. In scope inside a template: ctx , data (= ctx.data ), params (= ctx.params ), include , slot , asset (= ctx.asset ), meta (= ctx.meta ), require (the same require as page code, 1). A template returns its text. There is no echo ; anything you want in the output goes through a tag.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 4.2 Partials: include
text: include(name, locals?) renders a template from a _private/ folder and returns its text. Use . A page or layout gets an empty locals . Including more than 32 levels deep is an error (recursion guard).

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 4.3 Slots and layouts
text: +layout.ejs files wrap pages. A page's layouts are every +layout.ejs from its own folder up to pb_pages/ , applied innermost first. A folder may have one layout. { % slot(name, fn) defines a named slot: fn 's output is captured and nothing is output in place. slot(name) returns a slot's content ( '' if not defined). slot() returns the content being wrapped: the page, or the inner layout. (no call, as 0.x layouts wrote it) prints the same thing. Named slots defined by the page or by any inner layout are visible to every outer layout. Defining the same name again replaces it; inside the new definition's fn , slot(name) still returns the previous content, so a layout can wrap it ( slot('title', () = { % Docs: <% }) ). Layouts are skipped when the response isn't HTML (a handler set another Content-Type ) or after ctx.res.layout(false) . A page with an inner extension gets that type: robots.txt.ejs serves /robots.txt as text/plain and feed.xml.ejs serves /feed.xml as XML, so layouts are skipped. .html (or no inner extension) is HTML. Page code can still set another Content-Type .

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 4.4 Markdown pages
text: A .md page is EJS first, then Markdown (CommonMark + GFM tables, strikethrough, task lists, autolinks). Front matter between lines at the top is YAML, removed before EJS runs. Each top-level key is passed to ctx.meta(key, value) , for pages and for included .md partials. Headings get id s: lowercased, characters other than a-z 0-9 - _ space removed, spaces to - ; a repeated id gets -1 , -2 , ... appended. Fenced code blocks render as " . Raw HTML passes through unchanged. Relative image paths go through ctx.asset . A .md partial is rendered (EJS, then Markdown) on its own and inserted as HTML; Markdown never runs twice on the same text. Leave blank lines around an include in Markdown so the HTML stays a block.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 4.5 JSX and TSX
text: .jsx and .tsx files are templates too: pages, layouts ( +layout.tsx ), +error / +404 , and partials in _private/ . They're compiled when first used by esbuild, which is built into the binary (no Node, no build step), and cached by content like EJS. TypeScript types are stripped, not checked. TSX is the component style; the docs use ETS (4.1) and treat TSX as the alternative, one style per app. // pb_pages/products/[id].tsx import Price from './_private/Price' export default function Product({ data, slot }: pages.Props) { slot('title', data.product.getString('name')) return ( {data.product.getString('name')} ) } The file's default export is a component: a function from props to markup. Props: ctx , data , params , meta , asset , include , slot , children , plus an include 's locals. JSX renders straight to HTML on the server. There's no virtual DOM, no hydration, no client-side React. Event handler props (functions) are dropped; use plain attributes ( onclick="..." , hx-get , data-on:click ). Text and attribute values are escaped. dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html }} inserts raw HTML. class and className both work, as do for and htmlFor . style takes a string or an object ( { marginTop: 4 } → margin-top:4 ). true renders a bare attribute; false , null and undefined leave it out. renders with in front of it (JSX can't write a doctype). In a layout, children is the inner content. slot(name) reads a named slot, slot(name, content) sets one (content is JSX or a string), slot() is the same as children . include(name, locals) returns the partial's HTML, ready to put in JSX. An EJS/ETS template can include a .jsx / .tsx partial: its locals become props. Components are ordinary modules: import Card from './_private/Card' (resolved like require , 3.2). Partials are looked up with extensions in this order: .ets , .ejs , .md , .jsx , .tsx . Async components. Any component may be async , the file's default export included. The render waits for it wherever it sits in the tree; sibling async components run concurrently. include() of an async partial and slot(name, content) with async content work the same way, and a layout reads the slot once it has settled. TypeScript modules. +page.ts , +api.ts , +middleware.ts , +config.ts and any .ts file reached by require / import work like their .js versions. A module whose only export is export default behaves like module.exports = ... . Types. The extension adds its declarations to the app's types.d.ts (the JS engine's TypeScript() hook): a pages namespace ( Context , Handlers , Middleware , Config , PluginFactory , Props ) and a permissive JSX namespace. They add no globals. pages.Data and pages.Context are interfaces an app may extend.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 5. Responses
text: A handler or middleware sent one That one Page rendered 200 text/html; charset=utf-8 (or the status set with ctx.res.status ) HEAD As GET , without a body No handler for the method Page: rendered as usual. +api.js or a +page.js without a page: 405 + Allow Error thrown 500 (see 8) JSON is only sent through ctx.res.json (or +api.js ). Template output is never parsed as JSON.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 6. The ctx object
text: One object per request, passed to middleware, handlers, templates and plugins.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 6.1 ctx.req
text: method "GET" , "POST" , ... url { href, origin, pathname, search } query(name) First value of a query parameter as a string, or undefined query(name, { all: true }) Every value, as an array of strings query() { name: firstValue } for every parameter header(name) Request header, '' if absent cookie(name) Cookie value as a string, or undefined cookie(name, { json: true }) Cookie parsed as JSON ( undefined if absent or not JSON) cookies() { name: value } , strings body() Parsed body: JSON object, or form fields ( application/x-www-form-urlencoded , multipart/form-data ) as { name: value } (repeated names as arrays) files(name) Uploaded files for a multipart field, as PocketBase filesystem.File values ready for a record field ip Client IP as PocketBase resolves it (trusted proxy settings apply) event The underlying PocketBase RequestEvent , for anything not covered here Query values and cookies are strings unless you ask for JSON. Nothing is parsed for you.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 6.2 ctx.res
text: status(code) Status for the rendered page. Returns ctx.res . header(name, value) Set a response header; returns ctx.res . header(name) reads it back. cookie(name, value, options?) Set a cookie. Non-string values are JSON.stringify 'd; the value is then percent-encoded ( encodeURIComponent ), and ctx.req.cookie decodes it. Defaults: path=/ , HttpOnly , SameSite=Lax , Secure when the request is HTTPS. Options: path , domain , maxAge (seconds), expires (a Date , milliseconds since the epoch, or a date string; with maxAge too, browsers use maxAge ), httpOnly , secure , sameSite . clearCookie(name, options?) Expire a cookie (same path / domain as when set). redirect(location, { status = 302, flash }?) or redirect(location, status) Send a redirect. status must be a 3xx code. flash sets a one-time message (6.4). json(data) / json(status, data) Send JSON. html(html) / html(status, html) Send HTML as-is (no layouts). text(text) / text(status, text) Send plain text. file(path) Send a file from pb_pages (path relative to pb_pages ). sse() Start a text/event-stream response; returns { send(event, data, { id, retry }?), comment(text), close() } . layout(false) Render this page without layouts (e.g. an HTML fragment for htmx). sent true once a response has been sent.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 6.3 Data and routing
text: ctx.data Plain object shared by middleware, handlers and templates. Starts as {} . ctx.params Route parameters, strings. Never includes query parameters. ctx.route { path, name, file } : the URL pattern without groups ( /products/[id] , /docs for docs/index.md ), the file name without extension ( [id] , index ; +api for API routes) and the file relative to pb_pages , groups included.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 6.4 Flash messages
text: ctx.res.redirect(path, { flash: 'Saved' }) stores the message as JSON in a cookie ( pp_flash , encoded like any cookie, HttpOnly , Max-Age=300 ). ctx.flash() on the next request returns it and clears it ( Max-Age=0 ). It returns undefined when there is none. Calling it again in the same request returns the same value. A flash can be any JSON value.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 6.5 Helpers
text: ctx.auth The authenticated record, or null . Set by PocketBase's own auth (an Authorization header) or by the auth plugin's cookie. ctx.app The app ( $app ): records, collections, settings. ctx.pb() A PocketBase JS SDK client (the bundled synchronous build) acting as the signed-in user ( ctx.auth ), or as a guest. Its requests go to the app's own API in-process (no network), so collection API rules, expand and field visibility apply exactly as for a browser. API errors throw the SDK's ClientResponseError ( e.status , e.response ). Only /api/ routes; file uploads through the SDK aren't supported (use ctx.app ). ctx.env(name) Environment variable, '' if unset (the app's environment; under the sandbox, the instance's). ctx.log debug , info , warn , error : to the app's log. debug only shows in dev. ctx.meta(key, value?) Per-request key/value store for page metadata (title, description). Set with two arguments, read with one. ctx.asset(path) URL for a static file in pb_pages , with its content hash: asset('app.css') → /assets/app.3f9a1c2b7d4e.css . Relative paths resolve from the current file's folder; / -paths from pb_pages . A path that isn't a file in pb_pages is returned unchanged. ctx.include(name, locals?) Render a _private/ partial from JS (handlers, middleware, plugins) and get its text; same lookup as the template include , from the route's folder. ctx.resolve(name, { mode }?) Load a module from _private/ , looked up from the route's folder up (like ctx.include ; wherever it's called from); without an extension, the name, then .js , .ts and .json are tried. Modes: require (default, the module's exports), raw (file text), script (text wrapped in ), style (wrapped in ). ctx.pagesDir The absolute path of this app's pb_pages folder, e.g. for listing files with $os.readDir . Read-only. ctx.store(name, value?) The app's in-memory store ( $app.store() ): set with two arguments, read with one. ctx.dev true in dev mode. Fingerprinted asset names carry the first 12 hex characters of the file's SHA-256: name. .ext .

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 7. Configuration: +config.js
text: // pb_pages/+config.js module.exports = { plugins: ['auth', 'realtime', 'datastar'], debug: false, } plugins [] Module names, built-in names ( auth , realtime ), or custom plugin factories such as add-ons (9). Templates and Markdown are always on. debug false Detailed error pages and ctx.log.debug output even outside dev mode. A string in plugins is a module name, required from +config.js (1): a _private/ file ( 'datastar' finds _private/datastar.js ), a package in node_modules ( 'my-plugin' ) or a path ( './plugins/my-plugin.js' ). Its export, or its default export, must be a plugin factory (9.2). Only when no module by that name is found is the string a built-in (9.1), so a _private/auth.js or a package named auth would replace the built-in auth . To skip that order and load one exact file, list require('./path') instead of the name: a ./ path is never looked up in _private/ or node_modules . A module that is found but fails to load is an error; it never falls back to the built-in. +config.js runs on each page request, so these aren't caught at startup: unknown keys, names that are neither a module nor a built-in, or a plugin listed twice make every page answer with an error (a 500; dev mode shows the reason on the page), and the reason goes to the log.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 8. Errors
text: Anything thrown in middleware, a handler or a template becomes a 500 . Dev mode or debug: true : an HTML error page with the message, the file and line (template lines map to the .ets / .ejs / .md source), and the stack trimmed to pb_pages -relative paths. Otherwise: a plain "Something went wrong" page. The full error always goes to the app's log. throw ctx.httpError(status, message) sends that status (e.g. 404 , 403 ) with a plain page showing message . In a +api.js it's JSON: { "status": 404, "message": "..." } . A custom error page: pb_pages/+error.ejs renders for every ctx.httpError and every 500 outside dev mode, with ctx.error = { status, message } , inside the root layout.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 9.1 Built-in
text: Turned on by name in +config.js when no module by that name is found (7). auth : cookie sessions on PocketBase auth, without calling the app over HTTP. Every request: reads the pb_auth cookie, validates the token, sets ctx.auth (or clears a bad cookie). The cookie holds { token, record } as JSON (the JS SDK's cookie format), HttpOnly , SameSite=Lax , Secure on HTTPS, lasting as long as the collection's auth token. identity arguments accept any of the collection's identity fields (email by default). MFA: pages has no second sign-in step yet, so every sign-in method (password, OTP, anonymous, OAuth2, and register 's sign-in) refuses an account that needs MFA, as PocketBase decides it: the collection has MFA on and its MFA rule matches the record (an empty rule matches everyone; a rule that can't be checked counts as a match). The error says so; nothing is signed in and an OTP isn't used up. A wrong password still says only that the credentials are invalid. ctx.session.signIn(record) is the exception: it signs in a record the app authenticated itself. ctx.session.authMethods({ collection }) → { password: { enabled, identityFields }, otp: { enabled }, mfa: { enabled }, oauth2: { enabled, providers: [{ name, displayName }] } } , as PocketBase's auth-methods API. ctx.session.register(email, password, { collection = 'users', data, verify = true, signIn = true }) : creates the record; sends the verification email when verify ; signs in when signIn . ctx.session.signInWithPassword(identity, password, { collection }) ctx.session.requestOTP(email, { collection, create = false }) → otpId . Always returns an id (unknown emails get one that never validates, as PocketBase does); with create: true a missing record is created first. ctx.session.signInWithOTP(otpId, code, { collection }) ctx.session.signInAnonymously({ collection }) ctx.session.requestOAuth2(provider, { collection, redirectPath = '/auth/oauth/confirm', redirect = true }) : stores state in a cookie and returns the provider's URL; with redirect it also sends the redirect ( ctx.res.sent ). redirectPath must be a path on this site. PKCE is used when the provider supports it. ctx.session.signInWithOAuth2(state, code, { createData }?) : completes it on the redirect path (the state cookie carries the provider, collection and PKCE verifier; it lasts 10 minutes and works once). The sign-in runs through PocketBase's own auth-with-oauth2 endpoint in-process, so sign-up, account linking (to the signed-in account, if any), the anti-hijacking checks and onRecordAuthWithOAuth2Request hooks behave as in PocketBase. createData is extra data for a new record. Returns { token, record, meta } ( meta is PocketBase's OAuth2 meta, with isNew ). Accounts that need MFA throw an error: pages doesn't do MFA yet. Apple answers with a POST, so read state and code from ctx.req.body() there. On HTTPS the state cookie is SameSite=None so it survives that cross-site POST. ctx.session.signIn(record) : set the cookie for a record you authenticated yourself. ctx.session.signOut() Email flows, with PocketBase's own checks and mail templates: requestVerification(email, { collection }) , confirmVerification(token) , requestPasswordReset(email, { collection }) , confirmPasswordReset(token, password, passwordConfirm) , requestEmailChange(newEmail) (needs ctx.auth ), confirmEmailChange(token, password) . Request methods never reveal whether an email exists. Every sign-in method sets ctx.auth for the rest of the request and returns { token, record } . realtime : PocketBase realtime from page code. ctx.realtime.send(topic, data, { filter }?) sends to every client subscribed to topic (the filter only narrows that set). data is always JSON-encoded (a string arrives as a JSON string, as PocketBase's own messages do). filter(client) returns true to include a client. client is PocketBase's realtime client: id() , get(key) , set(key, value) , hasSubscription(topic) . ctx.realtime.client(id) returns one client by id, or null . Sending never waits for slow clients: each message is handed to the client's queue in the background.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 9.2 Custom plugins
text: A custom plugin is a factory that returns hooks: module.exports = (config) = ({ name: 'my-plugin', onRequest(ctx) {}, // before middleware extendContext(ctx) { ctx.hello = () = 'hi' }, transform({ html, ctx, file }) { return html }, // after each page or layout renders (not partials) }) config is the plugin's entry in +config.js when it's an object ( { factory, ...options } ), else {} . name is required and unique. 0.x hook names ( onExtendContextApi , onRender , onResponse , handles ) are an error that names the v1 hook to use. There's no hook for treating other kinds of files as pages: a page's inner extension already does that ( robots.txt.ejs serves /robots.txt as text/plain , 4.5). Hooks run in config order. Every hook is optional. Custom plugins run with the same permissions as the rest of the app's code (sandboxed in a multitenant host).

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 9.3 Add-ons
text: Plugins for third-party libraries ship as JS files in ext/pages/addons/ , not built into ext/pages . Copy one into pb_pages/_private/ and list it in +config.js by name ( 'datastar' ). datastar.js (Datastar) adds ctx.datastar : ctx.datastar.scripts({ spa: { scope, selector }, realtime }?) returns the script tags ( spa turns on client-side navigation for links under scope , swapping selector ). With realtime: true the page subscribes to the datastar realtime topic and sets a $clientId signal to its realtime client id. ctx.datastar.patchElements(html, { selector, mode }?) , ctx.datastar.patchSignals(signals, { onlyIfMissing }?) ( signals is an object), ctx.datastar.executeScript(js) send SSE events on the current response. The first one starts the stream ( ctx.res.sent becomes true ); later steps still run, but their output isn't sent and the automatic patch below doesn't happen. The stream closes when the request ends. ctx.datastar.signals() returns the request's signals as an object (from the datastar query parameter on GET , the JSON body otherwise). readSignals(target) (or 0.x's readSignals(request, target) ) merges them into target and returns it. Script helpers, each an executeScript (options { eventId, retryDuration, autoRemove = true, attributes } ; autoRemove adds data-effect="el.remove()" so the script tag removes itself, attributes is a list of extra attribute strings such as 'type="module"' ): consoleLog(msg) , consoleError(err) , redirect(url) (a full page load), dispatchCustomEvent(name, detail, { selector, bubbles, cancelable, composed, eventId, retryDuration }?) (on document by default), replaceURL(url) ( history.replaceState ) and prefetch(urls) (a speculationrules script that stays in the page). mode is one of outer (default), inner , replace , prepend , append , before , after , remove . When a request has Datastar-Request: true , the rendered page (without layouts) is sent as a patchElements event, into Datastar-Selector if given. ctx.datastar.realtime.patchElements(html, options?, { filter }?) , .patchSignals(signals, options?, { filter }?) and .executeScript(js, { filter }?) send the same events to datastar realtime subscribers (needs realtime ).

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 10. Dev mode
text: On when the app runs in dev mode ( --dev ) or +config.js sets debug: true : detailed error pages (8); ctx.log.debug output; template cache keyed by content hash, so edits show on the next request (the route table is rebuilt on any file change in every mode).

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 11. Starter kits
text: pocketone pages create [--starter ] creates the folder (it must not exist) and copies the whole kit into it. Run it with cd && pocketone serve --dir ./pb_data ( pocketone keeps pb_data next to its executable by default; pb_pages and pb_migrations are found next to pb_data ). pocketone pages starters lists the kits. Kits: minimal (default), mvp , htmx , daisyui , daisyui-docs , datastar , auth . The command needs a build that includes ext/pages . It copies pb_pages/ plus anything beside it ( pb_migrations/ , README.md , a package.json for CSS tooling). Kits ship inside ext/pages ( starters/ ).

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 12. Changes from 0.x (npm PocketPages)
text: pb_hooks/pages/ , booted by require('pocketpages') in a .pb.js pb_pages/ , no boot file, no npm install api object, re-spread into each call ctx with req , res , data , params , route , helpers Query parameters mixed into params , JSON-parsed ctx.params is route parameters only; ctx.req.query() returns strings Cookies JSON-parsed on read Strings; { json: true } to parse Middleware: return a value, or call next(extra) , chosen by arity (ctx, next) , data on ctx.data +load.js , +get.js , +post.js , ... per folder, results deep-merged One +page.js exporting load , get , post , ...; returned objects shallow-assigned +config.js may export (api) = ({...}) It must export an object; a function is an error Template output that parses as JSON is sent as JSON Only ctx.res.json or +api.js comments; layouts read slot / slots slot(name, fn) to define, slot(name) / slot() to read echo() writes during render Templates return text; streaming only through ctx.res.sse() redirect(path, { message }) puts the flash in ?__flash= ctx.res.redirect(path, { flash }) , one-time cookie, ctx.flash() asset() fingerprint: full SHA-256 First 12 hex characters +config.js plugins: npm package names, EJS options A name is required first (a _private/ file or package), then a built-in; or a JS factory. EJS and Markdown always on Plugin hooks onRequest({ request, response }) , onExtendContextApi , onRender , onResponse , handles extendContext(ctx) , onRequest(ctx) , transform ; a 0.x hook name is an error .pb.js beside pages in pb_hooks/pages/ Hook files stay in pb_hooks ; in pb_pages they're a startup error require('../lib/x') could reach pb_hooks from the pages folder require never leaves pb_pages ; use require(__hooks + '/lib/x') Cookies (and pb_auth ) readable by browser JS HttpOnly by default; pass { httpOnly: false } for a cookie the page's JS reads. pb_auth stays HttpOnly , so pb.authStore.loadFromCookie(document.cookie) no longer works Realtime send(topic, message) sent the message as is; filter(clientId, client, topic, message) replaced the subscription check The data is JSON-encoded (a string arrives quoted: JSON.parse it); filter(client) narrows clients that are subscribed to the topic .md , .jsx , .tsx were static files unless a plugin handled them Always pages EJS ran over the whole .md file, front matter included Front matter is plain YAML, read before EJS runs auth plugin through the JS SDK over HTTP ( api.pb() ) ctx.session. , direct app calls url() , stringify() , micro-dash globals Removed: use ctx.req.url , JSON.stringify , plain JS pb() (js-sdk plugin over HTTP to localhost:8090 ) ctx.pb() : same SDK, built in, in-process, as the signed-in user Route with fewer segments could match a longer URL Segment counts must match create-pocketpages pocketone pages create [--starter ]

title: Speedrun: Connecting Your Fly.io App to a Custom Domain with Cloudflare Proxy
text: Custom domains on your Fly.io app with Cloudflare in front can be a little complex because you must validate the domain on Fly.io BEFORE turning on Cloudflare proxying. Follow these steps.

title: Speedrun: Connecting Your Fly.io App to a Custom Domain with Cloudflare Proxy
heading: 1. Create the Fly.io App
text: Start by deploying your app on Fly.io. Follow the standard process to get your app up and running.

title: Speedrun: Connecting Your Fly.io App to a Custom Domain with Cloudflare Proxy
heading: 2. Register Your Domain
text: If you haven't already, register your domain. It's often convenient to register it through Cloudflare, which will also handle your DNS and proxying needs.

title: Speedrun: Connecting Your Fly.io App to a Custom Domain with Cloudflare Proxy
heading: 3. Configure DNS in Cloudflare
text: In Cloudflare's DNS settings, add A and AAAA records pointing to your Fly.io app's public IPv4 and IPv6 addresses. Important: Turn off proxying (the orange cloud icon) for these records. This ensures that the Fly.io app can be accessed directly.

title: Speedrun: Connecting Your Fly.io App to a Custom Domain with Cloudflare Proxy
heading: 4. Add a Certificate in Fly.io
text: In your Fly.io dashboard, add an SSL certificate for your custom domain. Since proxying is turned off, Fly.io should be able to validate the certificate immediately. Your app should now respond on your custom domain, but it's not yet proxied through Cloudflare.

title: Speedrun: Connecting Your Fly.io App to a Custom Domain with Cloudflare Proxy
heading: 5. Verify Domain Ownership and Proxying
text: From the Fly.io certificate area, add the CNAME record required for domain ownership verification. Important: Turn off proxying for the CNAME record as well. Fly.io needs to verify ownership whenever the SSL certificate is renewed, which requires direct access. Go back to Fly.io, check the certificate, and ensure domain ownership verification is successful.

title: Speedrun: Connecting Your Fly.io App to a Custom Domain with Cloudflare Proxy
heading: 6. Turn On Proxying in Cloudflare
text: Once everything is verified and working, return to Cloudflare and turn on proxying (enable the orange cloud) for your A and AAAA records. In Cloudflare’s SSL/TLS settings, set the encryption mode to Full (not Full Strict) to ensure proper SSL handshakes between Cloudflare and Fly.io.

title: Speedrun: Connecting Your Fly.io App to a Custom Domain with Cloudflare Proxy
heading: 7. Test Your Setup
text: Finally, browse to your new domain to confirm everything is working as expected with Cloudflare proxying enabled. You now have a fully functioning Fly.io app served through a custom domain with Cloudflare as the proxy!

title: Speedrun: Google OAuth2
text: This guide walks you through setting up Google OAuth2 sign-in for your PocketPages app.

title: Speedrun: Google OAuth2
heading: 1. Create/Select Google Cloud Project
text: Go to Google Cloud Console Either select an existing project or create a new one If creating new, provide a project name when prompted Creating a new Google Cloud project Naming the new project Selecting the project

title: Speedrun: Google OAuth2
heading: 2. Configure OAuth Credentials
text: Navigate to "Credentials" in the left sidebar Click "Create Credentials" and select "OAuth client ID" Navigating to credentials Creating OAuth credentials

title: Speedrun: Google OAuth2
heading: Configure Application Type
text: Select "Web application" as the application type Configure your authorized origins and redirect URIs: Authorized JavaScript origins : Your application domain (e.g., http://localhost:8090 ) Authorized redirect URIs : Your auth callback URL (e.g., http://localhost:8090/auth/oauth/confirm ) Selecting web application Configuring URIs

title: Speedrun: Google OAuth2
heading: Configure Consent Screen (if needed)
text: If you haven't set up a consent screen before, you'll need to configure it: Choose External/Internal user type Fill in the required application information Consent screen setup Consent screen details

title: Speedrun: Google OAuth2
heading: Download Credentials
text: After creating the OAuth client, download the JSON credentials file Store this file securely - it contains sensitive information Downloading credentials Credentials JSON format

title: Speedrun: Google OAuth2
heading: 3. Configure OAuth2 in the dashboard
text: OAuth2 providers belong to an auth collection, usually users : Open your app's dashboard ( /_/ ) and go to Collections . Open the users collection's settings (the gear icon) and its Options tab. Under OAuth2 , turn it on. Click Add provider and pick Google . OAuth2 settings for the users collection OAuth2 providers section Adding new provider Selecting Google provider There's no site URL to set for this. The auth plugin builds the redirect URL from the address the request came in on: the scheme and host the browser used, plus /auth/oauth/confirm . So the redirect URI in Google must match that address exactly. http://localhost:8090 and http://127.0.0.1:8090 are different to Google, so add each one you use, plus your live domain ( https://example.com/auth/oauth/confirm ). Behind a proxy, the host is the one the browser asked for, and HTTPS is detected from X-Forwarded-Proto .

title: Speedrun: Google OAuth2
heading: Provider Configuration
text: Enter your Client ID and Client Secret from the downloaded credentials Configure any additional auth options as needed Save your changes Configuring Google provider Saving changes

title: Speedrun: Google OAuth2
heading: Customizing the Return URL
text: By default, the auth plugin uses /auth/oauth/confirm as the OAuth2 return path. Change it when you start the flow: ctx.session.requestOAuth2('google', { redirectPath: '/custom/oauth/callback' }) Remember to add the new redirect URL to your Google OAuth2 configuration too.

title: Speedrun: Google OAuth2
heading: 1. Turn on the auth plugin
text: // pb_pages/+config.ts module.exports = { plugins: ['auth'], }

title: Speedrun: Google OAuth2
heading: 2. Login form
text: Sign in with Google

title: Speedrun: Google OAuth2
heading: 3. Start the flow
